👉What is religion?

👉What is the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo religion?

👉How is the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo religion different from other religions?

👉What is the role of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo religion in saving humanity?

Dear and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we transmit through the John's Repentance website, we have sent the following introductory lesson about the Orthodox Tewahedo religion as a starting point for our education

text:
For all those who ask what religion is, the first thing they should know is that 'religion' is the lens of conscience of all of us, in which we distinguish between creator and creature, righteousness and condemnation, light and darkness, life and death, heaven and hell. Since the creation of the human world; Religion is the true way to know and reach the invisible, intangible, abstract God (Creator).

Religion is a subtle way of believing and knowing God. Except through religion, we could not see it with our eyes, hear with our senses, think with our hearts, and listen with our senses. Therefore, religion is the secret by which we can accept the divine wisdom, which is distant and abstract to us, with faith that it will be done.In his message to the Hebrews about faith, the Apostle Saint Paul said, "Faith assures us of what we hope for; It explains what we do not see" and he said that 'religion' is a special grace by which we can see God and His subtle work that we cannot see with our eyes (Hebrews 11:1).

The foundation of religion is to accept your Creator. Acknowledging your Creator begins with believing in being a creature. Because there is no one who says that I was created by myself. If a person believes that he is created, then he believes that he has a creator. Then he begins to search for his creator. An example of this is Abraham, the great righteous man. Abraham was born in Karan, in what is now Turkey. His father was Tara and was a pot worshiper. It was not only worshiping, but it was also managed by carving and selling idols. Later, he realized that the material that was carved by his father's hand and carried to the market and sold could not be God and started searching for the creator. In the process of searching, he tried to worship rivers, winds, mountains and the sun. He affirmed that all these are creatures and not creators. In the end, he shouted, "O Creator, speak to me." At that time, God, the Creator of creation, appeared to him. He ordered him to leave Karan, where idols were worshipped, and go to the promised land of Canaan. (Genesis 12:1) From then on, Abraham believed God and lived faithfully to his word. This is to know that Abraham trusted God's word. Even today, what we mean by religion is believing in God and believing in God's commands like Abraham did.

text.text: 1. How does the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo religion differ from other faiths?

text:
The word 'religion is one' is a truth that does not raise any questions for a person who understands the unity of the creator. Religion means accepting your creator and trusting the law. And the Creator is one in character. Therefore, believing in one creator and worshiping him is the same thing. This is what we mean by religion. In short, religion means accepting the existence of a creator and being faithful to the laws of the creator. So if it is religion to accept that there is a creator of the worlds, a guardian and a leader, and if it is believed that the creator is one, then accepting that one creator and being governed by the law cannot be more than one unified system.

When the apostle Saint Paul said that religion is one as the Creator is one, he said, "There is one Lord, one religion, one baptism, who is above all, who works in all, and lives in all, and is the Father of all" (Eph 4:5).

In short, the creator of the worlds is one. The ritual of worshiping one creator is also the same. And this is the great truth.

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ said, "You are a rock, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it." It got the name 'Christianity', that is, the unity of Christ's people, the unity of Christ's disciples. The religion called by this name was only one until the beginning of the fourth century, that is, until 325 AD. But after that time, as Christ himself first told us "Be careful that no one deceives you. For many false Christs and false prophets will arise, and if they can, they will show great signs and wonders until they deceive even the elect. (Matt. 24+5; 24)

The Prophet Jeremiah, speaking about the true and straight path (religion), said, "Ask for the straight path that was before you, and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls" (Jer 6:16).

Basically, when we say "Orthodox Tewahedo Religion", we believe in the unity and trinity of God, and the knowledge that we cannot see with our fleshly eyes, that we cannot touch with our hands, that we cannot reach through research, and that there is a God (Creator) who precedes us even if we run. Through the laws of nature, he created heaven and earth, darkness and light, day and night, man and angels, wild animals and animals, plants and vegetables, creatures that move on land and sea, crawl on their chests, and fly on their wings, 22 creatures in total. 'Orthodox Tewahedo Religion' is the direct way to acknowledge the creator who feeds and guides all creatures. Therefore, as the creator is one, religion can be one. This is the main secret that makes it different from other types of faith. Because all faith is not religion; For example: those who believe in Satan, those who believe in worshiping gods, those who believe in the spirit of the king, those who worship fire, river, tree, stone, various spirits, we do not call all these nominal beliefs as 'religion'.

The true and direct religion is the treasure of the Holy Spirit given to us to believe in God alone, the Creator, Sustainer. “Religion is the foundation of everything; But the others are buildings and walls or roofs and walls." The foundation of a house does not support the whole building. Religion carries faith, conduct, and various good works. Just as a building does not stand without a foundation, there is no religion without conduct. Or it doesn't make sense. Apostle St. Jacob said, "If there is faith without works, it is dead in itself." Religion and morals; He said that they are like aspects of the same coin that cannot be spoken separately
Therefore, religion is not only believing in the existence of God, but also trusting. This means obeying God and performing the proper rituals according to the laws and regulations of the religion.

Beloved and respected, all our members who follow the orthodox education that we convey on John's Repentance website; today, we have sent you the following basic lesson based on the topic, so we entrust you all to read and learn from it.

text: The basis and center of religious education is the acceptance of God. Next questions: Who is God? How his character revealed? Does it have a body? etc., are answered with the list of religious education; and this education is called a mystery because it is understood only by faith. So, mystery in this lesson mean spiritual, subtle, invisible, unknown, admirable and understood only by faith. Because either it is revealed by the extent of faith; but for those who do not believe, it is a hidden secret. Because, it cannot be reached through physical knowledge and scientific wisdom. Or, even if we say that we know and understand it, it is said that it is impossible to know the full extent of the mystery, except that we might   understand only to the extent that it is enough for the survival of the soul .

Trinity is a noun derived from the Geez verb that means three. This is the lesson we learn about the trinity of God's body. Trinity is very different from three. For three speaks of three different things, and trinity speaks of three things in one thing. Therefore, when talking about trinity, it is necessary to talk about unity. 

Therefore, in the mystery of the Trinity, we learn not only about the threeness of God's body, but also about the unity of his character. In short, Trinity is the teaching that God is one and three. 

Their trinity is:- in name, in task, and in body.

Their unity is :- in character, in divinity, in power, in rulling, in will, in creating this world from non-existence to existence, as well as in feeding creation, protecting it, and in suspending this world.

Trinity means: Father has perfect form, perfect face, perfect body. And the Son has a perfect form, a perfect face and a perfect body. The Holy Spirit has a perfect form, a perfect face and a perfect body. The Father's body is always the Father's. The Son's body is always the Son's; The body of the Holy Spirit is always the Holy Spirit. That is, the bodies do not change, do not exchange, do not absorb. In their position, in their appearance and in their name, they will remain forever on their own. The names by which the bodies are called also remain unchanged for their bodies. Therefore, just as we say that the Trinity is three in body, so we say three in their name as well; and these Trinity Names are: Father, Son, Holy Spirit, (Matthew 28:19  ; Psalm 33:14, 118:73, Isaiah 66:1, Genesis 18:1-4 Matthew 3:16)

In the Old Testament

1.  "God said: let us make man in our image, after our likeness" (Genesis 1:26) Here: "God said" indicates unity, while "let us create man in our image" describes being more than one.

2.   "The Lord God said, Adam became as one of us to know good and evil" (Genesis 3:22). Here, "God said" refers to oneness, while "as one of us" refers to more than one.

5.  When God revealed himself to Abraham, "At noon, while he was sitting at the door of his tent, God appeared to him through the tree of Meri. He lifted up his eyes and saw three men standing before him. When he saw them, he ran from the door of the tent to meet them. He bowed to the earth. He said, "Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, I beg you not to let your servant pass over me." "And he lifted up his eyes and behold, he saw three men standing before him," and the saying that God is three in person (Trinity). And in the speech of Abraham, "O Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, I beseech you not to let your servant pass away from me." This indicates that God is one in character, will and power.

6.  In addition; When the prophet Isaiah explained the trinity, "I saw God sitting on a long and high throne, and the area of his garment filled the temple. ..And the seraphim were standing above him. And they were shouting to each other: "Holy, Holy, Holy, the Lord of hosts, the whole earth is full of his glory." The word refers to the unity and trinity of the Trinity. (Isaiah 6:3)

1.  The New Testament is an age of revelation. And it is God Himself who is revealed. The revelation that has been revealed in this age is very unique and clear compared to the revelation that was revealed to others in different ways previously. St. Paul explained this as follows: "Since ancient times, God has spoken to our fathers through prophets in many ways, and He has spoken to us at the end of this age through His Son, whom He made the heir of all things, and through whom He created the worlds." (Hebrews 1:1)

The physical word Jesus Christ taught in different ways that God is three in body, task, name, and unity, and one in character, will, and power, creating and sustaining the world. Occasionally, the trinity of God is revealed in an audible and visible body. For example, at the time of the baptism, on Matthew 3:16-17, he made it clear that there are three bodies: the Father who made a sound from heaven, the Holy Spirit who came down in the form of a dove, and the Son who stood in the middle of the Jordan in human flesh, and the three bodies have three names: Father, Son, Holy Spirit. And to see how the names were distinguished-  In heaven, "This is my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased." His fatherhood is known and called Father. And he said that Jesus is my son, so he is called son. It is clearly written that the one who came down in the form of a dove is the Holy Spirit as the Spirit of God, so we call the Trinity three by name. 

2.  Also, "Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you" is a powerful word that expresses unity and trinity indicating their name. (Matthew 28:19)

Beloved and respected, all our members who follow the orthodox education that we convey on John's Repentance website; Based on the topic, we have sent you the following basic lesson, so we entrust you all to read and learn from it.

text:
Understanding the identity of Jesus Christ is the foundation of the Christian faith. Because "Christian" means a Christian, a disciple of Christ. Anyone who does not know Christ cannot be called a disciple of Christ. So who is Christ?

It was Jesus Christ himself who asked who the Christ was. He asked them the twelve psalms and the question and the answer are as follows.

Jesus came to the camp of Caesarea Philippi and his disciples. Who do people call the son of man? he asked them. But they said, some John the Baptist, others Elijah, others Jeremiah, or one of the prophets. Jesus said to them. Who do you say I am? And Simon Peter answered. You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus answered and said to him. O Simon, son of Jonah, blessed are you, for flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father in heaven. And I say unto thee, Thou art Peter. And upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven. Whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven. (Matthew 16:13-19)

So, from this question and answer, we can understand that the people of the time when the Son of God called "Jesus" appeared in the flesh of Adam, more or less believed in Jesus as a prophet. It could be understood that he was not a prophet, apart from his work, even from the words he used to speak. When prophets teach, because they are sent from God and it is God who sent them, they say, "Thus saith God." But since Christ is the God who sent the prophets to tell you to speak like this, and the words he spoke were his own, he said, "But I tell you," "I tell you the truth, the truth." This is proof that he is not a prophet, but the God of prophets. In addition, he took three of his disciples (Peter, John, and James) and climbed Mount Tabor to show them that Jesus Christ is not a prophet, but the God of prophets. Among the prophets, he brought Moses from the grave and Elijah from the living. (Matthew 17:1-3) However, there are still many to whom the identity of Jesus has not been revealed.

From the question and answer above, we clearly understand that Jesus is the son of man and the son of God. Because when Jesus asked about himself, he said, "Who do they call the Son of Man?" Saint Peter replied, "You are the son of the living God." Therefore, as Christ is the son of God, he is God. As a human being, he is human. The Orthodox Tewahedo Church is founded on the belief of St. Peter, the Only Son, so it teaches Christ as a perfect God and a perfect man. If the Son of Man is called a man, then the Son of God is God. If it is God, then it is God. For there is no god but God. He is the creator, for there is no creator other than God. He is a judge because there is no true judge other than God. Therefore, we believe that Jesus is: 1/ Perfect Man, Perfect God, 2/ Creator, 3/ God, 4/ God, 5/ Judge. We will look at these in detail one by one

(to be continued)

And one: Because the Son is the Word of the Trinity, and judgment is spoken by words, therefore it is said that he gave judgment to the Son.

text.text: 6. If Jesus is a judgmental God, how did he receive the death penalty?

text:
Among the questions that many believers and heretics raise, why did Jesus die? takes precedence. The tendency of those who question this is to say that Jesus is not almighty God but a creature. It is possible to answer the question with a question by saying: - if he is a being, how did he conquer death and get up?  For there is no one among creatures who has died of his own will and has conquered death by his power. When we look at it broadly, why did Jesus Christ come? suddenly or on purpose? If it came with a purpose, what was the purpose? It is imperative to clarify the question.

Jesus Christ came to this earth with a plan and purpose. Its aims are exemplary and redemptive. Redemption means that Jesus shed his blood and broke his body to free Adam from the slavery of the devil and the citizenship of hell. Without being born of the Virgin Mary, without being baptized, without fasting, without being crucified, and without suffering all that, he could have done everything by his word alone. But the human being learns good and bad things from the human being himself, in order to teach human beings the way of life not by words but by deeds, he came to this earth by being born as a human being and doing everything that a human does except sin, and teaching us not to sin but to do righteousness (to be an example).

For example, after Jesus Christ was baptized by his servant John in the Jordan River, he made a law saying that whoever believed and was baptized would be saved, he entered the monastery of Corinth and after fasting for forty days and forty nights, he taught that when you fast, you should not be seen as hypocrites. After teaching by day and praying by night at Debrezeit, he warned us not to enter into temptation and pray. Finally, he washed the feet of the apostles and taught humility by saying, "Do to others as I have done to you." "For I have given you an example that you should do as I have done for you." (John 13:15)

For those who ask us why Christ died, another answer to their question will be why Christ was born. Adam was created and we Adamites are born from Adam to live forever. But Christ was born to die. What we should note about this is that birth and creation are very different things. For there is creation in our birth. But it should not be created at the birth of Jesus Christ. For He is eternal without beginning and without end. "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end." (Revelation 22:13)

So God brought us from non-existence to existence so that we might praise his name and inherit his glory and live forever. But when we, who were created to live, chose death instead of life, shame instead of honor, sorrow instead of happiness, and when we were expelled from heaven and descended to hell, God took our debt and sin upon himself, accepted the death sentence which we deserved, and returned us to our former glory. He died in order to achieve this goal, not by accident or by others' coercion. The Lord said that his death was by his will and his resurrection was under his authority. (Joh 10:15-18) The mystery of his crucifixion is to give us life. "Just as Moses revealed the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man deserves to be crucified so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but have eternal life." (John 3:14-15)

text:
I wish that God's peace stays with you. The only way that a human gets peace and happiness is to believe that Our Lord Jesus Christ, who was born in Bethlehem from our mother Saint Virgin Mary, is the Almighty God. The creator of the visible and invisible in this world. The one the prophets spoke that He came to save us from satan, evil things, and sins. The one who the disciples preached that He was crucified to give us everlasting life by His flesh and death. He is the one who rose after 3 days from the tomb and revealed himself to Madgelon Mariam/Mary and all his disciples at different times. He, the one who ascended to heaven, will come again with graciousness to judge the people (Isaiah 3:13).

What must I do?
1. Believe in Jesus Christ as Almighty God.
2. Believe in Jesus Christ as who judges on people, not who maketh the intersection for us.
3. Believe in Jesus Christ as the world's Holly Savior.
4. Believe Jesus Christ as “The everlasting Father, Prince of Peace” (Isaiah 9:6).
5. Believe that Saint Virgin Mary is our spiritual Mother who is given to us from our Lord Jesus Christ (Psalm 87:5 & John19:27)
6. Believe that saints, prophets, disciples, Archbishops, Priests...etc as they maketh intersections for us, through their prayers.
7. Pray every day to the Lord God (Mat 6:13, 26:41, Daniel 6:16). 
8. Love all human beings without a difference as Jesus Christ loved us all despite our sins, weakness, and flaws.
9. Read the Bible every day (one verse a day or a chapter a day depending on what you can) and spiritual books as they will explain the spiritual life and experiences of Orthodox scholars. Listen to Orthodox Tewahedo Hymns. 
10. Ask advice from church Fathers/ priests, and if you don’t have access to them, reach them through social media, or talk to your brothers and sisters in Christ.
11. Go to the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahido Church every day, if not as much as possible, and participate in spiritual ceremonies, liturgy, Annual celebrations...etc 

Try these and you will see changes in your spiritual and secular life. Always know that the Lord is with you! Always seek Him, and you, our sister, will find Him. Isaiah 41:10 

“Fear not, for I am with you; Be not dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, Yes, I will help you, I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.”


No money will give us happiness, no Authority will give us happiness, no beauty will give us peace, no fame will give us everlasting Love. No knowledge of sciences nor technology will give us everlasting peace and happiness. Happiness is possible only with the Almighty God Jesus Christ. We will keep you in our prayers and please continue to reach out to us.

text.text: 👉🏾 Question from member: I often feel depressed and lonely. Life has no meaning to me, I just want to die and live with Jesus, I've been looking for happiness all my life but I can't find it, I feel like my mind is going to explode, please pray for me, I need prayer, what do you recommend?

text:
Why does a person choose loneliness? Why does a person hide? In essence, man is not happy without God, because there is no peace without God. Jesus Christ said in the Gospel of John, chapter 14, verse 27, "Peace I leave with you, and my peace I give you, the peace I give you is not as the world gives; do not let your hearts be troubled, do not be afraid."
 
The world kisses us today then bites tomorrow; gives today then takes away tomorrow. But God does not take away what He has given, no matter what, there is no peace without God. What is life? Life is the opposite of death, life is living. Life is God, it is written, "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life."
 
Therefore, if we believe in the Son, we live with Jesus who is the life. It is Jesus Christ who gave life when human beings could not live according to the commandment, it is Jesus Christ who enlightened the dark world. In fact, this Christmas (birth) season is called the light. And if it is said who is the light: it is Jesus Christ.

This world was dark before God the Son became a man. The world lived in darkness. It is called light because God became a man and enlightened the world by making us members of His body. Many people's lives are in darkness. Darkness is sin, darkness is betrayal, darkness is hatred, darkness is lack of love; On the other hand, light is Jesus Christ, light is life, light is religion, light is peace, light is help, blessing and love. Because it is our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ who gave us that, there is no life without Jesus Christ.
 
As the owner himself told us, John Gospel chapter 15 verse 5 said "without me you can do nothing", so without Jesus Christ nothing can be done. How can peace be found without Jesus Christ? How can you live? Absolutely not possible. When Judas betrayed Jesus Christ for 30 dollars he died because he was separated from Jesus Christ who is life. We remember that when the devil was once the archangel, when he forgot God and said, "I am the creator," and then failed and separated from God who is life.

Also, when Adam lived peacefully in paradise for seven years and did what he was told not to do, he lost peace from God who is life, and found it difficult to live. but then we remember that he found peace when he returned to God, when he reconciled with God, so there is no peace without God.
 
Our questioner said that they want to die and live with Jesus Christ. So, those of us who do not have peace on earth, those who have fallen into sin on earth, those who have not tried to repent to find Jesus Christ, how can we find peace if we die? What qualifies us for the kingdom of heaven is the work we have done on earth to live with Jesus Christ and enable us to live in heaven. If we die on earth covered in sin, without repentance, confession, and reconciliation with God, we will not be able to live with Jesus. Therefore, it means that we cannot live with our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ before we repent.

text:
Our dear member told us that their mind is going to explode. It is God who gives us peace of mind. 
The mind wants shelter, it wants peace but the conscience blames it. For example, a person knows that stealing is bad before learning to steal, knows that killing is bad before learning to kill. Our consciousness tells us what is good and bad because that is the way it was created; Man is a creature created to distinguish good from evil, evil from good, and what is useful from what is not. 

Therefore, we must all seek life, and if we are willing to find life, we can repent of our sins and find God; God is near, God is love. "You return and I will return," God is not a cruel father who tells you to stay where you left. What He told us is  those of you who have fallen come back to me, . God is a compassionate and merciful father.
 
First He created us in His image, we humans failed to live, we fell, we were the kings of creation but because of our sin we fell from our glory; He came back in search of us, born of the Holy Virgin Mary as a man. After that, he paid many prices for us, to bring back our exiled ones, he was exiled for us, then He was whipped with 6666 lashes, crucified in the square of Calvary, to bring us back what we lost and even more. He gave us his holy body and his precious blood. Eat my flesh, drink my blood, that he may bring us back with food that we have fallen by eating, there is no greater life than this.

In the morning, when Nebuchadnezzar looked from his balcony, he saw four of them walking in the fire. Yesterday we tied three men and threw them out of the fiery furnace, but today I see four of them released  and walking in the fire. And immediately he went out of the oven and said to them, come out. They ran out. Not even an ash was found on their clothes. 👉 1st/ He told the prophet Daniel in a vision about what was going to happen. 15:16)

👉 2. Also, in the vision that the prophet Daniel saw again, he said this about the angel, "While I was still praying, the angel I had seen in the vision before, Gabriel, came flying... He taught me and told me... Daniel, I have come now to give you wisdom and understanding" (Dan 9: 21-23)

👉 3rd / Saint Gabriel is the angel who saved Daniel from the lion's mouth.

👉 4th /  Saint Gabriel saved the three men named Ananya, Azaria, and Misael from the furnace fire. 

👉 5th/ He announced to the priest Zacharias and Saint Elizabeth that they would give birth to John the Baptist in their old age.

👉 6. He announced to the Virgin Mary that the physical word Jesus Christ, who is the cure of the world, would be born from the her.

👉 7th/ He saved  St. Jeletan and the child Kirkos from a boiling fire in an iron tank. 

👉 8th/ He led the wise men to the city of Bethlehem where the Lord was born, leading them with the sign of a star.

👉 9th/ Old Joseph was told in a dream to take his mother and baby and flee to Egypt.

👉 10/ In addition, Saint Gabriel announced the conception of Samson; He brought forth water for Agar in the desert. He who interpreted the mystery to Daniel; He is an angel appointed over serpents and scorpions.

In general, we find this angel's intercession and guardianship in many readings of the holy books; God has helpes us to write to you on the occasion of the annual holiday that we celebrate today, December 28, so that we may all receive the intercession and blessings of the angel Saint Gabriel. 

Therefore, if the Lord God had not sent his angels to protect us night and morning, day and night, on the road, when we sleep at home and when we get up, Satan's army would have prevent us from having life in this world and the next .

God's prophet, Saint David, said, "No calamity will enter your house. He will raise up angels for you to guard you on your way. They will lift you up with their hands so that your feet will not stumble over a stone..." Telling us about the guardianship and protection of angels.

In another paragraph, he said, "God's angel will live around those who fear him, and will save them." He said that angels will save people who believe in the guardianship and intercession of angels, and that they will save us from physical and spiritual suffering. (Ps 33:7, 90/91:10')

Since angels are appointed to have authority over all creatures, the prophet Enoch told us about the power of intercessor and guardianship of Saint Gabriel saying that he is one of the noble angels appointed over the serpents, the righteous in heaven, and the cherubim. (Enoch 6:7)

May the prayers and supplications of this great angel of light rest upon us

👉Question:-

text:
I had a question and I need your sincere help: I have committed many sins in my life, especially the sin of adultery, I have committed adultery with many women, with animals, with a married person and with a relative. I want to confess my sins to a spiritual father but how can I say these things in front of him?

✍️Answer:- It would have been better if we hadn't made a mistake and fallen into sin in the first place, but after we fall, repenting and coming back is a must. If a person falls into sin, how can it be difficult for him to repent? We should never feel overwhelmed or afraid. Basically, if we don't get embarrassed when we do it, how can it be difficult for us to say it? When we sin, we are dying, but when we repent, we are being saved. Therefore, the one and only choice choice we have not to live a life hunted by sin nor to receive the wages of our sins is to repent.

When a person is ashamed to talk about their sins, they run away from repentance, pile sin on top of sin, and keep the door wide open for more sin.

The rightous deeds or sin that a person does every day is written in God's record. Therefore, a person should watch and control their deeds, humbly continue the good, and confess the bad every day. Otherwise, since we don't know the day we will be called, we need to be ready every day, lest we hear the words, 'Depart from me' on the day of judgment.

When a person commits a sin, they usually pretend that they have benefited and are happy, but later the results are not beneficial. In factz it is harmful, it does not give peace, it creates chaos and lack of peace. When they do it, they do it knowingly, but when they are about to speak and repent, it seems to them a shame. This is a hindrance to repentance which is the method that is most commonly used by the devil to prolong the time for people to repent and to keep them in sin and to prevent them from revealing the secrets of sin that he practices secretly and the methods he used to make them captives of sin.

Among the ways of salvation that Satan fights against, there is nothing greater than repentance. Repentance destroys all the buildings of sin that the enemy, the devil, has built to destroy the lives of Christians. Repentance wipes out all sins - This is a great mystery that is performed by the grace of God. 

We are humiliated when we first commit the sin, and we are glorified when we say and confess the sin we have committed. By sinning, we were dirty, damaged, defiled, but when we repent, we are being sanctified, freed and glorified. 

The idea that our dear member raised is one which many people do either without knowing, without thinking it is bad, or knowingly, influenced by peers or by satanic entertainment industries. Later, they find it difficult to get out as easily as they entered it. Whichever it may be, by sinning, we lose God, by sinning, by sinning we live in darkness, and darkness is Sheol, eternal fire.

text:
Our dear member stated, “I am ashamed to express the wrongs I have done to a confession father.”

But yet, repentance is to regret what we have done; it is saying that "I have done things that aren’t expected of a believer of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ." It is to say that we should accuse/judge ourselves before being accused by other people. It starts when a person accuses themselves, when they reveal their secrets to themselves, and when they are ashamed of what they have done in the past. It is followed by confessing our sins with heartfelt regrets before God. We should not be ashamed or embarrassed when we confess our sins as we were not ashamed or embarrassed when we were doing it because when we were doing the wrongdoings, we were dying but with confession, we are making reconciliation with God, and we are being saved. We are coming from death to life and coming out of darkness to light. It is a way that we are starting to live together with God. 

When we go to a confession father to repent for what we have done, we are admitting our hate for the sins and deciding that we would not do them again. St. Paul wrote, in 1 Corinthians 11: 31, “For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judges.” Repentance is when we, the sinners, judge ourselves and our sins. Therefore, what our questioner mentioned to us will be an answer for all of us, to say that we should be ashamed of our sins, repent, and decide not to do it again, but we should not be afraid to confess our sins to our fathers and repent.

Acts 3:19, St Paul wrote, “Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord.” 
Matthew 9:13 also mentions, “...For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, ]to repentance.”  Therefore, it is the sinner who needs repentance. Our brothers and sisters, you must understand that no matter how serious our sins are, we must come to God in repentance, believing that we will be forgiven and that we will be cleansed. We have the opportunity to choose a confession father or a spiritual father who is a true guardian, mentor, and teacher. You are expected to state your repentance in detail without being ashamed or embarrassed by your sins to your spiritual father. As said in the book, the priest means the grave, because the grave does not reveal everything, and the priest does not speak about anyone's sin, he should be a secret keeper.

Just as water washes the cleanest and the dirtiest, without discrimination, so should the Priest wash away the sins of the child indiscriminately, and not speak of the sins he hears. Perhaps, if there is a Priest who speaks, he is responsible to God, not us. But since we are told to go and examine ourselves to the priest, it means that we should go and confess our sins to our repentance father. It is God who commanded us to confess our sins. It is written in Matthew chapter 8:4 "And Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one; but go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.” So, we advise our fellow members to do as it is told. If in case you don't have a father of repentance, no Christian should spend a day without a father of repentance. Having a father of repentance and repenting is a spiritual obligation. And so we advise you to look for a spiritual father, talk to the head priest of your parish, and consult with friends and family who have a father of repentance. You may also reach out to us and we will assist you in this regard if you can't find a sheppard for your soul nearby.

👉 Question: Hello father, I have a question. Do we have to confess sins we unknowingly did as a child (under the age of 18)?

text:
The answer is yes we have to. If we remember a sin we did, we should tell it to our father of repentance, we should repent for it. There is healing and peace of mind that comes with communicating all our shortcomings with our father of repentance. 

We have to confess for all the sins we did after the age of 7 because that is the age that is set by our fathers. That is the age that a person starts differentiating good from evil. Even though a 7 years old is not required to fast like a 40 years old, they are required to start with the basics, abstaining from meat during the fasting seasons for example.

Our church starts our spiritual training from day one. text.text: How to overcome repeated sin and discouragement?

Question: How does one overcome feelings of defeat and discouragement when falling into the same sin continually?
How to accept God's love and grace and not give up / lose hope with struggles that come with my journey with God? 
I tend to fall short of the goals I set for myself in spiritual life and the discouragement / feeling depressed about that holds me back from making progress. 

Thank you and May God bless your service!

text:
This is a very important question because a lot of people confess their sins many times and go back to it many times. The main cause of this is not knowing what sin is and not understanding the depths of it's consequences. 

If a person confess their sins without understand what sin is, they will most likely fall back into it. If a person confesses their sins without understanding the benefits of repentance, it will be very hard for them to come back to repentance.

Hence we first need to learn about sin, it's consequences and the benefits of repentance. We need to learn from people that have fallen into sin, we need to know that sin separates us from God, sin deprives us from peace, sin brings curses to our lives, sin is the worst thing one can do. 

People who have fallen into sin have lost God, lost blessings, lost peace, lost life and can't even get alone with themselves. That is why Adam and Eve had a hard time living together after they fell into sin. Adam had asked Eve to get away from him, to depart form him accusing her to be the reason of his fall. People who have fallen into sin can't live with others nor be comfortable in their own skin. That is why Judas of Iscariot, who sold our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ with $30 thought that he was doing good for himself, that he would live but he couldn't. He threw away the money, hanged himself up on a tree and died after suffering for 40 days. Hence we need to understand that people trapped in sin can't live with God, with others nor with themselves. This, we have to believe before confessing. 

One needs to understand the depths of sin's consequences, and also understand the benefits of repentance. We need to learn from people who changed their lives and were healed through repentance. It is only then that we will have not repeatedly fall back to sin. 

We need to believe that everything is possible with God and nothing without Him. On Matthew 21:21, our Lord tells us "if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but also if you say to this mountain, ‘Be removed and be cast into the sea,’ it will be done." Hence why do we give up? We are winners in Christ, we fall and we get back up but we should never give up, why do we give up? Are we not the ones He created in His own image? Are we not the ones whom He appointed as rulers over creatures? It is us that He has delivered from the bondage of the devil by becoming one of us, it is for us that He has given his Holy Blood and Holy Flesh. It is for us that is given the interception of the apostles, the prophets, the angels, the saints, the virgins, the monks, our Lady Virgin Mary and others. Hence how can we give up? It is for us that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ established the mystery of Repentance so we can be reconciled with Him if we fall. Hence we do not give up. The holy water, the cross, the priests, the gospel, the prayer books, the advisors, the teachers, the fasts, prostration and countless more are ours. Hence how can we give up? We don't!

Then once we have fallen deep into it, he says: "Look at you, do you think God is going to forgive you? Are you not ashamed to approach God with all these sins? Are you not ashamed to go to a prist and admit to all these sins? You shameful being!" To make us think that God doesn't forgive, painting him as cruel.

Hence how can we give up? We don't! God died for us, it is for us that he gave his Holy Blood and his Holy Flesh, it is for us that he gave his mother the Virgin Mary. Hence we don't give up. 

May God help us confess all our sins and live a life or repentance so we can stay in His house until the last breathe and inherit His Kingdom.

Question: Peace be with you in Christ, dear family of the Most High God, Virgin Mary's tithes of the proud children of the cross, as well as my fathers and brothers, who tirelessly answer our questions, may God's peace be with you all.My question is If a girl is forced to rape, should she repent in this matter?

👉🏾Answer:

text:
Beloved members of John's repentance page, first we need to define what it means to confess. It means to communicate the things that our mind holds against us, the things that we feel guilty of, the things we do not feel comfortable living with to our father of repentance. Hence if our dear sister communicates what happened to her penitent father, she would be benefited but not harmed and it wouldn't be wrong to do so. She will learn how to consulate, comfort and calm herself from the spiritual and fatherly advice so communicating the situation with her spiritual father will benefit her in many ways but won't harm her in any way.

Our fathers say: "if the owner doesn't scream, the neighbors will not hear, the neighbors will not rescue" hence communicating our situation to those who are concerned will be useful but not harmful. 

A person needing medication will only get the right medication after they communicate all their issues but if they hide them, they don't have a cure. Hence since our member has been hurt and are in grief, they need spiritual and fatherly advice to comfort them. Hence it is good if she communicates the situation with her spiritual father who will determine what to do, what she needs to do and how she should continue. "You are not the only one to have faced this my daughter, come down it will be alright. You are not guilty of the sin because you were forced into it. It would have been better if this would not have happened in the first place, but after it did, all we can do is to leave everything to God and say it is for good." 

Repentance is neede for all of us because we all sin all the time. Sin can be performed in 3 different ways: in thought, in word and in action. Hence who is clean form sin of though? Who is clean form sin of word? Only the Virgin Mary is clean from all three types of sins. Hence we all need to confess, communicate our shortcomings to our spiritual father and continuously get spiritual and fatherly advices. Hence it is not only because our dear sister has faced such a terrible situation that she has to go see the priest. She should continuously seek spiritual and fatherly advice and consult with her spiritual father on what to do.

May God help us live a life or repentance so we can stay in His house until the last breathe and inherit His Kingdom.

text.text:
Question: I, as an Orthodox believe that Jesus Christ is God. There are also Bible verses that prove this. However, many have difficulty accepting that Jesus is God, and that he is one of the Holy Trinity, due to there still are other verses that say, "Hear my Father" when Jesus speaks. Therefore, how can we explain to those who do not believe in simple language? Becauseb this is difficult to understand it.

Answer:

text:
The question is related to theology and the mystery of the Trinity. He said not only 'my father', but 'he has begotten me'. To understand this, it is necessary to know about the mystical Trinity and the mystical incarnation. Previously, when we talked about the divinity of Jesus Christ, we talked extensively about the names of God. There are names by which the Lord was called in ancient times, that were unknown before His birth. And Jesus is his New Testament name. The names we call 'Jesus Christ', 'Jesus' are when he became flesh, became a perfect God (he was already God), a perfect Man; He is a Man and is God. He is God even after he dies, rises, and ascends. Therefore, when he becomes a man, what we speak about him, what He too speaks is that he speaks as if there is another father, another superior authority, to mean for the united body; The flesh that was a creature is saying that I have become God. (because he  was God before He united the flesh;   the flesh became absolute God when   Divinity united it; and He became absolute Man, absolute God) Jesus is the son of man and the son of God.

Our Lord Jesus is one of the Trinity Body, who was and is Glorified, praised equally together with the Almighty father & Holy spirit, before the creation of the world and forever. so, God the Son is God in a different form, he is the creator, he is almighty, he is pure and he is holy. When he was born from the virgin Mary, there is a body that arose from her, and he chose her as a pure saint for motherhood, starting from the womb, so that the sin of Adam would not be passed on to her. This is the teaching of our church, and this is what our holy fathers have revealed to them and said about her in all their books and common teachings.

In the holy book, when St. Gabriel announces her purity, virginity and is different from all women; he does not describe her femininity in the language used by other people. For example, a girl is called a 'woman' after losing her virginity; but  our Lady Virgin Mary is a virgin forever. She is a virgin before her conception, during her conception, and after her conception. She is a virgin before, during, and after giving birth.

Therefore, the flesh united from this mother is perfect God. What happened to the flesh that was the creature? He became a god. This is why:

1.  The expression "my father" refers to the birth of the pre-world without a mother. This is an inscrutable birth, it is a subtle birth, it is a birth beyond our imagination. Even we, let alone him, talk normally about the secret of reproduction from our mother and father,  but this even itself is abstract. Doctors confirm that a fetus lives in the mother's womb for nine months and five days before birth, and we know this from experience. But the secret of being born as a human being after this water and blood, as a boy or a girl, when he stayed in the mother's womb for 9 months and 5 days, what kind of food he was being fed, what kind of care, what kind of air he was getting, how he was born as a human being is amazing. After that, when we see how he comes from the darkness to the light world, from non-existence to existence, from the narrow to the wide world, this birth is a mystery. Hence, let alone the birth of God and the birth of man is even a subtle mystery.

text.text: Dear Orthodox friends of John's Repentance website spiritual program series; We have sent you the following educational message regarding the subject mentioned in the title, so we entrust you to read and understand it.

text:
There is a legend that has been told since ancient times. The Almighty God said to the angels, "Go to the earth and bring the most precious things that you find on earth." One of the angels brought a drop of blood that a man had shed to save another man. The Most High God said, "O angel; This that you have brought is glorious in my sight. However, it is not the most glorious one. Another angel came from a patient who died of an infectious disease and a nurse who died from the disease and brought her last breath. The Most High God said, "O angel; This that you have brought is glorious in my sight. However, it is not the most glorious one. Finally, another angel brought the tears of a sinner who had repented in a small cup before God. And God said to the angel, "O angel; "You have brought to me the most noble thing in the world," he replied. (Philokalia: the Bible of Orthodox Spirituality p.159)

The way for a person to return to God after he has sinned is through tears of repentance. The psalmist, Saint David, often tells us about the blessed pearl of the Holy Spirit. Let's notice what he said, "I wash my bed all night long, and I wipe my bed with my tears." He said this because his repentance is through the grace and mercy of the Holy Spirit. For his repentance was not in vain like the repentance of Judas. Again, the psalmist tells us that "weeping will come in the evening, but in the morning there will be joy" (Ps 29 (30):5). This signifies the joy of the Holy Spirit given with tears. It is related to what the Lord said in the Gospel, "Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted" (Matthew 5:4). Tears give spiritual rest to the soul lost in sin, and cause it to gain insight and the revelation of mysteries. When the Holy Gospel talks about Saint Peter, it says, "He went outside and wept bitterly" (Luke 22:62). He received the great responsibility to feed and lead the believers after walking in tears

Our ancestors taught that tears are a gift from God to give birth to a new life. Baptism is one; If a person sins after baptism and is in the work of death, his return and "rebirth" is this tear of repentance. Through the tears of repentance, he renews the grace that he received in baptism, but which was later corrupted by sin.

St. John the Baptist said, "The fire of sin is steadfast." But a few drops of tears extinguishes the burning of mistakes (like fire) and purifies our souls. He teaches us this spiritual lesson. Because the tears of true repentance are a gift from God, it explains to us that no matter how bad a person's wrongdoing is, it has the power to destroy that serious sin. St. John said this to indicate that a person can do wrong because of his free will, and whether he does not use it, will be questioned at the time of judgment. We find this holy father often teaching about tears of repentance. One of his teachings where he explained that "tears are both the mother and child of prayer" is worth mentioning. Tears have a great place for a person's eternal life and the union of grace with God. It makes a person compassionate, pure, loving others, forgiving and humble. If he does this, he will live forever as his creator (God).

In general, all members; Thinking only of God's things, we should repent, be in a broken heart to fulfill our canon properly, and pray with tears; Similarly, if we come across other things that can mislead or distract us, we recommend that we need to stay away from them so that we don't fall into sin.

We will return in the next lesson about the obstacles to repentance, so stay tuned

text.text: What does the Church say about anxiety and depression treatment?

Question:  Hello. What are doctrines of the Church regarding anxiety and depression?  In the medical world, for example, it is mental illness that requires different types of treatment like therapy, medication etc. Does the church support this? Thank you

✍️ Answer:

text:
First, before we ask What anxiety or depression is, it is important to know how anxiety happnes, What leads people to anexity, What  will be the end result of it? Because if we know the cause of the problem and the damage, the solution will be easy. 

First when we look closely at man, we see that a man becomes anxious, distressed, despaired, depressed, and sad due to being separated from God, the Creator. For this basic principle, it is enough to remember the first man, Adam. Adam is a creature of God created in the image and example of God, in heaven, he was given everything to live in glory. When he lived in Heaven, a law is made for him and he did what he was told to do and did not do what he was told not to do. He lived without worry for seven years, enjoying peace, love, and help, giving thanks, and singing with the holy angels. By saying, God is my father, heaven is my inheritance, paradise is my inheritance and my place. All these blessings came to him because he abided by the law that was set forth for him. 

Once he transpassed God's law, he lost a Lord like God, a place like heaven. After that, he became an abode of anxiety, he became a house of anxiety and he became worried, gripped, self-reprimanded, lost confidence, swallowed by sadness, fell into sadness.

Sin means to lose, to be deprived, to be away, to be lost, to be separated. When we talk about loss, we mean peace, help, sleeplessness, lack of dignity, which conflicts with oneself, discourages, and creates anxiety. Committing sin makes you lose God because God is the owner of everything, the owner of peace, the owner of blessings, the owner of help, the owner of grace. Therefore, when we separate from God, we lose all of these. Sin is transpassinf God's commandments. Anything that is bad is called sin. Therefore, one of the symptoms of a sinful person is anxiety or lack of peace. "There is no peace for the wicked, says my God" (Isaiah 57:20-21). Therefore, when we are in this mood, what we should do is to get up and repent and be reconciled with the Creator. Saint John Chrysostom said, "He who raises himself in repentance is better than he who raises death." It is true, it is greater.

So if we say what is anxiety, it means that it is the result of sin. If we say what sin is, it means losing God. When Adam lost God, he got that kind of anxiety. If we were to say what caused this anxiety, it was his mental problem, his disturbance, his lack of peace. So when we look at what the final solution was, he found peace when he was reconciled with God, and this is possible first of all by sincerely hating sin and returning to God in repentance. This is what the Church teaches. So, it means the only way to cure anxiety and depression is through repentance and living with God. He told us, "You can do nothing without me." John 15:5

As our questioner said above, medical experts also tell us that people who have lost their peace, people who are depressed can be saved with medicine. This may be reassuring for a while. But it does not bring a permanent solution. Man can never be at peace apart from God, so the solution is to live with God in religion. People who have fallen into sin, repenting, fulfilling their canons, receiving His holy body and precious blood, listening to the voice of God regularly, fasting, praying, prostrating, obeying God's commands, doing what God says to do, and not doing what God says not to do, will bring them out of anxiety.

text.text: Christ is born! Glory be to Him!

Beloved and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on John's Repentance page, we send you this writing about today's feast, the nativity of Christ written by Bishop Youssef of the Coptic Orthodox Church because it is important to understand what we are celebrating, so we entrust you to read it and learn from it.

text:
The birth of our Lord Jesus Christ marks the beginning of a New Covenant between God and man, a covenant previously and purposefully foreshadowed and prepared for by a prior covenant.

In order to understand and appreciate the New Covenant that God has instituted with humanity, it is necessary to take a close look at the old one.

The Old Covenant was between God and Israel "And I will establish My covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you in their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and your descendants after you" (Genesis 17:7). The New Covenant, however, is established between God and any person who will receive the Son of God "But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God (John 1:12,13).

The Old Covenant was temporary, and conditioned upon the Israelites’ obedience of the law. God foretold to Moses that this covenant would not last but would soon be broken, "this people will rise and play the harlot with the gods of the foreigners of the land, where they go to be among them, and they will forsake Me and break My covenant which I have made with them. Then My anger shall be aroused against them in that day, and I will forsake them" (Deut 31:16,17). On the other hand, the New Covenant is designed for eternal life; and will thus last forever. St. Paul says, "The God of peace who brought up our Lord Jesus from the dead, that great Shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant …" (Heb 13:20,21).

In the Old Covenant, there was no hope of eternal life for a person who broke any of the prescribed laws. In that sense, the law could not bring salvation nor justify anyone. All it could do was teach people the need for salvation by a Savior and by His grace granted henceforth. In contrast, in the New Testament, we are justified and sanctified by the work of our Lord Jesus Christ through the Holy Spirit.

The ceremony of the Old Covenant included the slaughter of a heifer, a goat, a ram, a dove, and a young pigeon. After that Abraham cut the carcasses in half, and then at sunset only God walked the blood path between the two pieces of the carcasses (Genesis 15). Usually both parties of the Covenant would walk the blood path between the slaughtered animals as a symbol of what would happen to either party if they violated the terms of the agreement. It is interesting to note that with Abraham, only God walked the blood path to indicate that if Abraham or his descendants dishonored the covenant, God and only God would have to pay the price with His own blood.

The New Covenant has been established not by the slaughter of animals but by the slaughter of the Son of God on the holy wood of the Cross, after having walked the blood path Himself. "Why is Your apparel red, And Your garments like one who treads in the winepress? I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the peoples no one was with Me. For I have trodden them in My anger, And trampled them in My fury; Their blood is sprinkled upon My garments, and I have stained all My robes" (Isaiah 63:2-3).

The old law revolved around a system of animal sacrifices performed by chosen priests from the tribe of Levi. These Levitical priests had to make an offering for their own sins before they could offer sacrifices on behalf of anyone else. It is important to note that, there were many priests, who because of their sins and consequent spiritual death were prevented from continually offering the sacrifice. On the other hand, in the New Covenant our Mediator is a High Priest who being sinless, offered His own blood (for our forgiveness) for us and brought His sacrifice to Heaven itself as the only perfect offering to God. Because He has been raised from the dead, His perfect priesthood continues forever (Heb 7:23,24).

While the Old Covenant was written on two tablets of stone, the New Covenant is an Internal Covenant written on our hearts by the Holy Spirit who dwells in us "I will put my laws into their minds, and I will write them on their hearts" (Heb 8:10).

We knew sin through the Law "the Old Covenant" (Rom 7:7-11) and with the Law, there was no forgiveness but curse and wrath. However, through the New Covenant we have received the forgiveness of our sins: "For I will be merciful to their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more" (Heb 8:12).

The Old Covenant revealed the holiness of God in the righteous standard of the Mosaic Law and promised the coming of the Redeemer, but the New Covenant has shown the holiness of God in the righteousness of His Son.

The Old Covenant became obsolete with the appearance of the New Covenant which is eternal: "When He said, ’A New Covenant,’ He has made the first obsolete. But whatever is becoming obsolete and growing old is ready to disappear" (Heb 8:13).

From the above comparison between the old and new covenants, it is obvious that the New Covenant is a much better one because it establishes a new and better relationship between God and man… As St Paul says, "And for this reason He is the Mediator of the New covenant" (Heb9:15) because "… now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, inasmuch as He is also Mediator of a better covenant, which was established on better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for a second" (Heb 8:6,7).

Through His incarnation, our Lord Jesus Christ became a Mediator of the New Covenant that was foreseen by Jeremiah the prophet, "Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah--not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, My covenant which they broke, though I was a husband to them, says the Lord. But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put My law in their minds, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people. No more shall every man teach his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' for they all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them, says the Lord. For I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more" (Jeremiah 31: 31-34).

St. John Chrysostom explains the meaning of a Mediator, "What is a 'Mediator'? A mediator is not lord of the thing of which he is mediator, but the thing belongs to one person, and the mediator is another: as for instance, the mediator of a marriage is not the bridegroom, but one who aids him who is about to be married. So then also here: The Son became Mediator between the Father and us. The Father willed not to leave us this inheritance, but was wroth against us, and was displeased with us as being estranged from Him; He accordingly became Mediator between us and Him, and prevailed with Him."

text:
👆🏾

The New Covenant has been instituted by the blood of the Lamb, "In the same manner He also took the cup after supper, saying, this cup is the new covenant in My blood. This do, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me" (1Cor 11:25). St. John Chrysostom elaborates, "But they were not sprinkled with "scarlet wool," nor yet "with hyssop." Why was this? Because the cleansing was not bodily but spiritual, and the blood was spiritual. How? It flowed not from the body of irrational animals, but from the Body prepared by the Spirit. With this blood not Moses but Christ sprinkled us, through the word which was spoken; "This is the blood of the New Testament, for the remission of sins." This word, instead of hyssop, having been dipped in the blood, sprinkles all. And there indeed the body was cleansed outwardly, for the purifying was bodily; but here, since the purifying is spiritual, it enters into the soul, and cleanses it, not being simply sprinkled over, but gushing forth in our souls. The initiated understand what is said. And in their case indeed one sprinkled just the surface; but he who was sprinkled washed it off again; for surely he did not go about continually stained with blood. But in the case of the soul it is not so, but the blood is mixed with its very substance, making it vigorous and pure, and leading it to the very unapproachable beauty."

Let us praise the Lord with the angels for His birth and the establishment of the New Covenant saying, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill toward men."

May the Glorious Feast of the Nativity bless us and alert us to rededicate our hearts and lives to the New Covenant with our Lord Jesus Christ.

Bishop Youssef, 
              Coptic Orthodox
              Diocese of the Southern 
              United States

text.text: Why confess to a Priest instead of confessing directly to God?

Question - Why do I have to confess to a Priest? can't I, myself, confess directly to God?

Answer:

text:
Repentance is one of the requirements for any Christian. A person who confesses their sins to the priest considers the priest as God's messenger and God as the judge. The Bible says, "For the priest is the messenger of the Lord of hosts." (Malik 2:7) Repentance is a great thing that includes various actions. Among these are: admitting the wrongdoing and confessing the sin to God, to the priest and accepting the canon through the priest or penitent father.

Therefore, when a person commits a sin, they first confesses to God admiting to their sin and pouring tears of repentance before God. We confess our sins to God not to tell him what he doesn't know, but to ask for his forgiveness and mercy by trusting that we have wronged him. But this does not exclude confessing to a priest; Confession to a priest is part of confessing to God, not a substitute for that. Confession to a priest does not exclude confession to God; On the other hand, it is wrong to think that confession to God is a substitute to confession to a priest

Confession of sins to the penitent father is not only appropriate and necessary, but it is also a duty that has no alternative because it is God's command. The priestly authority that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ gave to the holy apostles is an abstract and heavenly authority allowing them to bind and loose sin. It is also the authority given to them by the Holy Spirit to help people enter into the kingdom of God and to prevent them from the kingdom of God. This means that when God Jesus Christ, who has all power, chose and appointed the 12 apostles and 72 disciples from among the world so that when people  committed sins, they could come to the apostles repented of their sins and confessed their sins, because they were given the authority to forgive all those who have sinned, because the authority given to them will destroy all their sins. - Our Lord says to the priests in his gospel, "You are the light of the world" Matthew 5-14. Priests are the ones who lead us to the Kingdom of God through repentance, lead us away from impurity, darkness and sin, and lead us to hate sin and live a virtuous life.
 
On the day when the Holy Spirit descended, through the sermon of Saint Peter, the apostles converted 2000 people. The people then asked the apostles 'What should we do?  We don't have our own personal lives anymore and there is nothing better than this. There is blessing under you and around you.' The apostles replied to them saying 'Repent'. If we ask what the apostles mean when they say this, it means 'come tell us your repentance' (confess your sins)

When we look at the story of Lazarus, when a man in hell said to Abraham, please let me come to you, and let me rest for a moment. Abrham said to him there is a great gulf between you and me, you cannot come to me. Then he said to Abrham, "I beg you father, send Lazarus to my family, 28 for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also come to this place of torment.." And Abraham said, "They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them."

text:
👆🏾

Therefore, what we learn from this is that it is God who taught, placed and appointed these fathers among us to tell us the truth, teach us, and advise us. The penitent fathers are also responsible and accountable for the souls of every person under their fatherhood. God said through the prophet Ezekiel "When I say to the wicked, ‘You shall surely die,’ and you give him no warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life, that same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require at your hand." Which is a strong reminder of this serious responsibility. This is why the Apostle St. Paul said, "Obey your superiors, be submissive; As if they were giving a reckoning, so that they would do this not with sorrow but with joy...strive for your souls" (Hebrews 13:17). These are the fathers of penitence who are said to give account and fight for your soul.

Therefore, our questioner should understand it in this regard. Also, a quote from the Bible? For those who asked, we recommend that you read and understand what we have listed below.

- St. John the Baptist was baptizing the people with a baptism of repentance that prepares them for Christ. At that time, the people would come to him and confess their sins to him before being baptized in the baptism of repentance. When the Holy Bible talks about this, it says: "At that time all Jerusalem and Judea and all the country around the Jordan would go up to him and be baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins" (Matthew 3:5-6). Therefore, just as the people used to confess their sins to John the Baptist when they repented so that they could be baptized in the baptism of repentance, it means that the faithful confess their sins to their penitent fathers before they approach the holy mysteries. Also, just as John gave them advice and rebuke, the fathers of penitence will give advice and canon that they think is appropriate based on the life and circumstances of the deceased. Matthew 3:8-10

- When we look at Achan's story, in Isaiah 7:21-23, Joshua said to Achan: My son, give glory to God, the God of Israel, confess to Him, and tell me what you have done, don't hide from me. And Achan answered Joshua and said, "I have indeed sinned against the God of Israel, I have done such and such" (7:21-23). Joshua, give Achan the glory of God, confess; Just as he says, "Tell me, don't hide from me, what a person confesses to his penitent father is part of his confession to God." When Achan confessed to Joshua, he was confessing to God. Therefore, when he confesses to his penitent father, he makes God the judge, and the penitent believes that his father will forgive his sins and be forgiven according to the authority given by God, and reconcile him to his creator.

In the New Testament, when a man with leprosy approached him and asked, "Lord, if you want to, you can cleanse me," bowing down; then the Lord stretched out his hand and touched him and said, "I want to cleanse you. Be Cleansed." And he was free from leprosy. After that, our Lord immediately ordered the leper whom he had just cleansed to say: " Be careful not to tell anyone, but go and show yourself to the priest; And as a witness to them, offer him the offering that Moses commanded." Matthew 8:2-4 The surprising thing is that, even though our Lord healed the leper himself, (although there was nothing else that was needed more in our Lord's healing), but our Lord himself  has ordered the person by saying :- "Go, and show yourself to the priest,”

text:
👆🏾

We can also see this father-son relationship of repentance in the relationship between King David and the prophet Nathan. When David was thinking about building a temple, it was the prophet Nathan who consulted him and told him to refer to God. Prophet Nathan was praying to God and telling David the answer he received from God. Later, when David was hindered by sin, God sent the same prophet, Nathan to wake David up from the sleep of sin and to repent. And Nathan went and told David his sin with wisdom and tact. At that time, David admitted his mistake, repented, and confessed. By this we understand that the father of repentance is needed not only for confession, but also to advise and bring to repentance.

Our Lord and God Jesus Christ has shown us the actions and performance of the father of repentance. The Samaritan woman was heartbroken and hurt from the complex ups and downs of her life, so she came to draw water when no one was around so that no one would see her. When our Lord spoke to her, starting the conversation by taking about water, he gradually elevated the conversation from earthly to heavenly, from temporal matters to eternal matters. Then our Lord said to her, "Go, call your husband and come here." He was opening the door and showing her the way for her to confess her sin. She replied, "I don't have a husband." Then our Lord said, "You said well that I do not have a husband; For you have had five husbands, and the one who is with you now is not your husband; And in this you have spoken the truth" by saying what she was afraid to say, he made her understand that he is her God who knows all her life. (John 4:1-42) Our Lord showed us this in practice, to teach that the father of repentance should talk to each soul and find a way to heal it, not in a public sermon where many people have gathered, but in a private, slow, wise and careful manner. Therefore, the relationship between the penitent father and the repentant son is such a mysterious relationship that exists only between the two of whom only God is the witness.

- Father of repentance means our confidant, our closest advisors in our spiritual and physical life. The wise man Sirach said, "Let many people be your friends, and let one of many be your counsel, and let your counsel be one with your heart." Sirac 6-6. This means that even though the faithful may have many priests to teach them about religion and morals, one of them should be the teacher to whom they confess their repentance. Father of repentance means confidant and counselor.

- Therefore, we should not live without a penitent father or stay away from a penitent father. Because we need a priest who can stand as a witness for all the spiritual work we do before God. In subtle and mysterious ways the holy angels stand as our guardians; In this real world and in the life we live as a Christian, our priests and fathers have been appointed by God to be shepherds of our souls. Because the authority given to them by God to bind and loose sins is not in vain, we should respect and use the system of repentance that God has made for us.

We must also understand that repentance is not a human command, but a Creator's directive. No Christian should spend a single day without a repentant father. Therefore, every member of the Orthodox Church, from the time he reaches the age of majority, has a Christian duty to have a penitent father and confess his sins to his penitent father for it is said “And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven." (Matthew 16᎓19)

text:
According to the evidence mentioned above, the keys to the kingdom of God were given to the apostles and those who came after them. It is important to note that the opening and closing of the keys to a house or door is not a physical thing; rather, it refers to the authority given to the apostles to enter the kingdom of heaven and to deny entry to those who do not deserve it. Instead, it refers to the grace given by the Holy Spirit to atone for the sins of sinners and to hold their lives accountable, as previously explained.

text.text: Beloved and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on John's Repentance page, we send you this writing about the nativity and incarnation of Christ written by Bishop Youssef of the Coptic Orthodox Church because it is important to understand the mistery of incarnation, so we entrust you to read it and learn from it.

text:
Upon the Feast of the Incarnation of the Word, it is important to reflect upon the birth of the Lord Jesus Christ and what He represents. St. John in His Holy Gospel wrote, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." (1:1) and the Apostle also wrote, "The Word became flesh and dwelt among us." (1:14) Through these Holy Scriptures we learn that the Lord Jesus Christ is God, for He was with God before all times. This is the reason we recite, "We believe in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Only begotten Son of God…" in the Nicene Creed.

Lactantius (c.304) wrote, "He who hears the Son of God mentioned should not conceive in his mind so great an impiety as to think that God begat Him by marriage and union with a woman…In what manner, then, did God beget Him? First of all, divine operations cannot be known or declared by anyone. Nevertheless, the sacred writings teach us…that this Son of God is the speech or even the reason of God…With good reason, therefore, He is called the Speech and the Word of God. For, by a certain incomprehensible energy and power of His Majesty, God enclosed the vocal spirit proceeding from His mouth into a form that has life through its own perception and wisdom. So God did not conceive the Word in His womb, but in His mind…Now, our human words are mingled with the air and they fade away. However, they can still be preserved in writing. How much more must we believe that the voice of God both remains forever and is accompanied with perception and power? It has derived this from God the Father like a stream from a fountain. Someone may be puzzled that God could be produced from God the Father by putting forth of the voice and breath. However, if such a person is acquainted with the sacred utterances of the prophets, he will cease to wonder…The Greeks speak of Him as the Logos, more appropriately that we Romans do as the "Word" or "Speech." For logos means both speech and reason. And He is both the Voice and the Wisdom of God."

His birth on earth was not His actual beginning, as the Lord Jesus Christ is without beginning. He has existed forever, for all times. From the very beginning the Incarnation was planned. This is the reason we recite in the Nicene Creed, "Begotten of the Father before all age; Light of Light, true God of true God…"

 St. Clement of Alexandria (c. 195), a learned and respected scholar who was in charge of the theological college in Alexandria, Egypt, wrote, "That the Son was always the Word is signified by saying, 'In the beginning was the Word."

Clearly we understand that He was born a man, "for He became flesh." He was like the earthly human but without sin dwelling among us. He was born both as God and man never denying His Divinity. The two are united without confusion between them. God has entered into earthly history as a man.

Thus with understanding we recite, "Begotten not created, of one essence with the Father, by Whom all things were made; Who for us, men, and for our salvation, came down from Heaven, and was incarnated of the Holy Spirit and became man" in the Nicene Creed.
