👉👉🏾Question: Thank God for answering all my questions and I have benefited from the answer. The next questions I have are :-

👉#1. How to choose a confessor and

 👉#2. How to  prepare to confess my sins?

Answer:

text:
Dear member; askng more questions and being eager to bear spiritual fruit based on what we learned previously is truly commendable. We entrust you to persevere in your purpose until the end, we too will do our best to serve you in all your way.  To repent or to come to a life of repentance and to confess your sins as a priority and to prepare for repentance is really the loyalty expected of a true Christian. God is a God of love, He always waits for us to return from our sins, with an open arms and call us His children.

When the prophet Ezekiel said that God does not like the death of a person and loves the return of a person to repentance, he said, "“Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways,” says the Lord God. “Repent, and turn from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your ruin. 31 Cast away from you all the transgressions which you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Israel? 32 For I have no pleasure in the death of one who dies,” says the Lord God. “Therefore turn and live!” (Ezekiel 18:30-32)

If we quote this word as an introduction; When we come to the question proposed by our questioner, let's start with your 2nd question, what should we do before we repent and after we repent? 

The following are mainly mentioned in the emotional and practical processes that are important if a believer is to do the awareness or understanding before he reaches the repentance of the believer.

-

Before we repent, we must confess our sin and feel remorse. This type of regret follows failure, embarrassment, shame, loss, mistakes. A person who knows his sinfulness thinks about his transgression against God, other people, and his own soul. He mainly hates the sin he committed. The kindling of this kind of feeling in us is one of the signs of our vitality that explains why we do not lie comfortably on the bed of sin. As the prophet advised us, "If you repent and cry, you will be saved" (Isaiah 30:15). Crying for the sins we have committed is a great and bright way to be saved and to find forgiveness for our sins.

-

One of the behaviors that help us easily hate sin is fearing God. The wise Solomon said, "He who fears God hates sin; "He hates envy and pride, and hates evil ways" (Proverbs 8:13). The great holy father Mar Isaac told us the great spiritual truth that if we do not hate the sin that we are repeatedly tempted by, it will reign on us. Abhorrence is the greatest degree of hatred, so it is necessary not only to abhor sin, but also to abhor thinking about it.

-

Being ashamed of sin, hating sin, and turning back. A person who knows these well and has not come out of the slavery of sin will not hesitate for a moment to return to his former duty. Therefore, the first and most important thing that helps us not to go back to sin again is to admit that we have sinned and confess to ourselves, and to hate sin. Hating sin is the greatest force that helps us separate from sin and leave it forever. We cannot truly repent of sin while in the love of sin; Also, living in a fixable problem, we cannot fix it without separating from it.
 
-

To solve a problem in any area of our life, we must have a different perspective and desire than the one we had when the problem was created. Problems cannot be solved with a lazy mind, it is impossible to love with a hateful mind, and it is difficult to hate with a loving mind. Nor will he come to repentance with a sinful mind. Therefore, any change requires a change of thinking first. For this, our greatest powers are faith, good vision, and hope.

text:

text:

Their first children are "Cain and Cain's twin Lud". Next to Cain are "Abel and his twin Akelema."

After Adam and Eve gave birth to their children, Adam said to Eve, "Eve, your children have reached the age of marriage." Then it was revealed to Adam that when he was making a law in the Torah, in the days of Moses, that a relative should not marry a relative would be written. This shows us that in the future there will be a law that would state one should not marry a relative.

Adam then said it was better for Cain's twin to marry Abel than to marry her own twin. He did this because, in Adam's opinion, their relationship was a bit distant. Similarly, he thought that it would be better for Abel's twin to marry Cain than to marry her twin. Cain’s twin sister, Lud, looked like Eve and was good-looking unlike Abel’s twin, Akelema, and Cain was not happy about marrying Akelema and was disappointed.

He questioned, why should Abel marry my beautiful sister? Why should I marry Abel’s twin, who is not beautiful in appearance? He said he was disappointed. Adam said to him, this is not to happen, he should not marry his own sister, it will be annulled.

After that, they offered a sacrifice. Abel offered the sacrifice to God, which was a lamb that had no horns and no claws. Cain prepared a sacrifice saying 'God will not eat my sacrifice, whether he accepted it or not.' God looked at Abel's sacrifice. The look shows that he accepted Abel’s offerings, but he did not look at Cain and his sacrifice, which means that he did not accept it.

Cain was very angry because God accepted Abel's sacrifice and he felt that his father Adam and God were unfair to him. He thought to himself "who can be evil like me?" But when he brought it out, Satan appeared to him and said to him, "What happened to you?" Cain replied, "my brother took the wife that was right for me, and my father gave it to Abel. God accepted his sacrifice, but he did not accept mine." Satan said, "What bothers you about this? Call Abel to the field and ask him to go drink water and kill him and you can have both." Driven by jealousy, Cain killed his brother Abel.

When Adam married his sons, as we said above, he gave Abel's twin to Cain and Cain's twin to Abel. This means that he separated them and did not make them marry each other. This shows us that one should not marry a relative.

text: The birth of our Lord Jesus Christ has become a turning point in the history of mankind; making it feasible to classify incidents into pre and post Nativity. It has also marked the birth of humanity; for in the Nativity was the Incarnation, and in the Incarnation was Salvation and through Salvation we received adoption becoming heirs to the Kingdom.

The Imminence and the Indispensability of Salvation
The Incarnation basically means that God became man; taking a body from the Virgin Mary by the Holy Spirit. "Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel" (Isaiah 7:14). The most important reason for the Incarnation was to resolve the redemption issue bringing man back to his first rank of which he had fallen off because of sin. God had created Adam and placed him in the garden of Eden commanding him to not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, warning him that the day he would disobey, he would die "but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die" (Genesis 2:17). Through his wickedness, Satan enticed Eve to eat from the forbidden fruit. In doing so, Adam and Eve disobeyed God and broke the law. Consequently Adam had to die and perish in order to satisfy and fulfill God’s justice; otherwise God would breach his own claim of justice and credibility.

However, Adam’s death would have caused a number of ramifications, and would have been:
Against God’s Mercy. Adam was the victim of Satan’s enticing and tempting.

Against God’s Dignity. God created man in His own image and made him ruler over all his creatures. How then would God’s image be torn up so easily?

Against God’s Wisdom. God created man with wisdom to enjoy His love, blessings and sonship. How dare Satan deprive man of these free gifts? St. Athanasuis contemplates on this saying; "it was better for man if he was not created than to be created to face this fate."

Against God’s Power. God had not created man to desert him and leave him without protection against Satan; for the power is God’s and not the devils; "Thine is the power" (the Lord’s Prayer).

Thus, it is only through the unity of the Divinity with the Humanity that all the specifications required from a redeemer would get to be fulfilled. These specifications are:

Divinity: Through His divinity and infinite righteousness, the redeemer would pay off the punishment for our infinite sin.

Humanity: Through His humanity, the redeemer would represent man who had sinned and had been sentenced to die in order to pay the price which is death itself. "And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifested in the flesh" (1 Timothy 3:16).

Redemption Resided in the Incarnation
Because man sinned against the infinite God; his sin was limitless demanding limitless punishment which could not be atoned for through man’s limited capacity for repentance. Man’s nature had become corrupted by sin; and so required a limitless atonement. Who is limitless except God Himself? God Himself had to take upon Himself the redeeming and atoning act in order to rescue man from this eternal death.

Terms of Redemption
God’s justice demands that the redeemer be:

text:
Pure, Holy, and without Sin. Man has certainly fallen short of these qualities because "they have all turned aside; they have together become unprofitable; There is none who does good, no, not one" (Romans 3:12).

Omnipotent. It requires someone stronger than the enemy to defeat him. Only God is stronger than Satan, the accuser and manipulator. He is the only one who could pay off man’s debts and remove his unlimited sin. No one is omnipotent but God.

Of Human Nature. The verdict was decreed against man. Therefore neither an animal nor an angel was eligible to revert it. The former is not human and the latter is a spirit.

Willing to die for Man. For God to fulfill His ultimate justice He would not impose atonement. It has to be a voluntary, unconditional love act. Thus the imminence of the Incarnation becomes evident. It is impossible for man to be redeemed from his fallen nature except by God Himself. Through His Incarnation, He becomes representative of man, mortal like him and through his Godhead He remains omnipotent and sinless.

The Blessings of the Incarnation
Adoption. "But when the fullness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption as sons" (Galatians 4:4,5).

Partakers of the divine nature. "those who were once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit" (Hebrews 6:4).

Blessed in Him. Our new man has become renewed in the Creator’s image "since you have put off the old man with his deeds" (Colossians 3:9) and our human nature has become blessed in him after He has given our nature the spirit of power and victory. "But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you" (Acts 1:8).

God's proximity to us. God became close to man "That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, concerning the Word of life" (1 John 1:1).

Establishment of Peace on Earth. "And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God and saying "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill toward men!" (Luke 2:13,14).

👉

Trinity is a noun derived from the Geez verb that means three. This is the lesson we learn about the trinity of God's body. Trinity is very different from three. For three speaks of three different things, and trinity speaks of three things in one thing. Therefore, when talking about trinity, it is necessary to talk about unity. 

Therefore, in the mystery of the Trinity, we learn not only about the threeness of God's body, but also about the unity of his character. In short, Trinity is the teaching that God is one and three.

The Son's body is always the Son's; The body of the Holy Spirit is always the Holy Spirit. That is, the bodies do not change, do not exchange, do not absorb. In their position, in their appearance and in their name, they will remain forever on their own. The names by which the bodies are called also remain unchanged for their bodies. Therefore, just as we say that the Trinity is three in body, so we say three in their name as well; and these Trinity Names are: Father, Son, Holy Spirit, (Matthew 28:19  ; Psalm 33:14, 118:73, Isaiah 66:1, Genesis 18:1-4 Matthew 3:16)

Question፦ I was once told that the prayer of absolution at the beginning of the Divine Liturgy Service can be considered as forgiveness of sin before partaking in the Sacrament of Holy Communion is this Orthodox practice? Can this be considered a substitute for confession of you didn't have time to meet with your priest before?

👉Answer:

text:
If we understand the purpose of the question correctly: In the Liturgy, after the prayer, the priest blesses the people with a cross saying, 'May God forgive', does this system of atonement for sins replace the system where we will personally go to the Father of repentance and confess our sins and receive forgiveness of sins? Also, if we approach any priest in person (without confessing our sins) and say 'God forgive you' and bless us with a cross, will all our sins be forgiven? Before we answer these questions, it is appropriate to look at the types of sin.  

Types of sin: Although there are many types and methods of sin, they can be divided into 3 categories. These are of thought, speech, and action. The basis of sin is thought. Because no one commits any sin unintentionally. If something happens unexpectedly, it is not often questioned; But he will be punished for not being careful in his simplicity. Therefore, every human being must get rid of the thoughts that are the root of sin. When it is thought of, he must immediately correct himself by calling upon God's name and condemning Satan.

Constantly thinking about something wrong reveals a willingness to do it. He will become addicted to it. This will count as done. In other words, it is a matter of time, place, and situation that he was not able to do it, because if it is convenient for him, he wouldn't  hesitate to do it. In fact, if after he has spent a lot effort, he allows himself to commit his sin but faces an obstacle that is beyond his control and returns, it is considered that he has already committed , it and committed a complete wrongdoing.

Also, a person may see, hear, or speak evil things while walking, or wherever he is. But if he realizes that this is an offense and immediately calls upon the name of God and condemns Satan and abandons him, and does not follow his thoughts, it is not considered an offense. But if he is still eager to watch, hear, and talk about that thing, and if he is motivated to make that thing happen, then he will be considered to have put all this into action, committed wrongdoing, and committed a sin. On the other hand, there is a reason why a sin committed instantly without thinking about it is not considered a major sin, and we have explained this above, but there will be a canon that finds it as it is.

When the priests pray that God will forgive us, which of these types of sins (thoughts, words, deeds) will be forgiven?👇

As we have seen above, every evil desire that a person has taken out and brought down in his inner conscience and has not yet put into action is called a sin of thought. The sin that is thought in the heart is called the sin of speech when it is spoken by the mouth. If the sin that is said orally is put into action, it is called the sin of action.

text:

A/ The ten words of the old testament

text:
The ten words of the old testament are the ten words that God made a covenant with mankind.

We believe that God has given His true word that by keeping these laws, we will receive grace and blessings from God, and that if we break them, we will suffer calamities. They are as follows.

1. I am God your God, you shall worship no other god before me (Exodus 22:7)

2. Do not take the name of God your God in vain; For God will surely punish him who makes his name worthless. (Exodus 20:7).

3. Consider the Sabbath day, that you may sanctify it. (Exodus 20:1-11)

4. Honor your father and mother; In the land that God will give you so that your life will be long. (Zech 20:12)

5. Do not kill a soul (Zech 20:13).

6. Do not commit adultery (Exodus 20:14)

7. Do not steal; (Exodus 20:15)

8. Do not bear false witness against your neighbor (Exodus 20:16).

9. Do not covet everything that belongs to your neighbor (Exodus 20:17).

10. Love your neighbor as yourself (Leviticus 19:18)

God is the supreme king, the God of gods. He is the creator and ruler of the visible and invisible worlds. He has set forth a constitution that specifically governs human beings. Therefore, it is the duty of all to preserve what he has done, as no one can undo or improve it. These laws are divided into 10 articles, and 3 of them are related to God. They are:

1/ I am God your God. You shall not worship any other god before me.

2/ Don't take God's name, your God's name in vain; For God will surely punish him who makes his name worthless.

3/ Think of the Sabbath day, that you may sanctify it.

This revelation warns us that we should not give God's worship to idols or to fortune-telling. He is the only one who should be worshipped, because worship belongs to his nature and personality.

He alone was, and He alone is, and He alone is God who lives forever.

Therefore, we should not give the honor and worship that is due to him to a foreigner because there is no one who can compete with him.

He also warns us not to invoke his name in vain. God's name is only invoked in praise and in prayer;

The 3rd paragraph urges us to celebrate God's Sabbath, which God made as a day of rest for the glory of mankind, to make it a day of rest.

On this day, he warns us not to do any other physical activities than doing charity, listening and preaching the holy word.

But the other seven clauses are what everyone who is a human being should do for himself, human beings and the like, should do and fulfill. And they are:

That means, think about the expenses that parents spent on your life, food, health; It means that you have to know what you owe them and be greatful for what they did for you. 

His human wisdom in honoring his parents; It is revealed that he is a higher creation. Believe that tomorrow you will be repaid from your children, now you help and take care of your children.

The feast of Epiphany is the feast of Baptism. This feast is also called the feast of the divine manifestation (the Theophania).

text:

👉 Institution of the Sacrament

Our Lord instituted this Sacrament on Covenant Thursday, just a few hours before His arrest and trial. After He had washed the feet of the disciples as a sign of their repentance and preparation, “He took bread, blessed it and broke it, and gave it to the disciples and said, ‘Take, eat; this is My body.’ Then He took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, ‘Drink from it all of you. This do, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.’ For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death till He comes” (1 Cor 11:23-26)

👉 Symbols of the Eucharist in the Old Testament

The offering of Melchizedek (bread & wine) was a symbol of this Holy Sacrament, “Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was the priest of God Most High” (Gen 14:18). He who eats this bread will live forever” (Jn 6:58) – “I am the living bread which came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever and the bread that I shall give is My flesh” (Jn 6:51)

👉 The Question of the Real Presence

Our Lord spoke about this Sacrament openly to the Jews but they “quarreled among themselves saying, ‘How can this Man give us His flesh to eat?’” (Jn 6:52).

Moreover, many of the disciples protested saying, “This is a hard saying; who can understand it?” (Jn 6:60). When Lord Jesus explicitly emphasized His real presence in the Sacrament, it was written, “many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more” (Jn 6:66)

The question of the real presence is of considerable importance in relation to the differences, which have emerged within Christianity since the time of the so-called ‘Reformation’. A particularly important witness to the early Christian understanding of this Sacrament is provided by the ‘Catechetical lectures’ of St. Cyril of Jerusalem. This series of 24 lectures of instruction on the beliefs and practices of the Christian Church, given at some point around 350 AD to those preparing for baptism, are an important witness to the ideas that prevailed in the Jerusalem Church around this point. It is clear that St. Cyril regarded the bread and wine as becoming the real body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ:

text:
👆

“[Jesus Christ], by his own will, once changed water into wine at Cana of Galilee. So why should we not believe that he can change wine into blood? … We should therefore have full assurance that we are sharing in the body and blood of Christ. For in the type of bread, his body is given to you, and in the type of wine, his blood is given to you, so that by partaking of the body and blood of Christ you may become of one body and one blood with Him.” (St. Cyril of Jerusalem)

St. John of Damascus wrote the following about the question of how this transformation of the bread and wine takes place:

“And now you ask how the bread becomes the body of Christ, and the wine and the water become the blood of Christ. I shall tell you. The Holy Spirit comes upon them, and achieves things which surpass every word and thought … Let it be enough for you to understand that this takes place by the Holy Spirit” (St. John of Damascus).

👉

Abiding in Lord Jesus Christ: “He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him” (Jn 6:56). Consequently we bear the fruits of the spirit, “He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing” (Jn 15:5)

Obtaining Eternal Life: “Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day… He who eats this bread will live forever” (Jn 6:54,58)

Growth & Maintenance of Our Spiritual Life: “Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you… For My flesh is food indeed, and My blood is drink indeed… he who feeds on Me will live because of Me” (Jn 6:53,55,57)

Salvation & Remission of Sins: “This is My blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many for the remission of sins” (Mt 26:28)

Unification of Believers: “For we, being many, are one bread and one body; for we all partake of that one bread” (1 Cor 10:17)

👉

St. Paul said, “Whoever eats this bread or drinks this cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup. For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning (recognizing clearly) the Lord’s body. For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep (die). For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged.” (1 Cor 11:27-31)

text: The person who approaches the Eucharist must be an Orthodox Christian having no doubt concerning the bread & wine being the true body and precious blood of Lord Jesus Christ.
The person must be practicing the Sacrament of Repentance and Confession on regular basis as St. Paul said, “let a man examine himself” (1 Cor 11:28)

Lord Jesus Christ said, “If you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come offer your gift” (Mt 5:23-24)

The Orthodox Church believes and confesses that the Eucharist is a sacrifice and an offering to God in addition to being a Sacrament. The following supports this belief:

The words of Lord Jesus Christ Himself, “This is My blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many” (Mt 26:28; Mk 14:24) – “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you” (Lk 22:20) – “This is My body which is broken for you” (1 Cor 11:24) – “This is My body which is given for you” (Lk 22:19). Undoubtedly, the terms “broken body” and “shed blood” refer to a sacrifice.

Dear and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on the John's Repentance page;  Today,  we hereby sent you the following basic religion lesson which we prepared in simple way of discription so that everybody can easily understand it; Hence, we entrust you to read and learn from it.

In Orthodoxy, the Five Pillars of Mysteries are called absolute dogmas. Apostle St. Paul explained that there are five pillars of truth and doctrine of salvation in the church. 1 Cor 14:19

The five pillar mysteries are: -

1. Mystery of Trinity: This is where we learn the unity and trinity of the Holy Trinity. Holy Trinity a special and unique form of Trinity and it means three in One, One in three. 

2. Mystery of Incarnation: This is where we learn the mystery of God becoming human. (God came down to us from the heavens and saved us, he became a man and was born from Mary, this mystery is the mystery of God becoming a man.)

3. Mystery of Baptism: This is where we learn about the baptism of our Lord Jesus Christ and the mystery of being reborn from God through baptism. Therefore, the sacrement of baptism in which we are born of water and the Spirit and receive the sonship of God is called the second birth. In Ephesians chapter four, it is written that baptism is one.

4. Mystery of Eucharistic: It is where we learn about the fact that the Holy Body of Jesus Christ and His Precious Blood are eternal life. Drink my blood and eat my flesh, our Lord Jesus Christ told us in his gospel that we must all receive the Holy Communion in order to have eternal life.

5. The Mystery of Resurrection (Eternal Life): This is where we learn about the second coming (the end of the world) and the resurrection of the dead. We believe in the resurrection of the dead, that when our Lord Jesus Christ comes, we will rise from the dead on the last day.

In the below paragraphs, we will take a closer look to briefly explain about  each of the Five Pillars Mysteries፦

1. Mystery of Trinity

The Mystery of Trinity is the first among the five pillars of mysteries at our Orthodox Church. Because it is the most fundamental of all Christian dogmas; and it is the basis for our salvation.  

It is impossible to comprehend the fundamental teachings of the Holy Bible in the absence of a clear understanding about the Mystery of Holy Trinity. This mystery is part and parcel of each and every spiritual life and service.

The Holy Trinity thinks with the heart of the Father and speaks with the words of the Son, and by the breath of the Holy Spirit they live.

Question: Someone asked the question can the Holy Body be given without the precious blood? Must Holy Communion happen after Holy Baptism?
 
✍️Answer #1:

text:
The first question is can the Holy Body be given without the precious blood? Our questioner; First of all, we must understand that we are commanded to receive His Holy Body and His Precious Blood. Our Lord our God Jesus Christ, crucified on the cross, broke his holy body, shed his precious blood, he told us that whoever ate my body and drank my blood has eternal life. He told us that this is my flesh and blood that will be shed for the welfare of the world. Therefore, the creator spoke about both his holy body and his precious blood.

Therefore, we cannot say that if the flesh is present, the blood is not needed, because that is not the teaching we have received from our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. We do it God's way. Eat my flesh, we will eat his flesh; Drink my blood, we will drink his blood. We do what we are exactly told to do. When we look at John 6:55-56, "For my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink. He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, abideth in me, and I in him." He said. He did not say, "He who eats my flesh will live in me, and I will live in him." He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood means that we are commanded to take both. 
 
Therefore, we are commanded to receive his holy body and his precious blood. We are invited, given and commanded by God to have the flesh as food for the soul and the blood as drink for the soul. Therefore, it means that we receive his holy body and his precious blood. This command is God's, so when we accept it and carry it out, the benefit is for ourselves.

To your second question, must Holy Communion happen after Holy Baptism, the answer is Yes. Our Lord Jesus Christ ordered his disciples: “Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” (Mathew 28:19)  Baptism means immersion in a blessed water (in the name of the Holy Trinity). Baptism is the gate/door/Point of entry to Christianity. One cannot be a Christian without baptism. It’s the first sacrament to be performed for all Christians.

So, children, boys at 40 days and girls at 80 days, are baptized for the first time when they are baptized and after that they are sealed/confirmed/anointed with holy myron. The priest says, I anoint you in the name of the Father, I anoint you in the name of the Son, I anoint you in the name of the Holy Spirit, he anoints all the body parts and seals them with holy myron. Then they will be given a baptism name. After that, the person who brought the children to Christianity should take them to the church, and they will celebrate the day's Mass and receive Holy Communion.

So this is the baptism of childhood that we get once. But it does not mean that we are baptized regularly when we receive the holy flesh and the precious blood. Baptism is required for the first time. Only a baptized person can receive the holy flesh and the precious blood. Apart from that, an unbaptized person, an unbeliever will not be given his holy body and precious blood. Believing for the first time is mandatory to be baptized to receive His Holy Body and Precious Blood. Once we believe and are baptized, since infant baptism is once, we are not born again and again after being born once of the Trinity. It means that we are once born and baptized, and those who have fallen into sin, we rise in repentance and continue to receive His Holy Body and His Precious Blood. But for the first time, the foundation is baptism.

text.text: The Church does not provide his holy body and precious blood to unbaptized people.

2. Mystery of Incarnation

(Part 5)

The next major pillar, among the 5 pillar mysteries is called  'Mystery of Incarnation'. Mystery of Incarnation  basically defines the religious and spiritual identity of Orthodox Christianity. Through incarnation, mysteries of the kingdom of God were revealed to human beings. It’s on the basis of this mystery that our apostolic orthodox church got the prefix in its name “Tewahedo”. Tewahedo is a Geez word which represents the inseparable unity between Divinity and humanity in the person of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

This is a teaching about the revelation of God to human beings. This is the Word, one part of the Holy Trinity who never man. “No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.” (John 1:18) His coming is basically to save the world, to reveal his love, a religion where we declare that he is a perfect man. It reveals the reality of redemption of Adam's sin, about how God became Man. He loved mankind and was born of the Holy Virgin Mary to save mankind whose grace was rejected and was about to be crushed by the feet of demons. The other reason He chose to become Human is to reveal his love to mankind. He loved man to the extent of being crucified on the cross.  (Hos 14:4 John 3:16 1John 4:19 Romans 5:8 Ephe 2:4). "When the end of the age came, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, born under the law." As Galatians 4:4 says. The other  reason of His being human is to become an ultimate role model for human beings, (Gen 3:12 4:8 13:13 Ps 61:4 Matt 11:29 2Peter 2:21)., God taught us everything we need to do to become his children.  

We believe that God the Son (Jesus Christ) has two births.  In the pre world, God the Son, has been begotten from God the Father without a mother. In the latter days, through incarnation, He was born from the Holy Virgin Mary with Virginal conception and without a human fatherhood. Then after, the incarnated God the Son, was named Jesus (savior), Christ (the anointed one or Messiah.), Emmanuel (God is with us) and there are other names too, among them Orthodox Christians usually call Him 'Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ' (Medicine of the world). (Galatians 4:4 Isa 7:14 Gen 3:15 18:13 12:8 Ps 107:20).
 
In the mystery of the flesh, the divinity, which is invisible in its nature, was manifested by the incarnation of the flesh. The intangible was grasped, beaten, the immortal died in the flesh, the unhungry hungered and thirsted, the draft smote. The flesh was made alive by the divinity, the flesh to which the ages are counted, and the divinity to whom the ages are not counted (was before all ages), was called the first. Adam became one of us.” According to Genesis 3:22, the first deity was reckoned at the time of his incarnation, the son of God the Father became the son of the Virgin Mary. The Son of a Virgin was called the Son of God the Father.  

Based on Orthodox Tewahdo teaching, incarnation is from two Persons to one Person; and from two natures to one united nature. It means Divine Person and Human united in to one hypostasis, Jesus Christ – He is both perfectly Divine and perfectly Human. Likewise, from two natures to one nature means Divine nature and Human nature perfectly united into one united nature. We believe that this incarnation is without alteration/change, without reversion, without mingling/mixing, without dwelling, without superimposing, without separation, and without detachment.

1. Mystery of Incarnation (Cont'd)

(Part 6 )

The incarnated Lord Jesus Christ is truly God. As He truly is God, He rebuked the sea (Matt 8:23), created eyes (John 9:6) and entered through closed doors (John 20:26). These are possible only for a supernatural power. Moreover, many verses about Jesus’ birth confirm that He truly is God (Luke 2:11 Matt 2:11 Isai 9:6). The incarnated Lord Jesus Christ is also a Human being. He was sleeping (Matt 8:23). He spat on the ground (John 9:6). He ate after resurrection (Luke 24:42). All these confirm that He is also a human being. In short, He is God and human; yet Christ is not two, but one. He is one, however, not by his divinity being turned into flesh, but by God’s taking humanity to himself. He is one, certainly not by the blending of his essence, but by the unity of his person. For just as one human is both rational soul and flesh, so too the one Christ is both God and human. St. Cyril revealed the mystery of Christ's being a man as the mystery of salvation, and said, "Before being a man, Christ is God; And when he is a man, he is God. (Religious Father - St. Cyril. text: (Part 7)

The mystery of baptism is one of the five pillars of mysteries in the Orthodox Tewahdo church. Baptism means immersion in blessed water (in the name of the Holy Trinity). Adam and Eve, by their choice, became slaves to the devil's will. The Lord appeared to save us, and at the age of 30, he was baptized in the Jordan Sea by the hands of John.

The Lord is naturally compassionate, and He wasn't baptized because He needed it. He washed away our sins by being baptized, but not for the sake of adding glory to himself. He had nothing to lack or add to himself because he was baptized or not. He prophesied that he would baptize. Because he pretended to be an example, he was baptized by the hand of John in the Jordan Sea and became an example for us. And so do we. “And now why are you waiting? Arise and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord." According to the instructions of Acts 22:16, we are baptized in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

The mystery of baptism is established by our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. He established it in three ways: by performance, preaching, and giving commission to the church. He established baptism by being our role model and getting baptized by John the Baptist in the Jordan River. (Matthew 3) He cemented the place of baptism in Christian life by establishing baptism through His preaching, as he said, “He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who does not believe will be condemned.” Mark 16:16 says, “Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.” John 3:3-6. He also commissioned the Church to perform baptism as He ordered his disciples: “Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.” Matt 28:19

So, for all who believe in the mystery of the Trinity and the mystery of our incarnation, baptism is our power to erase sin, to receive childhood, and to inherit the kingdom of heaven. "He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who does not believe will be condemned." Mar. 16:16. Baptism is the gate, door, or point of entry to Christianity. One cannot be a Christian without baptism. It’s the first sacrament to be performed for all Christians.

We also believe in baptism for the remission of sins. St. Peter told the people to repent and be baptized: “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins.” Acts 2:38. This is a type of baptism for the remission of sins; there is another type of baptism in which we are baptized on a regular basis for blessing and healing from sickness; the other is sprinkling with holy water to be blessed in holy water during Epiphany to celebrate Jesus' baptism every year; all of these types of baptisms are reputable. But baptism of rebirth, to which we refer in this topic, is the most important of all these types of regular baptism; baptism of rebirth is a necessity for salvation. It’s not just a mere ceremony. The mystery of baptism is one of the five pillars of mysteries in the Orthodox Tewahdo church. Baptism means immersion in blessed water (in the name of the Holy Trinity). Adam and Eve, by their choice, became slaves to the devil's will. The Lord appeared to save us, and at the age of 30, he was baptized in the Jordan Sea by the hands of John.

The Lord is naturally compassionate, and He wasn't baptized because He needed it. He washed away our sins by being baptized, but not for the sake of adding glory to himself. He had nothing to lack or add to himself because he was baptized or not. He prophesied that he would baptize. Because he pretended to be an example, he was baptized by the hand of John in the Jordan Sea and became an example for us. And so do we. “And now why are you waiting? According to the instructions of Acts 22:16, we are baptized in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

text.text: The Link Between Repentance and Humility

text:
In an age when "self-focus" is the rule of the day, and where the ego seems to reign, it is hard for people to see the value of humility. Many people, from politicians to rock stars, seem to climb the ladder of success by being anything but humble. In our darkened state, with sin dominating our lives, and bad habits seemingly insurmountable, holiness seems to be about saints, but unattainable for ourselves. Stuck in our habitual patterns of behavior, we seem to have surrendered all hope for real change.

The antidote to this inertia can be found in one simple act, that of repenting. We fall down before our God, confessing our failure at having kept the commandments, and asking for God's help in turning our lives around. We commit ourselves to crushing down the ego, and acquiring a humble heart. We take every opportunity to accept correction or criticism, without becoming defensive, for we know the truth in the words of Saint John Climacus, "As with the appearance of light, darkness retreats; so, at the fragrance of humility, all anger and bitterness vanishes."

We refrain from judging anyone, but only examine our own conscience, accusing only ourselves. Saint Macarius the Great wrote, “Christians therefore ought to strive continually, and never to pass judgment on anyone—no, not upon the harlot on the street, or upon open sinners and disorderly persons—but to regard all men with singleness of intention and purity of eye, so that it may become like a fixed law of nature to despise no one, to abhor no one, to make no distinctions between them….This is purity of heart, when you see  sinners or sick people, to have compassion on them and be tenderhearted towards them.”

text.text: Source: Abbot Tryphon from the Russian Orthodox Church

Even so, he has no power unless he gets free consent from us.

This ability is voluntary and supported by behavior. The apostle St. Paul said, "Every man deserves to be commanded." 2 Pet 2:19 We can be slaves to those whom we love and to whom we obey. May God cut off the cord of sin that we are willingly drawn into.

What makes man human and separates him from animals is not only his knowledge but also his free will. In other words, our soul has the freedom to be whatever it wants. In general, if freedom, reason, truth, knowledge and good will (choice) are properly integrated, our life can continue spiritually as our God wants. If we do this, our interests will be good. If we do not do this, we will easily fall into the trap of sin. The damage a sinner suffers from his sin is worse than the person on whom he committed the sin or the evil counselor who encouraged him to commit the sin.

Therefore, when we are still thinking about sin, we should return to the good free will as soon as possible, thinking about its final result and the damage it will cause. This is possible by thinking of the words, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength." If this is the case, because the hatred will be faithful and perfect, then it will be difficult for us to even think about sin, and the thought will not come easily to us. Even if we think about it, the good spirit within us opposes it. Therefore, righteousness and sin can be seen and live together, fighting until one is built up and the other is completely defeated. But sin and righteousness do not continue to live together. In addition, if we regularly wash away sin with repentance, and practice planting good things in our minds little by little, the thought of sin will be replaced by righteousness.

text.text: When does a thought become a sin? Which thoughts should we confess and should we confess all bad thoughts?

Question: Is it when we allow and choose to focus on evil thoughts that it becomes a sin or when the thought first pops into our mind? How do we know which thoughts to confess? Do we repent only for the bad thoughts that we have entertained, or also for those that we have rejected when our thoughts flashed? Even if we try to worship and think about something else, if we don't get rid of the bad thoughts that pop up in our heads, do we also confess about them? Do we confess all the bad thoughts that pop into our heads?

Answer:

text: There are many types and methods of sin which all fall under 3 categories: thoughts, words and actions. Every evil desire that a person has brought out in his inner conscience and has not yet put into action is called the
. This sin becomes
when it is spoken by the mouth. And if the sin that is said orally is put into action, it is called the

.

The foundation of sin is thought, because no sin is committed without thought. If something happens unexpectedly, it is not often questioned. But he will be punished for not being careful in his simplicity. 

Therefore, every human being must get rid of the thoughts that are the root of sin. We should immediately correct ourselves by calling on the name of God and condemning Satan as it flashes in our mind. Therefore, when the thought of sin comes to our heart, if we immediately repent in our conscience and return to our mind, that is, without entertaining the thought, without saying it in words and without putting into action, then if we go to the priest and receive his blessings, kiss his cross, our sins will be forgiven. This is through the  authority given to the priest from God; saying  "Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven" Mat 18.18

Therefore, even if the thought of sin comes to our mind, if we don't think about it again and again, if we don't say it in words, if we don't put it into action, it will be forgiven by the blessings of the priest. Therefore, even though it is good to try not to forget this type of sin by saying that you will repent in the future, but in another way, keeping the sin in our mind and thinking about it again and again may create an opportunity for it to grow to the next level of sin. Therefore, the best way is to pray the priest's cross, go to church and pray, and remove this idea of sin from our hearts every day and stop thinking about it. Sin should not be something that we hoard like money, but something that we should get rid of regularly like garbage. This does not mean that we have to go and confess to our Father every day for the sin that we mentioned above as the sin of thought, but it is forgiven by the blessings of the priest's cross as explained above. Maybe if we are in an area where there is no priest and no church, we can talk to the priest by phone. And if this cannot be done, God knows our inner problems; Lord, forgive us, remove this thought from me, we pray in faith and believe that it has been done for us. 

However, it is important to understand that this kind of approach or receiving blessings from the priest does not free us from sins that we have committed by speech or by action. Also, as stated above, if we intend to do it and end up not because of inconvinient circumstances, it is considered that we have committed the sin of thought. Hence we need to repent for it. In general, if we reptedly think it in our mind, or if we speak it out, or if we get it into action, we need to  repent and confess and fulfill the canon given to us properly. At that time, all the damage we have done earlier knowingly and boldly, or unknowingly by mistake, will be forgiven all together.

Question #1: I have a lot of problems in my marriage. My marriage was done in church, in the Holy Communion! What do you recommend??

👉 Question #2:- I could not be a good wife. When I fight with my husband, I insult him, and want to strangle him very bad. What do you advise me?

✍Answer

text: : Our dear member, basically, our church teaches that any Christian should not be separated from the Holy Body and the Precious Blood from the time they receive the sonship of God through Baptism and are sealed with the Holy Communion on the 40th or 80th day of their life until the end. Along with this,

text.text: the Church emphasizes that it is a Christian obligation to marry in the Holy Communion.

Because what makes our marriage real is if we are married in the sacrament. As it is written, "the two shall become one flesh" during the sacred marriage ceremony, the great mystery of which the two bodies are transformed into physical unity and spiritual unity though Christ's Holy Body and His Precious Blood. (Mark 10:8). Apart from this, if it is a worldly marriage, this mystery will not be fulfilled in which the two become one. In short, this pair cannot be called two but one.

text:
Of course, when we think the fact that many believers are getting married in the secular system like the Gentiles, we appreicate your  appropriate Christian behavior to decide to perform your marriage in the Holy Communion; grace and blessings will be abundant for you. No matter how many lies and illegalities abound, those have never replaced a single truth; God's law never changes. Therefore, we recommend that people who are married in a worldly system without knowing this truth and God's law, should repent and be united in the sacrament so that their marriage can be called a true marriage. The reason we want to explain all this in our introduction is to create awareness for other members as well  based on the idea that our questioner's  raised  about getting married in Holy Communion.

Dear member, in your question, it seems that you have lost hope and already concluded the problem your marriage encountered cannot be solved at all. But you didn't specificaly mention to us what the problem is. Identifying the problem correctly is getting half of the solution so it would have been very useful if you specified. 

Hence, in response to your question, even if you have not mentioned the challenges you faced, we hereby explained to you a general way and perspective of how to manage your marriage with spiritual wisdom, so we entrust you to implement our advice:

text.text: There are two things that make a spiritual marriage strong. One is to be united in religion (live in religion) and the other is to be united in purity (righteousness)
The lack thereof is what destroys marriages.

text: In other words, marriage is a partnership in which the spouses agree that there is nothing that can separate them apart from death, adultery, and changing their religion. Therefore, if marriage is a place where people enter and do not leave, then we should be careful and aware enough to enter into it not blindly but with knowledge.

text.text: Therefore, it is important to learn about the nature of marriage before marriage. A house can support its roof only when its foundation is strong, and marriage requires preparation not only for temporary feelings and happiness, but also for challenges that may be faced in the long run.

text:
Indeed, some marriages bring blessings to husband and wife, children, and others. And some marriages don't come with this. What is the difference? The main difference between these marriages is the purpose of the marriage. If they get married for material things, or to satisfy their lust, or any other similar worldly view, the marriage will not bring blessings. Those who get married with the goal of righteousness and to travel with the spiritual goal of attaining salvation and eternal life, their marriage brings great happiness and blessing not only to the couple, but also to their children and other people.   

(to be continued)👇

text.text: St. John the Baptist taught us, this is why God instituted marriage - for those who cannot lead a monastic life, to live in marriage with the goal of righteousness!!!
Therefore, disagreements in Orthodox marriage can be compared to the Cross of Christ which we are called to carry.

text: Marriage requires not only happiness but also a willingness to bear these crosses. Therefore, some of the disagreements between the couple come from losing the orthodox path, forgetting the vision (purpose) of orthodox marriage, and not remembering that there is salvation, healing, justification, and blessing in the middle of the struggle. Therefore, the challenges we face in marriage can be overcome with wisdom and love. The important thing is that even if our spouse does not do what is expected of us, we should look at what is expected of ourselves in terms of the purpose of marriage.

text.text: Marriage is not a worldly life of competition or abandonment, but the purpose of being justified by walking together and supporting each other.

text:
For this is either marriage in Christ or spiritual marriage. The martyrs entered the kingdom of heaven because they were killed by the sword and shed their blood for the sake of their religion, so we who are asked for a lesser price than this, should see our marriage as a good way of salvation and justification, and we deserve to fulfill our duty to live in love.

Even if there is a problem that is beyond our control, we should discuss how to cope, how to correct this mistake and solve the problem by talking openly, but we should not enter into inappropriate satanic thinking, hatred and revenge. Even God, who is pure by nature, did not want to destroy us after seeing all this dirty work of ours.

text.text: Therefore, at any time, anywhere, any situation witout condition, since we the marriage promise we made is for our common purpose, we should mainly live with complete sympathy, love and forgiveness for our spouse.

text:
Even if there is a problem that is beyond our control, we should go as far as possible and solve the problem by talking openly about the way to correct our mistake in order to overcome it with the spirit of patience, forgiveness and tolerance. There is no one who can do my pre than we can to save our marriage, our children, and our future lives, so we ourselves, individually and collectively, must be ready to pay any price.

Therefore, we need to talk openly about the challenges and disagreements we may face in our marriage and how we can overcome them.

text.text: Marriage is where we learn about love, where we live love, where we understand the love of Christ. Christ the Bridegroom loves the Church with a selfless and unconditional love. When we show this love in practice, we wash away our sins with that love (1 John 4:12). This is why we call marriage a journey of righteousness.

text: The Church is Christ's body and bridegroom, and the wife is her husband's body and bridegroom. messages.full_text:
(continued part)👆👇

St. John the Baptist taught us, this is why God instituted marriage - for those who cannot lead a monastic life, to live in marriage with the goal of righteousness!!!

Therefore, disagreements in Orthodox marriage can be compared to the Cross of Christ which we are called to carry.  Marriage requires not only happiness but also a willingness to bear these crosses. Therefore, some of the disagreements between the couple come from losing the orthodox path, forgetting the vision (purpose) of orthodox marriage, and not remembering that there is salvation, healing, justification, and blessing in the middle of the struggle. Therefore, the challenges we face in marriage can be overcome with wisdom and love. The important thing is that even if our spouse does not do what is expected of us, we should look at what is expected of ourselves in terms of the purpose of marriage. Marriage is not a worldly life of competition or abandonment, but the purpose of being justified by walking together and supporting each other. For this is either marriage in Christ or spiritual marriage. The martyrs entered the kingdom of heaven because they were killed by the sword and shed their blood for the sake of their religion, so we who are asked for a lesser price than this, should see our marriage as a good way of salvation and justification, and we deserve to fulfill our duty to live in love.

Even if there is a problem that is beyond our control, we should discuss how to cope, how to correct this mistake and solve the problem by talking openly, but we should not enter into inappropriate satanic thinking, hatred and revenge. Even God, who is pure by nature, did not want to destroy us after seeing all this dirty work of ours. Therefore, at any time, anywhere, any situation witout condition, since we the marriage promise we made is for our common purpose, we should mainly live with complete sympathy, love and forgiveness for our spouse. Even if there is a problem that is beyond our control, we should go as far as possible and solve the problem by talking openly about the way to correct our mistake in order to overcome it with the spirit of patience, forgiveness and tolerance. There is no one who can do my pre than we can to save our marriage, our children, and our future lives, so we ourselves, individually and collectively, must be ready to pay any price.

Therefore, we need to talk openly about the challenges and disagreements we may face in our marriage and how we can overcome them. Marriage is where we learn about love, where we live love, where we understand the love of Christ. Christ the Bridegroom loves the Church with a selfless and unconditional love. The love in marriage is the key to this perfect love as St. Gregory the Great tells us. "If we love one another, God will live in us, and his love is perfected in us." When we show this love in practice, we wash away our sins with that love (1 John 4:12). This is why we call marriage a journey of righteousness.

The Church is Christ's body and bridegroom, and the wife is her husband's body and bridegroom. In order for the body to function in a healthy manner, unless the feet or hands are sick, it works without disobedience. This is the body's system (nature). A wife is equal to her husband and they are one body. Therefore, she should submit to her husband as she submits to the Lord for their common health. (Eph 5:22) This is the Christian order (nature). One of the things that make a family not run properly is to confuse this transience (nature). We should remember that when a wife obeys her husband, she is participating in our Lord's work of salvation, not the obedience of a master and a slave. A wife obeying her husband does not mean that her husband is perfect. The only perfect bridegroom (husband) is our Lord Jesus Christ!
 
(to be continued)👇

text:
(continued part)👆👇

Therefore, no matter how weak a husband is, you should not despise him. If you want to correct his weakness, as St. Peter advised us, "Wives, if some of your husbands are disobedient to teaching, submit to them so that they may find instruction in the lives of their wives, watching your chaste lives with fear" (1 Peter 3:1).

The fathers say, "May God throw all the anger, the quarrels, the sickness, the spirit of hatred into the sea and into the cliff." We should learn from the Bible, from history and from other people we know or heared that there is no  justification for a fight, no justification for divorce. In general, marriage is martyrdom, and our ancestors achieved martyrdom through many hardships, but our martyrdom is mainly to live patiently with the marriage we started.

Therefore, our dear member, we have briefly explained the spirituality of marriage above in this lesson, we believe that if you understand this properly, you will have learned the wisdom of caring instead of fighting, being one instead of being separated, loving instead of revenge and resentment, loving instead of hating, being justified instead of being lost.

We give you this as a general understanding and advice and we will give you advice based on the rest when you identify the problem you are facing and let us know. So contact us soon before Satan escalates the problem and turns your life into a chaos.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always. 

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

text.text: It is Christ who founded the Church

Dear and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on the John's Repentance website; This lesson prepared based on the topic is found in the book 'Hebr Serat Zebetristian Orthodox', and we have translated the lesson and made it available to you by referring to the recent challenges the Church has faced: We entrust you all to read it and gain a comprehensive understanding of the connection between the Church and religion.
1. It is Christ who founded the church

text:
Christ founded the church on Peter's religion. Peter's religion is to believe that Christ is God, the Son of God, the Alpha and Omega, who prophesied in the past through the prophets, and who fulfilled the prophecies that God spoke by becoming a man, who is one body from two bodies, one nature from two natures, God. . In order to understand that this religion was Peter's, when the Lord asked the Council of Caesarea, "Who do people call the Son of Man?", the other disciples said what they had heard from people, that they call you Elijah, John the Baptist, one of the prophets, but the question did not end there, because the Lord answered, "Who do you say that I am?" St. Peter replied, "You are the Christ, the Son of the Living God." Matthew 16:16 John 1:41

And another time, when the Lord was teaching about the sacrament, many of the people were going back saying, "This is troubling, who can hear it?" When the Lord asked the apostles, "Would you like to go too?" Saint Peter replied, "Lord. To whom shall we go when you have the promise of eternal life? "We believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God," he testified to his religion and that of his companions. John 6:80-89

In his message, when Saint Peter himself spoke about Christ's death, he said, "He died in the flesh, but he is alive in the spirit (divinity)." 1 Pet 3:19 This is what Peter's religion means. Whoever does not believe in this religion is different from the unity of the church, which is the family of the members of the body of Christ, and is not called a follower of Peter.  Therefore, the orthodox church was founded, stood firmly, and will continue forward, holding this creed of the great apostle St. Peter as its foundation. Rtu Hai page 34

John the Evangelist said this in his message, "Who is a liar but he that denies that Jesus is the Christ?" 1st John 2:22 "Whosoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loves him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. He said. 1 John 5:1 Therefore, a person is called a Christian when he knows the teaching of the apostles and understands their religion well, accepts it and follows it. Apart from this, a religion made arbitrarily, by chance, by one's will, by one's own philosophy and guidance does not save from judgment. 

What explains that Peter's religion is correct: The Lord heard Peter's words and did not keep silent. "And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven." Matthew 16:16-17. Therefore, Peter's foundation is religion. The religion is "Only son" (The pre-world, born of a father without a mother, the after-world, born of the Virgin Mary without a father, Jesus Christ is an only child.). It is a part of the church of Christ that stands and grows on the rock of Peter. Peter's foundation is belief, and Christ's foundation is trust: "For it has been declared unto me of you, my brethren, by them which are of the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you." 11). 1st Qor 1፥11

(continues)👇

text:

The church is said to be founded and sustained by the prophecies of the prophets, the sermons of the apostles, the teachings of the scholars, the wisdom of the martyrs, the prayers of the righteous saints, and the hard work of the devotees day and night. "Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God;" Eph 2:19-20. When we say that Christ founded the church, we mean that he is the one who was pierced by a spear and poured the holy water from his right side, crucified on the cross, raised it with his broken flesh and shed blood, and he is its origin and its destination.

This means: The first Adam produced Eve who brought death from his side, and the second Adam produced from his side the holy water on which the life-giving church was founded. For the head is above all the bodies and is the gathering place of all the bodies, and Christ as the head of the church is the home of all believers. "For we are members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones." Eph 5:30 - "The tree was first of all, all things were established by him, he is the head of the church, the first tree was raised from the dead to be the head of all" Col 1:17 Eph 1:21, Eph 5:23

text.text: 2. Be careful ye who build on this foundation

text:
Christ founded the church and did not leave it. He has chosen and appointed seven apostles who will lead and manage the church and teach about Him. "And he gave grace, and appointed apostles from the churches, and from them prophets and evangelists, guardians and teachers, so that the saints may be steadfast in the work of the ministry and the building up of the body of Christ" Ephesians 4:11 1 Corinthians 12:27

text:
Fast of Nineveh is three days subsequent fast and repentance of the Ninevites by the warning message of the Prophet Jonah. It is known to be the fast of repentance, humility and the return to God. Thus, the Church considers this fast amongst the Great Fast; Lent and other Fasts.

The people of Nineveh fasted, wore sackcloth from the youngest to the oldest and prayed to God for forgiveness. God accepted their repentance; “God saw their works that they turned from their evil way; and God relented from the disaster that He had said He would bring upon them; and He did not do it.” (Jonah 3:10)

The story of Jonah presages the redemptive work of Lord Jesus Christ. God send Prophet Jonah to the people of Nineveh for they were Gentiles and needed repentance. “But in every nation whoever fears Him and works righteousness is accepted by Him.” (Acts 10:35)

God saved the mariners on the boat who were Gentiles through Jonah for they were men seeking the Lord. Tough, they prayed to their gods they knew the true God is the almighty. So, they asked Jonah to pray to his God. Prophet Jonah also told the mariners, “I am a servant of the Lord, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.” Believing his words, they feared the Lord and offered Him sacrifices. (Jonah 1:16, 1:9-10)

Then, even after he told them to throw him in the sea; “They were endeavoring to find God’s will in order that they might carry it out. When the sea ceased its raging by their throwing Jonah into it they were assured of the presence of God in the matter. They believed in the Lord, offered Him a sacrifice and made vows. In their belief in the Lord they not only believed that He was God but by offering Him a sacrifice they professed their belief in the propitiation of blood.” (Jonah 1:13)

However, it was not the will of God for Jonah to drawn, so He prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah and uses the whale to save him. Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights praying to God. At the third day, God answered his prayers and the whale put Jonah put out on dry Land; He did not prepare it to destroy him but to preserve him.

God command Prophet Jonah again to go to Nineveh. He was first commanded to preach the Ninevites although his prophecy did not reach upon them till after the whale had emitted him out.

God saves Jonah from his pride as he was still egocentric when He caused a plant with thick leaves to grow up and shade Jonah from the sun and GOD destroyed the plant with worm. The next day, he suffered from the heat of a wind blow. Once more, with rage, Prophet Jonah wished his death and God reveals his mercy and compassion through the plant.

Prophet Jonah was preaching God’s words to spread His kingdom in Nineveh City and God willed to save Ninevites. “A greater than Jonah is here” Jonah was a figure of Lord Christ. Saint Cyril of Jerusalem says, “As Jonah was thrown to the belly of the whale, the Lord Christ went by His own will to the unseen whale of death, to coerce him to give those who were swallowed by him; as it is written, “I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death.” (Matthew 12:41, Hosea 13:14)

The Ninevites were saved by the Prophet Jonah. Saint John Chrysostom said, “Nineveh freed itself from death by fasting. Like a heavenly power overseeing Nineveh’s charge, fasting snatched the city from the gates of death and returned Nineveh to Life."

text.text: Dear members of John's Repentance page; We have sent you the following educational message regarding the tears of repentance so we entrust you to read and take it to heart as you fast, pray and suppoicate God to send his mercy upon us.

text:
There is a legend that has been told since ancient times. The Almighty God said to the angels, "Go to the earth and bring the most precious things that you find on earth." One of the angels brought a drop of blood that a man had shed to save another man. The Most High God said, "O angel; This that you have brought is glorious in my sight. However, it is not the most glorious one. Another angel came from a patient who died of an infectious disease and a nurse who died from the disease and brought her last breath. The Most High God said, "O angel; This that you have brought is glorious in my sight. However, it is not the most glorious one. Finally, another angel brought the tears of a sinner who had repented in a small cup before God. And God said to the angel, "O angel; "You have brought to me the most noble thing in the world," he replied. (Philokalia: the Bible of Orthodox Spirituality p.159)

The way for a person to return to God after he has sinned is through tears of repentance. The psalmist, Saint David, often tells us about the blessed pearl of the Holy Spirit. Let's notice what he said, "I wash my bed all night long, and I wipe my bed with my tears." He said this because his repentance is through the grace and mercy of the Holy Spirit. For his repentance was not in vain like the repentance of Judas. Again, the psalmist tells us that "weeping will come in the evening, but in the morning there will be joy" (Ps 29 (30):5). This signifies the joy of the Holy Spirit given with tears. It is related to what the Lord said in the Gospel, "Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted" (Matthew 5:4). Tears give spiritual rest to the soul lost in sin, and cause it to gain insight and the revelation of mysteries. When the Holy Gospel talks about Saint Peter, it says, "He went outside and wept bitterly" (Luke 22:62). He received the great responsibility to feed and lead the believers after walking in tears

Our ancestors taught that tears are a gift from God to give birth to a new life. Baptism is one; If a person sins after baptism and is in the work of death, his return and "rebirth" is this tear of repentance. Through the tears of repentance, he renews the grace that he received in baptism, but which was later corrupted by sin.

St. John the Baptist said, "The fire of sin is steadfast." But a few drops of tears extinguishes the burning of mistakes (like fire) and purifies our souls. He teaches us this spiritual lesson. Because the tears of true repentance are a gift from God, it explains to us that no matter how bad a person's wrongdoing is, it has the power to destroy that serious sin. St. John said this to indicate that a person can do wrong because of his free will, and whether he does not use it, will be questioned at the time of judgment. We find this holy father often teaching about tears of repentance. One of his teachings where he explained that "tears are both the mother and child of prayer" is worth mentioning. Tears have a great place for a person's eternal life and the union of grace with God. It makes a person compassionate, pure, loving others, forgiving and humble. If he does this, he will live forever as his creator (God).

In general, all members; Thinking only of God's things, we should repent, be in a broken heart to fulfill our canon properly, and pray with tears; Similarly, if we come across other things that can mislead or distract us, we recommend that we need to stay away from them so that we don't fall into sin.

We will return in the next lesson about the obstacles to repentance, so stay tuned

Many people fall into this dilemma and are heard to say, "I don't even know what's bothering me." But most of the time, when we examine the root of our anxiety, we find it to be fear. And fear is a bully against those who do not have faith in God and the weak. In addition, the so-called sources of stress, such as sadness, panic, conflict and anger, are directly or indirectly the source and aggravating means of stress.

Therefore, if we are not able to calmly examine the cause of our anxiety and find a solution to the problem, it will deprive us of many good things and our inner peace. Therefore, it is important to identify the source of our anxiety. We should also distance ourselves from negative emotions. And we're told we can't make a difference by worrying. "Who can add a cubit to his stature by being worried about you?" (Matthew 6:27)

5. Mystery of Resurrection of (from) the dead

text:
Resurrection refers to the re-uniting of soul and body at the end of ages. It is the return of all the dead in to life at the end of the world. It marks the start of eternal ‘life’ after the second coming of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. Resurrection also denotes the final removal of the consequences of Adam’s sin (human disobedience). This mystery represents all what is at stake in our spiritual journey on earth. We believe in the authentic apostolic Gospel to be genuine candidates of the Kingdom of God, which would be revealed at the end of the ages. We take part in sacramental rituals implementing two among the five pillars of mysteries (Mystery of Baptism and Mystery of Holy Eucharist) for the same reason. The essence of Christianity is the life we have after death. We don’t dare to sacrifice our everlasting life in heaven for “a moment of happiness” on earth which transgresses God’s commandments. We believe and proclaim that all the dead humans will rise up for glory or demise. We believe the way we do and perform good deeds to be genuine candidates of God’s grace for a glorious resurrection.

So, when a person dies, he faces two opportunities of places where he lives with soul, and we decide one of the two when we are still alive before we die. This means that if we do righteous deeds, we will go to paradise. If we sin, we go to hell. So first, until the second coming, if a person is a sinner, his soul will go to hell, and if his deeds are good, he will go to paradise. After the second coming, the soul of the righteous will be sent to the kingdom of heaven, and the soul of the sinner will be sent to the fire of hell.

The second coming of Jesus Christ will be as lightning as it’s said: “For as lightning that comes from the east is visible even in the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.” (Matthew 24:27). He will be seen with great power and authority: “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky, with power and great glory” (Matthew 24:30-31). “For the Son of Man is going to come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he will reward each person according to what he has done” ((Matthew 16:27 Luke 17:28-30 Luke 21:34-36 Matthew 25:1-12 Luke 12:37-38 John 14:1-3 Luke 12:40 Mark 8:38).

The lord said “For as the lightening cometh out of the east, and shines even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” (Mathew 24:27) Church scholars rightly note that the moment of our physical death on earth, even before judgement day, is our “final day”. We don’t have the chance to have the faith and deeds for salvation after departure. Hence, our final day is our judgement day and there is no point to speculate about the “final day of the world” while our final day comes without being noticed.

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was crucified and died to save the human race in order to bring us back to our original inheritance in heaven.  Paradise is a place of temporary happiness where the righteous will stay.

(Part 12 Continues)👇

👉🏾👉🏾👉🏾 About #Betrothal

Dear and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on the John's Repentance website; Based on the title mentioned in above, we have sent you the following important lesson, so we entrust you to read and learn from it.

Betrothal/Engagement:- means choosing, preparing. Betrothal is a time of togetherness between the two couples before marriage, and it is a time of hope leading to marriage.

Engagement

Engagement is a journey of purpose, courtship, and preparation that you embark on together for a successful marriage life. This is a way for us to start with consent; and wait for the holy marriage and the blessings it will bring us to a great chapter of responsibility. Thus, since betrothal is not a permanent relationship or marriage, matters that happen after marriage should not be done during betrothal. Instead, it is a time to gather our scattered conscience and help each other with a holy purpose.

Things To Do during Engagement

- Religious Unity: Since religion is the primary issue in the life of a Christian betrothed; and most importantly, since marriage is a journey to salvation, religious unity should be the main selection criterion.

- Staying Virgin - Betrothal with virginity and virginity with betrothal have an inseparable basic combination. The Orthodox Church emphatically teaches that both men and women have a Christian responsibility to maintain chastity until the day of their marriage, and in other word, it is a sin to lose virginity before marriage.

- Pray - Praying and asking for God's will to be worthy of holy marriage

- Not extending the engagement period - Unless there is a special reason, it is preferable that it is not less than six months and not more than two years.

   - Getting married in the church system : agreeing to perform their marriage in the church system based on one intention and purpose; Apart from this, if both or one of them are not on the same path, having different thoughts and objectives, their destination will be different. Besides, marriage is not a way of abandoning, but a path of righteousness where you walk together with each other and support each other. Moreover , the covenant of marriage is said to be valid when its basis is confirmed by the sacraments in the true Church order. it is the secret of coming to unity from duality.
