text.text:
What is the Holy Communion? 
What is the origin and system of the Holy Communion? 
Why is the sacrament called a mystery? 
Who is worthy of the Holy Communion? 
What preparation do we do before and after receiving the Holy Communion?

text:
The sacrament of Holy Communion is one of the seven sacraments of the Orthodox Church. The term "Qurban" is an Arabic word meaning "blessing," "gift of money, knowledge, labor and time." In the Old Testament, the blood of animals offered by the Israelites for their sins and for the glory of God was called a sacrifice.

In the New Testament, communion or sacrifice means the faithful (true) sacrifice that God offered as an offering to reconcile Himself with mankind. This offering is Jesus Christ, the Lamb of God. Thus, the sacrament means the perfect Body and Blood of our God, Jesus Christ, our Savior.

It was Jesus Christ who founded the sacrament of Holy Communion on the eve of the crucifixion on Thursday. Only his twelve disciples were with him when he established this great sacrement and mystery. He did not reveal it to all the people who were following him like he did with other sacrements. This is why the Holy Church shroudes it in veil and honor as she offers it to the faithful. 

The Holy Communion is called a mystery because of the transformation of bread into the flesh of God and wine into the blood of God, which is visible only to believers with the eyes of faith. The priests prepare the bread only from pure wheat and prepare the wine only from pure grapes or raisins. When the priest blesses the bread and wine by saying, "Aækote Barëkë Wokëdësë," the authority of the priest, the word of God, and the action of the Holy Spirit transform the bread and wine into the flesh and blood of God, making it a mystery that is hidden from the unbeliever.

Before receiving the Holy Communion, one must believe without doubt in the change of the bread and wine into the flesh and blood of God, which is necessary for the healing of the stain and wound of sin and the source of eternal life. One must also repent from past sins, confess, return, and guard against future sins. There is no age limit for receiving Holy Communion, and one should not stay away from the Holy Communion until the end of one's life.

After receiving the Holy Communion, one should take precautions, such as refraining from eating or drinking for a certain period, and contemplating on the spiritual benefit received from the sacrament. The Holy Communion is a great mystery and is the sacrament that is central to the Orthodox Church's teachings.

(Continues) 👇

text:
(Continued) 👆

If those who receive the sacrament are married, they should abstain from meat for three days before receiving communion. This is not because sexual relationship is a sin or unclean but because it is a work of the flesh. We do this out of reverence for the Eucharist. 

One should confesses a known sin and say, "Forgive me for any unknown sins," and cleanse their heart of revenge and keep their body away from wrongdoing.

In order to receive Holy Communion, one should fast for 18 hours without food or water, and wait until the food is removed from the stomach.
If a person has a nocturnal emission the night of, they should not receive communion on that day.

On the eve, one should take a bath and prepare clean clothes.

It is necessary to get to church before the services start. A person who comes in the middle of the Liturgy and has not properly consecrated themselves should not receive communion.

A woman should not receive communion during her menstrual period for up to seven days. Afterward, she should wash herself and receive communion. As she gets close to giving birth, she should not receive communion until the child is born and christened. She should wait until she has gains back her energy before she continues taking part of the Eucharist.

text.text: About how our Lord and Savior

"To destroy the works of the devil, the Son of God has been revealed" (1 John 3:8).

Dear children of God, we appreciate you very much when we see that you are following the teachings and spiritual advice that we always convey on John's Repentance page. As God has entrusted us to serve we entrust you to read and friends and family.

text: Something new and wonderful happened in earth 5500 years after creation. It was a miracle that has never happened before, an abstract secret that is impossible for a creature but possible for a creator: the secret of Christ's birth from his mother, the Holy Virgin Mary, who gave Him flesh and became a man. Even though it was prophesied that He would come down from heaven and be born of Mary, it was a marvel that He was born from her body, her soul, and her flesh.

The apostle St. Paul wrote, "In the past God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets at many times and in various ways, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, and through whom also he made the universe" (Hebrews 1:1-2).

The apostle St. Paul said, "When the end of the age came, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law" (Galatians 4:4).

Christ's main purpose and reason for coming to earth in the flesh was to live forever in glory as the first physical word of His character. He experienced hunger, thirst, weariness, death, illness, and everything that human beings go through. This was necessary to make Him compatible with Adam's nature (1 John 3:8) so that He could destroy the works of the devil.

What is the work of the devil? The devil's work is to commit sin. Betrayal, arrogance, and falsehood are some examples of sins that the devil committed.

The devil, who had the position of leadership in the world of angels, arose an evil desire and sought the authority of the Creator, denying the Creatorship of God, even denying himself, and sowing the weeds of betrayal. The devil, filled with the rebellion of apostasy in his evil mind, sowed the weeds of apostasy on the hearts of Adam's children. (Mathew 13:25) But Christ removed Adam and his children from the sin of apostasy that the devil brought into the world, destroyed the tares that the devil had sown in the wheat field, and removed them from the hearts of mankind. (Ezekiel 36:25-32)

"However, false prophets were also among the people, and they will be false teachers among you, and they will deny even the Lord who redeemed them, and many will follow them in their own ways, and the path of truth will be insulted by them." (2 Peter 1:1:2) 

"For certain individuals whose condemnation was written about long ago have secretly slipped in among you. They are ungodly people, who pervert the grace of our God into a license for immorality and deny Jesus Christ our only Sovereign and Lord." (Jude 1:4) 

"He says, 'They deny religion, they are numb, as if they are burning in their own conscience'" (1 Timothy 4:2) which describes the devil's work of treason and explains his evil deeds.

(Continued) 👇🏾

Pride is a behavior that originated from the devil himself. It is a devilish trait (1 Timothy 3:6). The devil, motivated by his pride, caused a division among the angels. The prophet Isaiah speaks of this pride leading to failure: "How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! You have been cast down to the earth" (Isaiah 14:12).

However, our Lord has humbled us and destroyed the pride that the devil raised in our hearts. He, being the Most High God, humbled Himself and lived a sinless human life. He washed the feet of His disciples, demonstrating the wisdom that overcomes pride, which is the work of the devil (John 13:4-17). In His teachings, He exhorted us to learn from His example of meekness and lowliness of heart, assuring us that we will find rest for our souls (Matthew 11:29).

Falsehood is also a trait that originated from the devil himself, and he is called the father of lies (John 8:44). His aim is to twist what is good and make it evil, what is sweet and make it bitter, and to pretend that lies are truth. He misled our first parents, Adam and Eve, with his lies (Genesis 3:4-5).

But the truth of our Lord Jesus Christ has shattered the false world that the devil created (John 14:16, 1 John 2:21, John 18:37).

When Adam and his children were first created, they didn't know about death. However, the devil was envious of them, having lost his own paradise through pride and betrayal. He wanted to cause their downfall as well, so he taught Cain to kill Abel (Gen 4).

Murder began with Cain, and all the children of Adam have lived with the stain of bloodshed. However, Christ teaches us to lay down our lives for one another and to forgive those who do evil (Luke 23:34).

Question፦ To begin, if a person is married, must they constantly attend Holy Communion with their spouse?  Because my mother really wants to partake in holy communion and has already confessed her sins when we went to Ethiopia and she did timket, but my father doesn't go to church and only follows church services from home, is it possible for my mother to take Kurban without my father or do they have to do it together because she really wants to partake in holy communion (they are married)?  

Answer፦

text:
The question is regarding a husband and wife who are living together but are not united in their spiritual life. One of them wants to partake of Holy Communion but the other is not attending church regularly.

The first issue is that the penance fathers have not provided adequate guidance and discipline to the couple to help them walk together in their spiritual journey. This is a problem that affects many faithful believers and is a failure on the part of the penance fathers. They should show the right path and teach the way so that people can live by the teachings of the Church.  

Secondly, couples must start their marriage with a focus on their spiritual life rather than solely on material wealth and property. They should not be driven by materialistic desires, but rather by their faith. Even if they give tithes or attend church, it should not be out of obligation but rather out of love for God. It is important to seek God's kingdom and righteousness first, and all other things will be added.

Regarding the question of whether the wife can receive Holy Communion alone, the answer is no. As long as they are living together and sharing a bed, one cannot receive Holy Communion alone. If the man is not able to adjust his position and come back to the faith, and if they have exhausted all efforts to reconcile, the woman may choose to separate and receive Holy Communion alone. However, it is important to try to keep the couple together and give them advice so that they can be together until the end.

The couple should seek guidance from elders and penance fathers to avoid any unwanted issues in their relationship that may lead to separation. The father is not going to church because he lacks a Christian education but not because he hates salvation, so it is important to involve responsible fathers in this process so they can pull him into the church using the wisdom that has been given to them. 

In conclusion, it is important to prioritize one's spiritual life and seek guidance from penance fathers to walk together with one's spouse. Holy Communion entails unity in flesh and should only be received together as a couple.

Question፦ Hello, I was wondering if it's okay to wear other kinds of cross necklaces (gold, silverm etc) or does it have to be the type that is shaped in wood? If so, I was wondering what the meaning is. Thank you!

Answer፦

text:
The cross is a special symbol for the Orthodox Church members and indicates our unity in faith. 

As our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ said, "If anyone loves me, he will carry the cross and follow me." The cross represents the martyrdom of suffering in the Christian life, the spiritual activities we do, and the good deeds that we do voluntarily. It reminds us that there are many trials we must face.

Thirdly, the cross is our power, symbolizing the source of all life. It is the symbol from which we overcome all demons and rise to victory over all our subtle spiritual enemies.

Therefore, it is important to consider which type of cross wear. We know that the cross on which our Lord Jesus Christ was crucified was made of wood. The Ethiopian Orthodox Church, uses wood, bronze and gold and other metals to make a cross which is prepared according to our canon.

Although gold, silver, and bronze are valuable, it would be impossible to make crosses out of these minerals for everyone to use because they are too expensive. The grace given by God through the cross is not valued by money. The cross has a subtle grace and power from God that cannot be bought. Therefore, we should bind the cross to be a symbol of our religion, whatever it may be made from, so that we can be protected from the power of demons.

The bronze cross is similar to the altar tool used in the Old Testament sacrifices, while the silver and gold crosses are symbols of God's grace. The gold cross represents the purity, novelty and previousness of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. 

In summary, the Orthodox Church uses wooden, bronze, silver, and gold crosses in service. Each material has its own significance, and we can understand their meaning through comparison with the prophecy in Daniel chapter 2. The great image that King Nebuchadnezzar saw had a head of fine gold, chest and arms of silver, belly and loins of bronze, and thighs of iron.

Just as the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the earth completely, the cross is a powerful symbol that reminds us of God's grace, protection, and victory over our enemies. We should therefore cherish and respect the cross as a manifestation of good things and as a protection against evil.

All of these elements have their own secrets of manifestation.

Nebuchadnezzar saw the vision because God intended to reveal something to him but he couldn't understand it. The prophet Daniel, a man of God, was able to interpret this mystery and reveal it. This was in contrast to the sorcerers and soothsayers who were far from God's help.

Thus, when God revealed the vision to Nebuchadnezzar, there was a wide commentary on what each element represented, such as gold, silver, clay, bronze, and iron. Since we are allowed to use them all for good, it means that we can use the cross made of gold, bronze, silver, and wood, among other materials.

(Continues)👇🏾

text.text:
Question፦ What preparation is needed for repentance? What do we say when we repent?? What should we do after we repent?

Answer፦

text:
The concept of repentance in the Orthodox Church is a fundamental question that requires careful consideration. Before embarking on the process of repentance, one must first ask oneself why they wish to repent. The reasons for repentance must be thoroughly understood, including an awareness of one's sinful nature, the need for repentance, and what one has lost by sinning. Repentance is necessary because we are all sinners, and only those who are sick need to be healed, not the healthy.

Therefore, it is important to understand the meaning of sin before repentance. Sin signifies a loss, separation, and avoidance. We lose blessings, peace, help, love, and the ability to live with God. Sin also causes deprivation and separation from holy places, prayer, blessings, and all good things.

To illustrate this point, we can examine the example of the devil, who was not initially created as an evil being. He was created as the chief of the holy angels and was close to God. However, he attempted to use his creative talents for his own benefit and was consequently cast out from the presence of God. He lost his sanctity, just as Adam was separated from God and lost his holiness, peace, and blessings. Therefore, before repenting, one must understand the severity and essence of sin and repent to regain what was lost.

When we repent, the first step is to acknowledge that we are sinners. This involves listing all of our sins, from actions to thoughts, without concealing anything. It is crucial to recognize that hiding our sins is akin to being a secret friend of the evil spirit. On the other hand, confessing our sins is living with God. We must confess to both our repentant father and to God himself. It is vital to understand that the choice to live or die is ours.

Finally, we must have the willingness to repent. Living in sin is not living. It is essential to realize that it is not right and to repent of our sinful ways. It is not challenging to turn back when we understand that the path we are on is wrong. We must hate and abhor sin and understand that it is more poisonous than poison itself. Only then can we avoid it and genuinely repent.

Moreover, repentance is a vital process that requires understanding and willingness. By acknowledging our sins, we can regain what we have lost and live with God.

(Continues)👇🏾

Additionally, when we repent, we should not make excuses, such as blaming Satan or others. We should accept responsibility for our actions and believe that God is merciful and forgiving.

In regards to how we should confess, we should write down our sins so we don't forget anything during confession. We should not sugarcoat our sins in anyway but rather say them as they are, admitting guilt and responsibility. We should confess our sins in detail and not make superficial statements like 'I lied'. What was the lie? Why did you lie? To whom did you lie? What are the causes and effects of the lie? What are you doing to make sure this doesn't happen again? 

We can learn from the stories of those who have been forgiven, as well as follow the canons given to us by the priest. It is crucial to follow these canons precisely and accept the Holy Flesh and Precious Blood without any hindrance. After confessing and fulfilling the canons, there is nothing stopping us from receiving the Holy Body and Blood.

However, after repentance, we must stay away from sin and strive to listen to the word of God, seek advice from teachers, and sanctify ourselves. If we unintentionally fall into sin, we should rise up with repentance, and if we repeatedly fall, we must repent again and again. The journey towards God is long, and we should not separate ourselves from Him after repentance.

text.text: 👉🏾 Question from member: I often feel depressed and lonely. Life has no meaning to me, I just want to die and live with Jesus, I've been looking for happiness all my life but I can't find it, I feel like my mind is going to explode, please pray for me, I need prayer, what do you recommend?

text:
Why does a person choose loneliness? Why does a person hide? In essence, man is not happy without God, because there is no peace without God. Jesus Christ said in the Gospel of John, chapter 14, verse 27, "Peace I leave with you, and my peace I give you, the peace I give you is not as the world gives; do not let your hearts be troubled, do not be afraid."
 
The world kisses us today then bites tomorrow; gives today then takes away tomorrow. But God does not take away what He has given, no matter what, there is no peace without God. What is life? Life is the opposite of death, life is living. Life is God, it is written, "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life."
 
Therefore, if we believe in the Son, we live with Jesus who is the life. It is Jesus Christ who gave life when human beings could not live according to the commandment, it is Jesus Christ who enlightened the dark world. In fact, this Christmas (birth) season is called the light. And if it is said who is the light: it is Jesus Christ.

This world was dark before God the Son became a man. The world lived in darkness. It is called light because God became a man and enlightened the world by making us members of His body. Many people's lives are in darkness. Darkness is sin, darkness is betrayal, darkness is hatred, darkness is lack of love; On the other hand, light is Jesus Christ, light is life, light is religion, light is peace, light is help, blessing and love. Because it is our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ who gave us that, there is no life without Jesus Christ.
 
As the owner himself told us, John Gospel chapter 15 verse 5 said "without me you can do nothing", so without Jesus Christ nothing can be done. How can peace be found without Jesus Christ? How can you live? Absolutely not possible. When Judas betrayed Jesus Christ for 30 dollars he died because he was separated from Jesus Christ who is life. We remember that when the devil was once the archangel, when he forgot God and said, "I am the creator," and then failed and separated from God who is life.

Also, when Adam lived peacefully in paradise for seven years and did what he was told not to do, he lost peace from God who is life, and found it difficult to live. but then we remember that he found peace when he returned to God, when he reconciled with God, so there is no peace without God.
 
Our questioner said that they want to die and live with Jesus Christ. So, those of us who do not have peace on earth, those who have fallen into sin on earth, those who have not tried to repent to find Jesus Christ, how can we find peace if we die? What qualifies us for the kingdom of heaven is the work we have done on earth to live with Jesus Christ and enable us to live in heaven. If we die on earth covered in sin, without repentance, confession, and reconciliation with God, we will not be able to live with Jesus. Therefore, it means that we cannot live with our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ before we repent.

text:
St. George is a Christian saint who is widely known for his courage, steadfast faith, and unwavering devotion to God. He was born in 280 A.D. in the city of Capadocia, which was part of the Eastern Empire in Asia Minor. He came from a wealthy and noble Christian family and followed the usual career path of young nobleman by joining the Roman army.

St. George's ability and charm quickly brought him promotion within the army, and eventually, he was made a tribune or an officer in the Imperial Guard by the Emperor. According to one story, he was a friend of Constantine, another officer who later became the first Christian emperor. The legend says that St. George accompanied Constantine to Britain and visited some holy places, including Glastonbury and Caerleon. When he returned to Nicomedia, the capital of the Eastern Empire, he encountered the fierce storm of persecution against Christians.

Diocletian, the emperor at the time, issued a formal edict against Christians on February 23, 303 A.D., which was the feast of Termhlalia. The edict mandated that all churches should be leveled to the ground, all sacred books burned, all Christians who held any honorable rank were to be degraded and deprived of civil rights, and all Christians who were not officials were to be reduced to slavery.

Despite the persecution, St. George boldly stood up for his faith. He pushed his way through the market to read the proclamation in front of the awe-stricken crowd and then deliberately tore down the Imperial edict and threw it away. This act of defiance resulted in his arrest and subsequent encounter with Diocletian.

The Emperor tried to seduce St. George by promising him a higher position in the empire, but St. George remained steadfast in his faith. Diocletian then began to threaten him with unbearable tortures that he would inflict on him. St. George refused to renounce his faith, even in the face of torture, and eventually was imprisoned.

St. George's chastity and suffering are two prominent aspects of his story. Diocletian arranged for a very beautiful woman to spend the night with him in prison to try to debauch him. St. George, who could only look forward to heavenly joy, began to pray and within a short while managed to swing her heart to the Christian faith. She seriously began to inquire about salvation, and by morning she declared that she found her true Bridegroom, Jesus Christ. With great courage, she announced her Christianity to the Emperor and his men and joined the other saintly martyrs.

(Continues)👇🏾

👉Question: When the other three Eastern Orthodox churches have three liturgies, why do we have fourteen liturgies?

👉Answer: This is a matter of faith. We know that the liturgy is a very sacred and mysterious act, and these fourteen liturgies are named after the saints who have been entrusted with the secrets of the Holy Spirit. They participated in the composition of the liturgy, each contributing their own genius.

text:
The Ethiopian Orthodox Church has a unique liturgical tradition that includes fourteen different Anaphoras (the part of the Eucharistic Prayer in which the bread and wine are consecrated). These Anaphoras are attributed to different saints and church fathers who contributed to the development of the church's theology and liturgy.

The fourteen Anaphoras used in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church are: St. Basil, St. Gregory, St. Cyril, St. Dioscorus, St. John the Evangelist, St. James, St. Adai and Mari, St. Julius, St. Philoxenus, St. Peter, St. Matthew, St. Mark, St. Luke, and St. Menas. Each of these saints represents a unique theological perspective, and their contributions are recognized and celebrated in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church through the use of their respective Anaphoras.

The use of multiple Anaphoras in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church is based on the belief that each saint has a unique contribution to make to the understanding of the Eucharist. It is believed that the Holy Spirit inspired each of these saints to write their Anaphoras, and that each one offers a different perspective on the mystery of the Eucharist and its significance in the life of the church.

The Ethiopian Orthodox Church also recognizes the three Anaphoras used by other Eastern Orthodox churches, namely the Anaphoras of St. John Chrysostom, St. Basil, and the Presanctified Gifts. However, the church believes that the use of multiple Anaphoras allows for a deeper understanding of the Eucharist and a more complete expression of the church's theology.

The liturgy they composed was inspired by the Holy Spirit and met the required standards. It was not simply put together by a person or a committee who collected money and then released it. When we consider the mystical composition of our these liturgies, it is truly wonderful. There is no word of God that is not included or touched upon. Why should we limit ourselves to only three liturgies, as in the case of the other Eastern Orthodox churches? They have their own reasons for having only these three liturgies in their canon.

To finish,, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church has fourteen different Anaphoras that are used during Mass, each attributed to a different saint or church father who contributed to the development of the church's theology and liturgy. The use of multiple Anaphoras allows for a more complete expression of the church's theology and a deeper understanding of the mystery of the Eucharist.

text.text: in the Life of the Church

text:
Orthodoxy offers a very precise way in which to enter into communion with God. It is a way that must be learned, for simply "becoming Orthodox" will not lead the seeker into an inner life that will transform, and enlighten. Membership in the Church is simply not enough, for the Church is not about beautiful services, icons, or mystical theology. As a hospital for the soul, the Church is a place wherein we can receive healing for that which ails us. It is the place where we can be cured, and made whole.

Like the emergency room of a local hospital, a patient can't simply walk in, and expect to be healed. They have to submit themselves to examination by the ER staff, who will ask them to describe what is going on, where they are hurting, run tests, and, finally, prescribe the necessary medication that will bring about healing.

Within the hospital of the soul, that is the Church, her priests act in the same capacity as the ER personnel. They interview the patient (parishioner), and examine the heart to find the sickness, and recommend the cure. The priest becomes the therapeutic guide, recommending what the patient (seeker) can do in order to be made whole.

A prayer rule, the daily reading of the Holy Scriptures, frequent confession and reception of the Holy Mysteries, are all part of the Church's medicine that will bring about the cure. Just as the doctor will prescribe the proper dosage, after getting to know his patient, so too, does the priest prescribe that which will help his spiritual son or daughter.

The spiritual life is something that needs to be learned, perhaps more so now, than at any time in the history of our world. As godlessness increases, so do the obstacles to spiritual progress. The degradation of the whole of our society, and the depths of depravity that have become a normal part of our age, have made this a dangerous time. Going it alone spirituality can leave one vulnerable to spiritual delusion. We all need a trusted and experienced guide who can help us avoid the pitfalls of the pride and self-will that would lead us down to perdition.

Question: How can I overcome my anxiety? How can I find peace in the midst of life's trials?

Answer:

text:
Are we, as Orthodox Christians, meant to worry? Our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, told us not to worry, so why are we worried? When a person is separated from God, sin becomes their dwelling place. Sin and lack of understanding deprives us from peace and makes us anxious.

A person without God has no peace or sleep. In general, a person who is dwelling in sin loses everything, and is filled with anxiety. Therefore, we are told not to worry and to "Cast all your worries on God, for He cares for you" (1 Peter 5:7).

In the sixth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, it is written, "And why do you worry about clothes? See how the flowers of the field grow. They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his splendor was dressed like one of these. If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the fire, will He not much more clothe you—you of little faith? So do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’ For the pagans run after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them. But seek first His kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well" (Matthew 6:28-33).

This is why Orthodox Christians say "Our Father" in prayer, asking God to "have mercy on us as a father has compassion on his children" (Psalm 103:13). In addition, in Psalm 102, verse 1, it is written, "Praise the Lord, my soul; all my inmost being, praise His holy name. Praise the Lord, my soul, and forget not all His benefits—who forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the pit and crowns you with love and compassion, who satisfies your desires with good things so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s."

If God has mercy on us and can fulfill our desires, why should we worry? Worrying and thinking are different. We can think, dream, and plan without worrying. Worry is the result of despair, but we are people who have hope.

If we have everything we need with God, why should we give up? Our purpose is to do what we can with God and never give up hope. If we fall into sin, we repent, for "the one who conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy" (Proverbs 28:13). If we are reconciled to God through repentance, what we lost will be returned to us. Therefore, we should not give up but rather think it through.

Let us give all our worries to God, focus on what is expected of us, and leave the rest to Him. As the apostles said, "Cast all your anxiety on Him because He cares for you" (1 Peter 5:7). We need to understand that we are required to do this.

Knowing that anxiety is the result of sin and a sign of separation from God, the solution is to live with God, repent of our sins, listen to God, and let go of things that worry us.

Peace can be found in the midst of life's trials when we live with God. Jesus Christ is the Prince of Peace, and in John 14:27, He said, "Peace I leave with you".

Question: How to solve complex family problems? How to build a loving and Christ-centered family?
 
✍️Answer:

text:
- The first question we should ask ourselves is how did complexity arise? What is the source of this complexity, and answer these questions from the different stakeholders involved. When did it start, and how long did it last? Understanding these issues is crucial to finding a solution. As the saying goes, "knowing the problem is half the journey to the solution." Therefore, the first step in solving a problem is to understand it.

If there is complex problems in a family, this is often a sign of lack of Love in the family. Love is the foundation of everything, and if it is present in our families, everything else follows suit. As the book says, "Where there is love, there is no mistrust, hatred, or possession. Love is the root of all good."

Therefore, the complexity of our lives is due to the lack of love in our homes, neighborhoods, and surroundings. Saint Peter said, "With love, anything is possible, and with love, there is patience and meekness." The absence of love creates complex problems in our homes and elsewhere.

The solution is to cultivate love in our homes. Love is God, and if Christ is in our homes, there will be no problems. When Christ is in our homes, love is present. Therefore, we are all called to live in love and in Christ. We should never have a life or family outside of Christ. Christ loved us and gave us His holy body to eat and His precious blood to drink. This is what Christianity is all about. It is when we understand this that we understand what Love is.

To build a family that is free of complexity, we must rely on love, hold on to God, make the Virgin Mary our mother, seek the intercession of holy angels, righteous martyrs, virgin monks, and look to the way of life of our ancestors for guidance. This is possible through the grace of God, and may our God help us live in love.

👉 Question: How can I cope with the loss of a loved one and be comforted by the hope of resurrection?

✍️ Answer:

text:
The first step in coping with death is understanding what it is. Ecclesiastes Chapter 7, Verse 1 says, "The day of death is better than the day of birth. The righteous are born to suffering and pain, but their death is rest from all this." Thus, we must understand that death is a rest from the hardships of life and hope that our loved ones are at peace.

We are comforted by the belief that death is a journey to God. St. Yared said, "The righteous do not die, but go to their Lord." Therefore, death is a path that leads to God.

However, there is a difference in death for the righteous and the wicked. The death of the righteous is glorious in the eyes of God, whereas the death of the wicked is not. Hence, it is crucial to reflect on the nature of the death we will experience.

The third type of death is separation from this world, from its pain and suffering, and entering a world without suffering.

St. Paul's Epistle to the Philippians from Chapter 1 verse 21-24 states, "For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain. If I am to go on living in the body, this will mean fruitful labor for me. Yet what shall I choose? I do not know! I am torn between the two: I desire to depart and be with Christ, which is better by far; but it is more necessary for you that I remain in the body." It is natural to want to accompany a loved one on their journey to God, and we can find solace in knowing that they are in His presence.

Death is a means by which God takes his people. We are God's possessions, and He has the right to take away His possessions whenever He wants. It is beyond our control, and we must accept it with understanding.

Therefore, whether a person is righteous or a sinner, they will die. The difference lies in the outcome of their death. The righteous die to enter heaven, and the sinner dies to descend into hell. It is important to acknowledge this difference while accepting death as a natural part of life.

We can find comfort in the hope of resurrection, as Christ rose from the dead and showed us that it is possible. We say "we hope for the resurrection of the dead" in our daily prayers, and it is one of the five pillar mysteries of the Church. Christ's resurrection is an example for us, and just as He rose from the dead, we will rise again by God's authority. This is the hope we hold onto.

text:
Our mother, Saint Christos Samra, was born in the district of Shewa Bulga. Her given name was Saint Gaye, and she was born to her God-fearing parents, Saint Deresani and Saint Eleni, on May 20th. Her parents, impressed by her character, raised her with a deep understanding of the laws of God and the order of the church. She later gave birth to eleven children from her husband, Samre Giorgis, nine of whom were males and two of whom were females.

During the reign of Emperor Gebre Meskel, Saint Christos Samra became a righteous Ethiopian who was universally praised for her morals and religion. Upon hearing of her fame, Emperor Gebre Meskel sent 174 servants from among his own to serve her. He also sent her many horses, mules, clothes made of silk and gold, fit for the wives of kings, and shoes of gold. However, Saint Christos Samra did not want any of these things, saying, "I will be hindered and praised for my purpose, the gold and jewelry will be sold and used to feed the poor, but what will I do with these servants?" She asked to God for guidance. A few days later, Saint Michael, the archangel, whose face shines like the sun, came to her with three loaves of bread in his hand and said, "O Kristos Samra, Behold, eat this bread, for God has given it to you in His kindness." Saint Christos Samra thanked her Creator and received the bread from the angel's hand. She ate it, and the aroma and taste fortified her body. As a result, she did not eat food or drink water for three days because the Holy Spirit was within her.

One day, one of her servants which was very troublesome angered her very much and St. Kristos Samra put fire in the servant's mouth. The fire went up to the servant's throat and killed her. Saint Christos Samra was shocked and went into another room, confessing her sins to God. She was very sad and regretful for her loss. God heard her prayer and resurrected her servant from the dead. Our mother Saint Christos Samra said, "Glory be to the God who has not neglected my pleas and has not removed His kindness from me and His servant." She took her baby and went to Mount Lebanon. As she left, the ogre, who lived with gentleness and care, made a trail despite the many barriers and obstacles. She cut the flesh and threw it to the ground, her blood spilling on the ground.

The baby she was carrying was a boy, and she put him down at the door. When the baby was crying bitterly, one of the nuns wanted to take him to her sanctuary. When the baby was crying, the Archangel Saint Michael snatched him away and placed him in heaven.

On one of the days, Saint Michael took her out of the fire, carried her on his wings, and brought her to the island of Tana. She remained there like a planted pillar in the sea for twelve years, standing and praying without coming out until her body was broken and became a passageway for sea fish. After twelve years, our Lord appeared to her and made a promise to her. After this, she spent her entire life in great struggle, and our Lord visited her with His Holy Mother every now and then. Saint Michael, her guardian of all time, blessed her. Our holy mother Christ used to go to the blessed country of Samara and talk with the saints living there for seven days. She was going back to the land of the living where Enoch and Elijah were.

Once, on the other side of Tana, there was a monk named Mekabe God, and an angel called Tsilmat came to him and said, "If you deny the Creator and bury this medicine in your body, death and old age will not overtake you." However, the monk, being warned by the angel about this evil idea, buried his body in the ground.

One day, God's punishment came upon the holy Christ and she prayed, "I send you peace and beg for your mercy. I have committed many sins, to the point of denying God who created me." At that time, our Holy Mother quickly got up and went to the church, being deeply saddened by the man's words, and pointed him towards his creator.

(Continues) 👇

text.text: About the birth of our Lady, the Virgin

text:
Dear esteemed members of the John’s Repentance telegram channel, we are pleased to send you this lesson in celebration of the anniversary of our Lady's birth, which is celebrated on May 9th.

The conception of the Holy Virgin Mary took place fifteen years before the Year of Mercy, in the year 5485 on the eve of the Year of Mercy. As the time for God to forgive His people drew near, the dove of peace appeared on earth to herald the end of destruction. Our Lady is descended from priests on her mother's side and kings on her father's side. Anyone who claims to know Christ but is ignorant of the Virgin Mary's identity, glory, holiness, and her role in the salvation of Adam's race is mistaken.

Some people wrongly claim that the Bible doesn't provide much information about the Virgin Mary. But what needs to be said? It was prophesied in advance that she would give birth to the Lord God, who made heaven, the throne, the earth, the footstool, the sanctity that is the money of nature, and all the creatures that were found by him in the past, and the infinite things that were found in him, the subtle and the giant that was held in the palm of his hand and appeared in front of his eyes. Later, the angel informed her that the time had come. And she gave birth to him, just as she was told. What could be more amazing than saying that she gave birth to the creator, nursed the milk of the all-giver, contained everything, carried Him in her womb, and carried Him on her back?

Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, is the purest of all people, the city of God. Her sanctity is unmatched.

When we say,  “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!" we are acknowledging God's plan to save humankind through a human being who was a pure seed passed down through the loins of the fathers. Through this plan, we were saved from destruction. (Luke 1:42) "Unless the Lord of hosts Had left to us a very small remnant, We would have become like Sodom, We would have been made like Gomorrah." (Isaiah 1:9)

Therefore, Our Lady is a saint who has never been touched by the sin of Adam and Eve that was passed down to generations. As it is written in the Book of Negere Mariam(ነገረ ማርያም), the ancestors of Our Lady on her mother's side, Hana, were named Petrika Tekta(ጴጥሪቃ ቴክታ
), and both of them were pious and God-fearing people who trusted in their God with all their hearts without doubt. They were very rich at that time. 

One day, Petrikah's friend went into the archives and saw the amount of wealth and said to his wife, Tekta, "Even the money we collected would have been saved for our grandchildren. You and I are barren and we have no children to inherit." She thought that he meant that he wanted to have a child, so she said to him in sadness, "If the Lord Israel does not give you a child from me, he will give you someone else, marry someone else and have a child." He said, "The God of Israel knows that I will not do this, and that I will not think it in my heart."

(Continues)👇🏾

The interpreter revealed that seven female calves and seven daughters would be born, and that the seventh daughter, who would give birth to the moon, would be more glorious than the angels. However, the interpreter did not reveal the name of the sun. When Petrikah relayed this to his wife, she thanked God, saying "He knows what the God of Israel does." Soon after, she gave birth to a daughter named Hemen, who in turn gave birth to Hemen, who gave birth to Derde. Derdem have birth to Tonan; And then she gave birth to Sikar. Sikar have birth to Setnan and she gave birth to Hermela. Hermela gave birth to Hanna, who was honored and chosen to be the grandmother of the Lord who created the whole world.

text.text: About the birth of our Lady, the Virgin

text:
Both Hannah and Jacob were God-fearing people who lived by the law, and God had chosen them. Since Hannah was barren, they went to God's house every day and begged for a child who would be a delight to their eyes and a hope for their hearts. One day when they were sad and praying, they saw doves happily playing with their children. Hannah cried bitterly and said, "O my Lord, who gave a child for an animal who has no conscience? Why did you not bless me with a child?" They immediately started fasting and private retreat. Jacob went to the desert and prayed, while Hannah started in the garden around her house. At the end of their fasting and private retreat, they both saw a vision and spoke.

The seven heavens appeared like a veil, and they told Hannah that she saw a white bird come down from the upper sky and sit on her head. The secret of the vision is that when the physical word called "Mif(ምፍ)" is Christ, and his whiteness is his purity. Hannah said, "I saw him come down from above and sit on my head." The fullness of our Lord is the interpretation of the seven heavens.

Hannah also told her husband about a vision she had, in which she saw a white dove sitting on her head, entering her ear, and sleeping in her womb. The secret behind this vision is that the Holy Virgin Mary is symbolized by a dove - a representation of her purity, holiness, and eternal virginity. In Hannah's vision, the white dove came down from her head, entered her ear, and rested in her womb. It was then that she heard the voice of the Archangel Gabriel in her ear, asking her if she would give birth to the pure dove that would conceive God through the Holy Spirit.

After Jacob and Hannah saw this vision on July 30th, they said, "If we have a son, he will be dedicated to serve the house of God. And if we have a daughter, we will make a veil for God's house and she will serve there." After they swore that they saw a vision, they did not meet again that day. The God who said to Adam and Eve, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth" also granted this to them. It was not only because Hannah and Joachim entered into fasting and private retreat to complete the mourning of the court, but it was also because of their piety and devotion to God that they were granted such a blessing. This event marked a new era in the history of mankind, and through the incarnation of Christ, God's plan for salvation was revealed.

In truth, many prophets announced the Sabbath and sanctified fasting. Jeremiah said that the seven days are one day, Daniel said that the seven weeks are one period of withdrawal from worldly affairs, and Enoch spoke many prophecies, counting the seven generations as one one period of withdrawal from worldly affairs. But the idea of all is the same, to reach the time of the virgin. The cry of all these ended with the cry of Hannah and Jacob.

On the thirteenth day of the month of August, the archangel Gabriel appeared to Hana and announced, "You will give birth to a daughter who is greater than any human and more glorious than all the angels." And so it was by the will of God that the conception of Our Lady took place on Sunday, August 13th.

Although the festival of the Conception of the Holy Virgin Mary is celebrated all over the world, the ancient and apostolic Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, where the head of God was conceived, celebrates it with great splendor on August 13th in Mahlet. The holiday is known as "Conception of Mary" and is also celebrated by Christians around the world as "The Conception of the Theotokos," but they observe it on December 9th in preparation for celebrating her birth.

(Continues) 👇🏾

The son of Tolik named Saminas, who was impressed by Ajgu, went from Edok to his uncle's house and passed away. While Hana was walking around holding the pillow of the bed, according to the custom of their country, Saminas quickly got up and said to her, 'Say to the God who created the heavens and the earth, and peace be with you, Hana.' The Jews who were there were frightened and asked, "What did you see, Saminas? What are you saying?"

He said, 'I heard all the angels praising her, saying that the child born from Hannah's womb will give birth to the God who created the heavens and the earth. And she is the one who raised me." Instead of thanking God, when they heard this, they were filled with jealousy and malice. They thought that if Hana saved the fetus in her womb, she would use it against them. Therefore, they urged to stone Hana and Yaakim to death before she gave birth.


At that time, the great archangel Gabriel appeared to Joachim and told him to take Hannah to a mountain called Lebanon. When he first revealed her to the angels on his wings, it was to give her the right of guardianship, as he said through the emissary who was entrusted to protect her from the time of mercy.

Because she is not of this world, she left her home accompanied by her spiritual relatives and angels so that the people who were in the house would not enjoy worldly pleasures because of her birth. As the mother of the Lord who was seeking Adam, who had left his home and lost God, she left the house and traveled to Mount Lebanon, a great place where her ancestors and prophets had seen her in a vision. For she is the Bride of Lebanon who was prophesied to be born in a den of lions under the shade of the mountains of Lebanon.

The wise King Solomon was visited by God and revealed to him that our Lady would be born on Mount Lebanon: "Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, With me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions’ dens, From the mountains of the leopards." (Song of Solomon 4:8). And so, the Holy Virgin Mary was born on Mount Lebanon (Mah 4:10).

Question: How to develop a deep prayer life and strengthen my spiritual life every day; How can I get closer to God?

Answer:

text:
In the pursuit of a profound prayer life and the strengthening of your spiritual journey, it is crucial to approach this endeavor with unwavering commitment, a sincere heart, and a deep understanding of its significance. Let us delve into several key principles, which can serve as guiding lights on the path to experiencing a deeper connection with God through prayer.

First and foremost, prayer should be recognized as a sacred conversation with the Creator—a transcendent opportunity to engage in a direct dialogue with the Almighty. It is not a mere ritualistic duty or an obligation to be fulfilled mechanically; rather, it is an invitation to commune intimately with the divine. In embracing this understanding, one's love for prayer will flourish, and the recognition of its indispensable role in nurturing spiritual well-being will deepen. Let prayer be seen as the very essence of life itself, for just as a person ceases to breathe without air, one who neglects prayer becomes spiritually lifeless.

To truly enter into the spirit of prayer, it is essential to direct our thoughts and intentions towards God. Begin by expressing heartfelt gratitude for His abundant blessings in your life—recognize the gifts of love, grace, and mercy bestowed upon you. Humbly seek His guidance and assistance in all aspects of your existence, acknowledging your dependence upon Him. Remember the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, who admonished us to "watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation." Approach prayer with unwavering sincerity, knowing that it strengthens your resolve, deepens your understanding of God's will, and helps you align your life with His divine purpose.

In order to nurture your spiritual life, it is beneficial to establish clear goals in your prayer practice. Take time to reflect upon your purpose and aspirations in your journey as a Christian. Identify areas in need of growth and development, and bring them before God in prayer. Focus your prayers on cultivating virtues such as love, patience, humility, and forgiveness. Seek to deepen your faith, exploring the mysteries of divine truth and opening your heart to receive spiritual illumination. Embrace a spirit of service, praying for opportunities to extend compassion, kindness, and generosity to those in need. By establishing such intentional goals, you infuse your prayers with purpose and align them with your desired spiritual development.

Consistency in prayer is vital. Establish dedicated times each day, free from distractions, to commune with God. Find a peaceful and secluded space where you can withdraw from the noise and busyness of the world, creating an atmosphere conducive to deepening your connection with the divine. By adhering to a regular prayer routine, you establish a rhythm that reinforces your spiritual bond and fosters a sense of discipline in your spiritual life. Whether it be in the early morning, before meals, or before retiring to rest, choose a time that best suits your circumstances and commit to it unwaveringly.

(Continued) 👇

👉Question: How can I deal with feelings of loneliness and isolation and establish healthy relationships with others?

✍️

text:
፦ Beloved members of Joh’s repentance service, let us delve deeply into the profound topic of loneliness and isolation, and the path towards establishing healthy relationships with others. Understand, my dear ones, that loneliness in the context of our Orthodox faith transcends mere physical solitude. It encompasses a far-reaching spiritual state, where one has renounced the allure of worldly desires, material possessions, and all that displeases our Lord. However, it is vital to discern that this loneliness does not imply a lack of love for our fellow human beings or for our Creator. When we speak of loneliness, it is essential to distinguish it from the condition of one who rejects the ways of Christ and lives contrary to the teachings of our faith.

As devout Orthodox Christians, we firmly believe that we are never truly alone. We are an integral part of a vast and blessed spiritual community, encompassing the Holy Virgin Mary, the angelic hosts, the holy prophets, the noble apostles, the courageous martyrs, the pure virgins, the devoted monks, the reverent priests, and the diligent deacons. that is above all sins 

Question፦

text: What is Ethiopia Orthodox church stand about suicide?

The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church holds a firm stance against suicide, considering it a grave sin and strongly condemning the act. The Church does not provide a dignified funeral or orderly burial for individuals who have taken their own lives, as a means to discourage and set an example for others.

When a child is born into the Church, it is believed that they will grow up to replace their parents and contribute positively to the world. Therefore, when a child tragically succumbs to suicide, it is seen as deviating from their purpose and succumbing to the hidden and abstract influence of evil spirits. The Church views suicide as a spiritual issue, often associated with struggles such as addictions, disharmony within families, marital problems, and difficulties in social relationships.

Suicide is regarded as an act of sin and is considered evil and cursed according to the religious laws and canons of the Church. The prevalence of sin in today's society has made such acts more common, with individuals resorting to various methods such as poisoning, using weapons, drowning, or engaging in car accidents. The Church firmly condemns these actions and deems them as sinful.

To distance ourselves from the influence of the world and satanic forces, we must strive to live a righteous and virtuous life. Even in the face of disasters or circumstances that may bring shame to the soul and body, forsaking eternal life and perishing in this world without a peaceful death signifies the peak of our own injustice and self-destruction. The Church acknowledges that vulnerable individuals, including children, women, and innocents, may succumb to suicide due to pressure and temptation from the same enemy—Satan, who takes pleasure in destroying people and leading them towards self-annihilation.

While there may be instances where individuals use weapons to end their lives, perhaps driven by a misguided sense of bravery or refusing to surrender their country's honor or personal dignity on the battlefield, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church strictly condemns and prohibits suicide. The Church recognizes that people can fall victim to such disasters, but it emphasizes that embracing suicide as an option and collaborating with the power of Satan or his destructive ideas is contrary to its teachings.

The Church is ready to provide spiritual services and support to its children who are confronted with the tragedy of suicide. However, it vehemently rejects any actions that would further lead its children to perish through negative examples. If you, as the questioner, have further inquiries or seek additional guidance on this matter, it would be beneficial for you to express your concerns and seek understanding through appropriate channels within the Church.

Question፦ What is the Ethiopian Orthodox Church Teaching on the Soul After Death?

Answer፦

text:
The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church teaches that after death, the soul and body separate. The soul continues to exist in an abstract form, while the body is laid to rest in the grave. It is believed that both the wicked and the righteous will experience this separation, but their ultimate fate differs.

According to the Orthodox doctrine, those who have committed evil deeds will go to hell, while those who have done good deeds will go to heaven. The criteria for entering heaven are based on the teachings of Matthew chapter 25, where Jesus speaks of acts of kindness such as giving bread and drink to the needy. It is believed that the righteous, who have demonstrated virtuous behavior in their earthly lives, will be rewarded with eternal life in heaven.

The concept of the afterlife in the kingdom of heaven is described as a state free from hunger, thirst, fatigue, envy, and racism. It is a realm where worldly limitations and transient nature cease to exist. The Church teaches that this eternal life is obtained through the resurrection, and it emphasizes that believers will not die but will be transformed.

The example of Christ's resurrection serves as a model for believers. Jesus, after being buried and guarded by soldiers, rose without the need for someone to open the grave or release Him. Similarly, the Church teaches that believers will be resurrected by the authority of Jesus Christ. It is believed that regardless of the circumstances of death, whether through burial or non-burial, all individuals will ultimately rise again when Christ returns.

The teaching of St. Paul provides further insight into the understanding of resurrection. He used the analogy of planting seeds to illustrate that just as grains sown in various conditions will ultimately grow, so too will individuals rise in accordance with their deeds. The wicked will rise with their sinful deeds, while the righteous will rise with their righteous deeds.

In summary, the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church affirms the existence of life after death. It teaches that the soul and body separate at the time of death, and while the body is laid to rest in the grave, the soul continues to exist. The ultimate fate of individuals is determined by their actions in life, with the wicked facing hell and the righteous attaining eternal life in heaven. The Church emphasizes the importance of resurrection, drawing inspiration from the example of Christ's resurrection, and teaches that believers will be transformed and enter into a state free from worldly limitations in the kingdom of heaven.

text.text:
Question፦ Why is it difficult for people to live together in peace and see each other as equals? 

Answer፦

text:
In Orthodox Christianity, the belief is that every person is created in the image and likeness of God. This fundamental teaching highlights the inherent value and dignity of every individual, emphasizing the importance of living together in peace and treating each other as equals. It raises the question: If we are all created as holy beings in the image of God, why is it so difficult for us to coexist harmoniously?

One of the underlying challenges lies in the deviation from our natural identity. In today's era, where various ideologies and beliefs abound, there are conflicting views on the origin and nature of humanity. While Orthodox Christianity affirms that humans are God's handiwork, some other perspectives propose alternative explanations, such as humans descending from apes. These divergent beliefs create a disconnect and contribute to conflicts among individuals, as they fail to recognize the shared foundation of our creation.

When we distance ourselves from our natural identity and disregard the fact that we are made in the image of God, we deviate from the correct understanding of our purpose and nature. God has taught us to love, respect, and refrain from harming one another. However, when individuals forget their divine origin, their behavior and mindset become distorted, leading to actions that contradict the principles of love and unity.

When we fail to acknowledge the inherent value of others and view them as equals, it stems from a lack of trust. This lack of trust is often fueled by the desire for honor, seeking personal recognition and avoiding any perception of inferiority. However, a person who is created in the image of God should not harbor such thoughts or engage in such behavior. It is important to remember that the purpose of our creation is not to exalt ourselves and seek superiority, but rather to glorify God's name and inherit His Kingdom.

The absence of trust gives rise to a pursuit of glory, vengeance, fame, and pride. It causes people to lose sight of their inherent equality and disrupts the bond between individuals. Love, which should be the foundation of our relationships, becomes scarce, and people find it difficult to trust one another equally. In the Orthodox Christian perspective, God's love transcends boundaries of race and language. As believers, we are called to adopt a Christian worldview that recognizes the equality of all people, for Christ died for each and every one of us.

The solution lies in embracing the Christian faith and cultivating a Christian mindset. To see everyone as equals, we need to realize that we all belong to God and that we are united before Him. By adopting an Orthodox perspective, which encompasses the teachings of Christ, we can overcome the barriers of distrust and perceive one another with the eyes of love and equality. This includes loving ourselves, loving our enemies, blessing those who curse us, doing good to those who harm us, and loving those who hate us, as Christ Himself taught.

Therefore, the key to living together in peace and seeing each other as equals is to follow Christ and embody His teachings. By recognizing the sacrificial love of Christ, who offered His holy body and precious blood for all humanity, we come to understand that His love extends to everyone. As Orthodox Christians, we strive to emulate His example and perceive all individuals as one, irrespective of their differences. May the grace of the Good Healer guide us in obeying His commandments and working towards our salvation.

Question፦ Why is the world the way it is today?

Answer፦

text:
The state of the world today can be attributed to a combination of human disobedience and forgetting the purpose for which we were created. The world encompasses not only the physical realm but also the people and their nature within it.

In the Bible, we are instructed not to love the world in the sense of embracing its sinful aspects such as theft, adultery, and lying. However, we are also reminded that God loved the world, referring to His love for humanity. In the teachings of the Church Fathers, the term "world" is often used to denote the people living in the world, including sinners, whom God desires to save.
When the Church Fathers used parables, they often referred to the owner of a house as a way to explain concepts. Similarly, God loved the inhabitants of the world, including sinners, and sought to save them. However, when individuals deviate from doing good and engage in actions that distance them from God, chaos and separation from His grace ensue. Examples of such actions include engaging in homosexual behavior, worshipping evil spirits, and other forms of moral decay.

The root cause of this state of affairs lies in humanity's forgetfulness of its divine purpose. Mankind was created to reflect and emulate God's image and likeness, and our purpose is to praise Him and inherit His kingdom. However, humanity, weakened by its inherent limitations, deviated from its intended path. Humans were created with the potential to be like the holy angels, to exist in a state of communion with God. Yet, through disobedience, humans erred and lost their rightful place. Consequently, they became wandering refugees, estranged from God's grace, and inclined toward embracing evil rather than goodness.

When humans were initially created, they were not destined for pain and suffering. Instead, mankind brought about these hardships through its own actions. Many people disregard the instructions given to us and engage in what they have been cautioned against.

However, after that time, he succumbed to temptation, committing the act he was forbidden from doing. As a consequence, he became a wanderer, losing his place alongside God and in paradise. Adam's transgression introduced scandal and discord into the world. Nevertheless, Adam repented for his mistake and reconciled with God. As St. Paul emphasized in his letter to the Romans (5:10), "While we were God's enemies, he forgave us through the death of his Son." The underlying reason for all these afflictions is humanity's separation from God.

However, despite humanity's inclination to stray from purity and holiness, there is always an opportunity for repentance. The Orthodox tradition teaches that through repentance, one can bridge the gap and restore their relationship with God. St. John the Baptist, known as the Forerunner, proclaimed, "It is better to raise a person who has fallen into sin by means of repentance than to raise the dead." This highlights the transformative power of repentance, which enables us to live in communion with God once again.

In summary, the current state of the world can be attributed to humanity's forgetfulness of its purpose and disobedience to God's commandments. Yet, despite our waywardness, God's love and desire for our salvation remain constant.

Question፦ I easily get very angry and frustrated, especially when someone gives me orders, and I really want to get rid of this behavior but I can't. What should I do?

Answer፦

text:
May the grace and blessings of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon you as you seek guidance in overcoming anger and frustration. Your desire to eliminate these behaviors is commendable. 

To address the issue of anger, we must first understand its root causes. Often, anger stems from our own self-will, our resistance to submitting to the will of others. You mentioned that you experience anger when someone gives you orders. This suggests a lack of appreciation for the value and benefits of obedience.

In the lives of the holy monks, we find exemplary humility and obedience. These spiritual fathers would rise in the night to chop wood and fetch water without anyone commanding them to do so. They understood that in obeying, they could transcend their own desires and draw closer to God. Through obedience, sin can be avoided, for even Christ Himself came to serve and obey for our sake.

Reflect upon the commandment given in the book of Exodus: "Honor your mother and father, obey your mother and father, that your days may be long on earth." The importance of obedience is clearly emphasized here. Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, exemplified humility and obedience to an extraordinary degree. He washed the feet of His disciples, taking on the role of a servant, teaching them the significance of humility.

Indeed, if our Lord, who is God incarnate, washes our feet, then it is our duty to obey and humble ourselves before Him. When we recognize the immense value of obedience, our frustration and anger dissipate. Christ defeated the devil through humility and obedience, triumphing over disobedience and pride. Therefore, by embracing obedience and humility, we align ourselves with the victory of Christ.

If past negative experiences contribute to your frustration and anger, you can gradually overcome them. Through purposeful reflection, discern the advantages and disadvantages of your behavior. Remember that St. Paul reminds us, "I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength." With faith, nothing is impossible.

Throughout history, countless believers who made God their strength, shield, and refuge have witnessed the limitless possibilities granted by God. Our ancestors traveled on the seas, Abune Argawi rode on a dragon, Abune Samuel was carried by a lion, and the Prophet Elijah ascended to the heavens. These remarkable occurrences demonstrate that with God, all things are possible for those who truly believe.

In your pursuit of overcoming anger and frustration, seek the intercession of the saints who have mastered these virtues. Invoke the prayers of St. John Chrysostom himself, for his teachings and writings provide profound insights into the spiritual life.

Embrace prayer, repentance, and the sacramental life of the Church. Frequent reception of the Holy Eucharist and sincere confession can provide you with the strength and grace needed to transform your heart and conquer anger. Cultivate virtues such as patience, kindness, and self-control, which counteract anger and foster inner peace.

Remember, this transformative journey requires perseverance and a steadfast commitment to God's will. Trust in His guidance, for He desires your spiritual growth and will grant you the strength to overcome these challenges. Surrender your anger and frustrations to Him, and allow His divine love to heal your heart.

May the Holy Spirit grant you wisdom, strength, and peace as you embark on this transformative path. Through obedience, humility, and unwavering faith, you will discover the freedom that comes from conquering anger and embracing the virtues of Christ.

text.text: Beloved brethren in Christ, may the grace and peace of God be upon you all. Today, we gather together to commemorate and celebrate the life and legacy of the esteemed Saint Yared of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. Let us delve into the profound teachings and experiences of this great scholar and draw valuable lessons for our own spiritual journey.

text:
Born in the year 505 A.D., near the ancient city of Axum, Saint Yared's upbringing was marked by an early struggle to grasp education. As a young child, he faced difficulties in understanding his studies, which left him disheartened. His mind, however, was captivated by the love for the Virgin Mary and her divine Son. One fateful day, his teacher remarked that he lacked color, insinuating his inability to comprehend the lessons. When tested, young Yared failed to respond and was consequently beaten.

The pain of the punishment deeply affected him, prompting Saint Yared to distance himself from his teacher. Exhausted, he sought refuge in the Mai Kirah area and, in his weariness, received a divine revelation from God. The Lord taught him the importance of perseverance and unwavering effort. Encouraged by this divine guidance, Saint Yared returned to his teacher, sought forgiveness, and resumed his education with renewed determination. He diligently applied himself to his studies and devoted himself to prayer, seeking communion with God.

In His infinite mercy, God blessed Saint Yared with a profound spiritual experience through the intercession of the Virgin Mary. The mysteries that had previously eluded him were unveiled, and he received divine insights and understanding. During his prayers, when heavenly hyms had not yet been revealed, three angels, in the form of birds, appeared before him and spoke to him, granting him their divine counsel.

Reinvigorated by this encounter, Saint Yared returned to the earthly realm, filled with inspiration and gratitude. He offered his thanksgiving in Axum Zion, where the people and the king marveled at the depth and beauty of his spiritual compositions. Saint Yared served diligently in Axum and Debre Damo, ascending to higher spiritual heights with each passing day. Eventually, he left his homeland, aspiring to join the company of the Virgin Mary and the heavenly host.

Throughout the remainder of his life, Saint Yared authored five significant books, leaving a profound legacy for future generations. He established centers of learning and spiritual instruction in Tana Kirkos, Zur Amba, and other locations, where he nurtured and mentored numerous disciples. Saint Yared's contributions to Ethiopian Orthodox Church music are characterized by three distinct types of songs: Geez, Ezl, and Ararai.

The Geez songs, meaning "found first," represent liberation, reminding us of the freedom we find in Christ. The Ezl songs, comprising thirty melodies sung in conjunction with Geez or Tazlo Ezl, inspire fortitude and endurance in the face of trials. Lastly, the Ararai songs, characterized by a melancholic and tender melody, represent the Holy Spirit, who comforts and emboldens believers.
Within Saint Yared's musical compositions, we encounter various symbols that add depth and richness to the musical expression. The "Difat" (ድፋት) symbolizes the descent of Christ from heaven, encouraging us to humbly submit to God's will. The "Hidet" (ሂደት) symbol, exemplified by the Lord's earthly ministry, urges us to continue our journey without hindrance, following in His footsteps.
Furthermore, the "Kinat" (ቅናት) symbol instructs us to lift our heads and proclaim the truth boldly, just as Christ did when confronted by His accusers. The "Yizet" (ይዘት) symbol, observed when a song is read swiftly, reminds us of the Lord's arrest by the Jews. The "Kurt" (ቁርጥ) symbol calls for strength and resilience, likening it to Christ's decision to endure suffering for the redemption of humanity.

The "Yizet" (ይዘት) symbol, observed when a song is read swiftly, reminds us of the Lord's arrest by the Jews. The "Kurt" (ቁርጥ) symbol calls for strength and resilience, likening it to Christ's decision to endure suffering for the redemption of humanity.

(Continues)👇🏾

text:
👆🏾

We also encounter the "Chiret" (ጭረት) symbol, which denotes a quick movement within the melody, reflecting the urgency and swiftness of God's action. The "Rikrik" (ርክርክ) symbol encourages us to lengthen our spiritual melodies, reminding us of the eternal sacrifice of Christ and the abundant grace He bestows upon us. Lastly, the "Deret" (ደረት) symbol, characterized by a powerful and resounding voice, signifies the Lord's ascension, urging us to exalt and proclaim His glory.

Let us now explore some of the notable compositions of Saint Yared. "Dgwa,"(ድጓ) a song offered on Sundays and annual holidays, encompasses the Eucharistic celebration and conveys the profound mystery and joy of the Holy Communion. "Tsome Dgwa" (ጾመ ድጓ) refers to a specific variant of the song sung during the period of Abiy Lent, incorporating verses from Zawadah-Hosanna.
Another remarkable composition is "Zimare," (ዝማሬ) which is performed after the Eucharist. "Mwaset"(መዋሥዕት) is a prayer for the departed, sung during funerals, while "Mieraf" (ምዕራፍ) is a composition sung in every chapter, symbolizing a place of rest. The works of Saint Yared are intricate and carry profound spiritual significance, inviting us to explore the depths of our faith.
Saint Yared's spiritual journey continued as he traveled extensively, leaving an indelible mark on the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. Saint Yared with his disciples Sawira, Eskender and Menker, embarked on a journey to the north, Semen Berh. They carried their hymn books and lived in the monastery by teaching hymns in the northern monastery. 

In one particularly extraordinary incident, Saint Yared entered the Axum Zion Church and placed his hands upon the sacred coffin. With a voice filled with reverence and awe, he uttered these words: "You are holy, you are blessed, you are praised; You are blessed. You are exalted, you are the ladder of light." As he recited his composition called "Anketse Berhan," (አንቀጸ ብርሃን) while singing the Ezl song, he ascended about an arm's length towards the heavens. This miraculous event left the psalmists astounded, and Saint Yared imparted his final words of guidance and farewell before retreating to a hidden cave, disappearing from this earthly realm.

On the 11th of May, in the year 571 A.D., at the age of 66, Saint Yared departed from this temporal existence, leaving behind a spiritual legacy that continues to inspire and uplift the faithful even to this day.

Dear brethren, as we reflect upon the life of Saint Yared, let us draw valuable lessons for our own spiritual journey. His unwavering commitment to education and perseverance in the face of challenges remind us of the importance of continuous learning and growth in our faith. Saint Yared's profound spiritual experiences and revelations underscore the transformative power of prayer and communion with God.

Through his hymnodical compositions and symbols, Saint Yared invites us to elevate our worship, allowing our voices and melodies to be a conduit for spiritual expression. His compositions, rich with deep meaning and divine inspiration, serve as a reminder of the beauty and majesty of our Orthodox tradition.

May we be inspired by the life and teachings of Saint Yared, remembering the importance of perseverance, unwavering faith, and an ardent pursuit of divine knowledge. Let us strive to cultivate a deep and vibrant spiritual life, expressing our devotion to God through worship and service. May Saint Yared's legacy continue to resonate within our hearts and guide us on our journey towards eternal communion with our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Amen.
