Dear members of John's Repentance service, grace and peace be with you all. Today, we bring you a profound lesson on the topic of fear—a lesson that can transform your relationship with God and grant you eternal value. As we delve into this teaching, let us remember the words of the Apostle Paul, who declared, "For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind" (2 Timothy 1:7).

Fear, my beloved, is a powerful force that often keeps us away from experiencing the fullness of God's love and presence in our lives. It is an insidious barrier that seeks to separate us from the divine truths and promises that are freely bestowed upon us. It is fear that instills doubt within us, casting shadows of uncertainty and hesitancy upon the path we tread.

In the scriptures, we encounter stories of faithful individuals who faced fear head-on, triumphing over its grip and emerging as beacons of unwavering devotion. Mary Magdalene, a woman of great faith, stood fearless before the armed Roman soldiers guarding the tomb of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. While others cowered in fear, she became the first witness to the glorious resurrection (Matthew 28:1-10).

Similarly, we learn of the three young boys who defied the powerful king Nebuchadnezzar. They refused to bow down to the image erected by the king, even when threatened with the fiery furnace. Their unwavering faith in God shielded them from the scorching flames, as the angel of the Lord came to their rescue (Daniel 3:1-30).

Saint George, known for his courageous spirit, fearlessly proclaimed his allegiance to God, even in the face of persecution. Presented with a millstone to grind a blade for his execution, he persevered, standing as a testament to his unyielding faith. His steadfastness transformed the heart of King Dudianus, who, in shame and fear, bore witness to God's divinity.

Consider the apostle John, who, when others succumbed to fear and fled, remained steadfast, accompanying Jesus to Calvary (John 19:26). In times of ease and joy, many profess their faith, but it is during times of trial and tribulation that true followers are revealed. Christ, burdened with the weight of the cross, found no one to comfort Him as He stumbled and fell along the arduous path.

Therefore, we implore you, our dear members, to cast off the shackles of fear and embrace the unwavering trust that should define our relationship with the Almighty. Let not your hearts be troubled by the challenges and uncertainties that surround us. We have been entrusted with the divine task of bearing witness to the Word of God without fear or hesitation. Embrace this calling, for it is worthy of the Lord Himself.

Take solace in the example of Aaron, the brother of Prophet Moses. Faced with the demands of a fearful people, he succumbed to their desires, fashioning a golden calf as an object of worship (Exodus 32:1-35). The fear that gripped Aaron caused him to stray from the path of righteousness, leading the Israelites astray. It is this kind of fear, born of doubt and insecurity, that we must eradicate from our hearts.

Even the apostles, in their weakness, succumbed to fear. They fled, discarding their garments, when confronted with the imminent arrest of Jesus. Fear led Peter to deny his Lord three times (Mark 14:50-52, 86-91). However, in the temporary nature of their fear, there arose an opportunity for repentance and restoration.

Let us, therefore, exercise caution, my brethren, so as not to allow this fleeting fear to become a hindrance to our repentance. May we not be deceived into believing that sin can be justified or excused by the passing fears of the present moment. Instead, let us cultivate a fear that is rooted in reverence for God, a fear that fuels our endurance and propels us towards salvation.

Dear members of John's Repentance service, grace and peace be with you all. Today, we bring you a profound lesson on the topic of fear—a lesson that can transform your relationship with God and grant you eternal value. As we delve into this teaching, let us remember the words of the Apostle Paul, who declared, "For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind" (2 Timothy 1:7).

Fear, my beloved, is a powerful force that often keeps us away from experiencing the fullness of God's love and presence in our lives. It is an insidious barrier that seeks to separate us from the divine truths and promises that are freely bestowed upon us. It is fear that instills doubt within us, casting shadows of uncertainty and hesitancy upon the path we tread.

In the scriptures, we encounter stories of faithful individuals who faced fear head-on, triumphing over its grip and emerging as beacons of unwavering devotion. Mary Magdalene, a woman of great faith, stood fearless before the armed Roman soldiers guarding the tomb of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. While others cowered in fear, she became the first witness to the glorious resurrection (Matthew 28:1-10).

Similarly, we learn of the three young boys who defied the powerful king Nebuchadnezzar. They refused to bow down to the image erected by the king, even when threatened with the fiery furnace. Their unwavering faith in God shielded them from the scorching flames, as the angel of the Lord came to their rescue (Daniel 3:1-30).

Saint George, known for his courageous spirit, fearlessly proclaimed his allegiance to God, even in the face of persecution. Presented with a millstone to grind a blade for his execution, he persevered, standing as a testament to his unyielding faith. His steadfastness transformed the heart of King Dudianus, who, in shame and fear, bore witness to God's divinity.

Consider the apostle John, who, when others succumbed to fear and fled, remained steadfast, accompanying Jesus to Calvary (John 19:26). In times of ease and joy, many profess their faith, but it is during times of trial and tribulation that true followers are revealed. Christ, burdened with the weight of the cross, found no one to comfort Him as He stumbled and fell along the arduous path.

Therefore, we implore you, our dear members, to cast off the shackles of fear and embrace the unwavering trust that should define our relationship with the Almighty. Let not your hearts be troubled by the challenges and uncertainties that surround us. We have been entrusted with the divine task of bearing witness to the Word of God without fear or hesitation. Embrace this calling, for it is worthy of the Lord Himself.

Take solace in the example of Aaron, the brother of Prophet Moses. Faced with the demands of a fearful people, he succumbed to their desires, fashioning a golden calf as an object of worship (Exodus 32:1-35). The fear that gripped Aaron caused him to stray from the path of righteousness, leading the Israelites astray. It is this kind of fear, born of doubt and insecurity, that we must eradicate from our hearts.

Even the apostles, in their weakness, succumbed to fear. They fled, discarding their garments, when confronted with the imminent arrest of Jesus. Fear led Peter to deny his Lord three times (Mark 14:50-52, 86-91). However, in the temporary nature of their fear, there arose an opportunity for repentance and restoration.

Let us, therefore, exercise caution, my brethren, so as not to allow this fleeting fear to become a hindrance to our repentance. May we not be deceived into believing that sin can be justified or excused by the passing fears of the present moment. Instead, let us cultivate a fear that is rooted in reverence for God, a fear that fuels our endurance and propels us towards salvation.

(Continues)  👇

text:
👆🏾

Let us turn our attention to the remarkable story of Saint Sosna—a woman falsely accused of adultery and sentenced to death by stoning. In the face of imminent peril, she fearlessly declared, "It is better for me to be sentenced to death than to be punished by God for committing this sin." Her steadfastness and unwavering faith invoked divine intervention, as God sent Daniel and His archangel, Saint Michael, to save her from her accusers.

In closing, our beloved members, we beseech you to cast off the garment of fear that impedes your journey towards God. Embrace the call to wholehearted devotion and unwavering trust. Remember that fear cannot conquer the human soul, for the soul's ultimate fate rests solely in the hands of the Divine.

Let your faith be a testament to the power and love of our Lord, Jesus Christ. For it is He who proclaims, "Be of good cheer, I have overcome the world" (John 16:33). In this knowledge, we find the strength to conquer fear, to embrace our divine calling, and to inherit the eternal blessings that await us.

text.text:
Question:" [Acts 7 : 6 - 7]

6. But God spoke in this way: that his descendants would dwell in a foreign land,  and that they would bring them into bondage and oppress them four hundred years.

7. ‘And the nation to whom they will be in bondage I will judge,’ said God, ‘and after that they shall come out and serve Me in this place.’

 Genesis 15 : 12 - 14
12. Now when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and behold, horror and great darkness fell upon him.

13. Then He said to Abram: “Know certainly that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them, and they will afflict them four hundred years.

14. And also the nation whom they serve I will judge; afterward they shall come out with great possessions.

Bless me my father ,..
Why 400 years and which nation was to be judged?"

Answer:

text:
Dear brethren, in addressing the question posed, let us delve into the profound teachings of the Bible, drawing from the Acts of the Apostles and the book of Genesis. These sacred scriptures contain the word of God and provide insights into His divine plan, as revealed to our revered forefather Abraham.

To fully grasp the significance of this passage, we must first recognize the extraordinary relationship between God and Abraham. The Old Testament attests to the multitude of times God communicated with the Prophet Moses, estimating around five hundred and seventy occasions. Yet, it is Abraham who holds a unique position as God's cherished friend, for the Lord Himself proclaimed, "I do not have a friend like Abraham on earth."

Even today, in the New Testament, we invoke the covenant established with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, beseeching their intercession for reconciliation with God and seeking His forgiveness. Abraham stands as the cornerstone, for without him, neither Isaac nor Jacob would have existed. They are referred to as "the fathers," but it is Abraham who lays the foundation for their lineage and their significance in God's plan.

Now, turning to the specific passage in question, we find a direct address to Abraham regarding his descendants. God speaks of their future plight, foretelling their sojourn in a foreign land and their subjugation and oppression for a period of four hundred years. This divine pronouncement is explicitly recorded in both the Acts of the Apostles and the book of Genesis.

During those four centuries, the children of Jacob, later known as the Israelites, endured the hardships of slavery and lived under the yoke of tyranny. God's promise to Abraham encompasses not only their earthly sufferings but also holds the promise of hope for all nations and peoples. Through Jesus Christ, born of Abraham's seed, salvation would be offered to all, unifying diverse peoples and redeeming their lives.

The Egyptians, as revealed in the Acts of the Apostles, would exercise dominion over the Israelites for four hundred years. God's words foretold that He would execute judgment upon the nation that oppressed His chosen people. Consequently, the Israelites would be liberated from their bondage and return to Canaan to worship and serve God in the land of their inheritance.

Turning our attention to Genesis 15 in the Torah, we encounter further details concerning the fulfillment of God's promises. At the time, Joseph held a position of high esteem as an esteemed counselor in the court of the Egyptian Pharaoh. The Pharaoh revered Joseph and granted him privileges, resulting in favorable treatment for the Israelites during this period.

However, when a new Pharaoh ascended the throne, ignorant of Joseph's legacy, the Israelites found themselves subjected to the burdensome weight of oppression. Their existence in Egypt, spanning four hundred and thirty years, was marked by hardship and servitude.

text.text: How to overcome repeated sin and discouragement?

Question: How does one overcome feelings of defeat and discouragement when falling into the same sin continually?
How to accept God's love and grace and not give up / lose hope with struggles that come with my journey with God? 
I tend to fall short of the goals I set for myself in spiritual life and the discouragement / feeling depressed about that holds me back from making progress. 

Thank you and May God bless your service!

text:
This is a very important question because a lot of people confess their sins many times and go back to it many times. The main cause of this is not knowing what sin is and not understanding the depths of it's consequences. 

If a person confess their sins without understand what sin is, they will most likely fall back into it. If a person confesses their sins without understanding the benefits of repentance, it will be very hard for them to come back to repentance.

Hence we first need to learn about sin, it's consequences and the benefits of repentance. We need to learn from people that have fallen into sin, we need to know that sin separates us from God, sin deprives us from peace, sin brings curses to our lives, sin is the worst thing one can do. 

People who have fallen into sin have lost God, lost blessings, lost peace, lost life and can't even get alone with themselves. That is why Adam and Eve had a hard time living together after they fell into sin. Adam had asked Eve to get away from him, to depart form him accusing her to be the reason of his fall. People who have fallen into sin can't live with others nor be comfortable in their own skin. That is why Judas of Iscariot, who sold our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ with $30 thought that he was doing good for himself, that he would live but he couldn't. He threw away the money, hanged himself up on a tree and died after suffering for 40 days. Hence we need to understand that people trapped in sin can't live with God, with others nor with themselves. This, we have to believe before confessing. 

One needs to understand the depths of sin's consequences, and also understand the benefits of repentance. We need to learn from people who changed their lives and were healed through repentance. It is only then that we will have not repeatedly fall back to sin. 

We need to believe that everything is possible with God and nothing without Him. On Matthew 21:21, our Lord tells us "if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but also if you say to this mountain, ‘Be removed and be cast into the sea,’ it will be done." Hence why do we give up? We are winners in Christ, we fall and we get back up but we should never give up, why do we give up? Are we not the ones He created in His own image? Are we not the ones whom He appointed as rulers over creatures? It is us that He has delivered from the bondage of the devil by becoming one of us, it is for us that He has given his Holy Blood and Holy Flesh. It is for us that is given the interception of the apostles, the prophets, the angels, the saints, the virgins, the monks, our Lady Virgin Mary and others. Hence how can we give up? It is for us that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ established the mystery of Repentance so we can be reconciled with Him if we fall. Hence we do not give up. The holy water, the cross, the priests, the gospel, the prayer books, the advisors, the teachers, the fasts, prostration and countless more are ours. Hence how can we give up? We don't!

text:
The biggest and most gravious temptation of the devil is to make us give up. But we Christians never give up. Let us recall a story of a monk: There was a father who repeatedly sinned and repeatedly confessed. Then the devil said to him: "Are you not ashamed? Everyday you sin and everyday you confess it, you go to your spiritual father and confess the sin knowing you will fall tomorrow as well." Then this father said to him: "You that have no repentance, you that do not wish to be reconciled with God, you be ashamed but how can I be ashamed since repentance was established for me". Truly, repentance was established for us so we shouldn't give up.

The devil makes sin seem trivial for those who haven't previously fallen into it by showing them people who have fallen into sin and saying: "what consequences did they have to face for their sins? Your sins are nothing compared to their sins, you have not done anything wrong" Then he teaches us to sin step by step making us immune and ignorant to the consequences of it.

Then once we have fallen deep into it, he says: "Look at you, do you think God is going to forgive you? Are you not ashamed to approach God with all these sins? Are you not ashamed to go to a prist and admit to all these sins? You shameful being!" To make us think that God doesn't forgive, painting him as cruel. 

Hence we should understand that this is the devil's trap and get up when we fall, never give up. We have the hope to inherit our Lord's Kingdom, which is eternal and absolute. Hence how can we give up? We don't! God died for us, it is for us that he gave his Holy Blood and his Holy Flesh, it is for us that he gave his mother the Virgin Mary. Hence we don't give up.

text.text: I have lots of challenges in

. I hate my life, what should I do?

Question፦

Fathers, I am suffering a lot on this earth, what should I do? I pray every day so lack of prayer is not the reason.  3 days ago, I tried to commit suicide but couldn't. And even today, I'm not happy. The problem is:

1) I am divorced
2) I work a lot but have nothing
3) I don't get along with my family. Nobody likes me. I live in my mother's house with my kids.

text:
Beloved child of God, we mpathize deeply with the suffering and pain you have endured on this earthly journey. It is in times like these that we must turn to our faith and seek solace in the wisdom and guidance of our Lord. Know that your struggles are not in vain, for God often uses trials to refine us and elevate us to greater heights of nobility and honor.

As human beings, we often fail to recognize the abundance of blessings that God bestows upon us. We become complacent and fail to work diligently to cultivate and nurture the gifts that have been entrusted to us. However, when faced with small challenges, we easily become disheartened and feel as if we are being consumed by fire, pierced by a knife, or plagued by misfortune. These hardships weigh heavily on our spirits, testing our inner strength in ways that seem unbearable.

Yet, remember the words of Scripture: "O Lord, deliver me from this snare, free me from the net in which I am entangled, and rescue me from the temptations that surround me." To shield us from these trials, we have been instructed to pray, "Lord, lead us not into temptation."

Though today may appear bleak and life may seem like an arduous journey, take heart, for we are alive in Christ forever. Though weariness may overwhelm us, our inner strength is far greater. Though we may be poor in material possessions, God, by His grace and divine will, will make us abundantly rich. He is the one who bestows honor upon us in countless ways, showering us with blessings beyond measure. This test that seems insurmountable is but a stepping stone to a future of joy and happiness.

Remember, God works in ways that surpass our understanding and imagination. His gifts are immeasurable and boundless, bestowed upon us generously. He may appear to be a judge, yet if He believes in us and loves us, He tests us with challenges that may seem insurmountable, but He knows we can overcome. 

To you, dear questioner, I beseech you, believe that this trial you are facing is a foundation and a bridge to a brighter tomorrow. Trust that God's plan for you encompasses things you cannot fathom or comprehend at this moment. Embrace the gift of faith and hold steadfast in the knowledge that God, in His infinite wisdom, is working in your life.

Regarding your sense of being unloved and rejected, do not perceive yourself as unlovable or despised by others. Love is a complex matter, and sometimes the reasons behind others' actions or emotions remain concealed. Do not hastily conclude that you are hated or cursed, for such thoughts only serve to empower Satan's influence in your life. Instead, seek the truth that lies beyond appearances and pray for understanding and reconciliation.

In your current circumstances, living in your mother's house with your children, it may be challenging to find peace and harmony within your family. However, I implore you, do not lose hope. Trust in God's providence and believe that He can heal and restore relationships. Many have experienced the mending of their lives through God's intervention, and I firmly believe the same can happen for you.

In your darkest hours and moments of sadness, turn to the Mother of God, the Blessed Virgin Mary. Entrust your troubles to her, for she is a source of comfort and strength. I have faith that she will intercede on your behalf and guide you through this storm. Please reach out to us at our address, for we are here to support you and walk alongside you on this journey of healing and restoration.

Question: It has been one year since I got married but I couldn't have physical intimacy with my wife, because she has no feelings at all, she feels great pain, we tried different solutions, advice, treatment, prayers, but we couldn't find a solution, what solution do you give us?

Answer:

text:
In facing such a challenging situation, we turn to the teachings of the Church and seek solace in our faith. What does the Church offer to the needy? Prayer. Our questioner has mentioned that they have already tried prayer, along with various solutions, advice, treatment, and yet they have not found a solution. As Christians, we believe in the power of prayer and in God's ability to heal, but we must also recognize that God's timing and plan may be different from our own.

When we approach prayer, it is important not to limit it to a fixed timeframe. God knows what we may not think, and He knows what we do not know. There may be something that will ultimately benefit us in ways we cannot yet comprehend. Our approach to prayer should not be focused solely on a predetermined date or outcome. It is essential to remember that everything is in God's hands.

If we set a specific date by which we expect to be saved or find a solution, and if that date passes without the desired outcome, it is not right for us to abandon our faith or lose hope. Instead, we should continue to seek God's guidance and intervention. By practicing the faith to the fullest, actively partaking from the Eucharist, We beseech God to make all things right. We have fulfilled our part, and if we grow weary and do not find an immediate solution, we must trust that we have done what we can.

It is crucial to understand that not all prayers are answered according to our desires or timeline. We must recognize that there are aspects beyond our control, and we have our part to play while God has His. Yet, even in situations where we do not understand the reasons behind our circumstances, we should accept God's will with joy. Ultimately, the solution lies in God Himself, and we should not lose sight of this truth.

During such challenges in life, it is not uncommon for people to offer help and solutions outside the teachings of the Church. However, we must remember that this is ultimately God's work. It is God's will for a husband and wife to be united and for them to be helpers to each other. It is not appropriate for anyone to intervene and suggest alternative solutions based on their own judgment. We must have faith in God's plan and trust that He will guide us through our difficulties.

Patience is a virtue we learn through our relationship with God. It is His will for us to come together in marriage, and beyond that, it is His will for us to remain united as one and potentially have children. We must not do anything that interferes with God's plan. We should trust that our actions will not harm our souls or bodies. We can draw inspiration from the story of Hannah and Joachim, who endured years of childlessness but remained steadfast in their faith. In their patience, God blessed them with a child who became the salvation of the entire world. Likewise, God worked a miraculous birth through the Virgin Mary, and He granted Elizabeth, who was old, a child who would baptize the Lord.

Therefore, dear member, your story is unique, and God has something in store for you that we may not yet comprehend. Perhaps it is a path towards holiness and sanctification. Have you considered this possibility? Remember the example of Demetrius and Princess Wine, who maintained their purity and holiness for forty-eight years, sleeping in the same bed, wearing the same clothes, and laying the same carpet. They trusted in God's plan and purpose. Who knows what God has prepared for you? We must contemplate this thought.

text:
Dear members of John's Repentance service, today is the day we celebrate the ascension of our Lord. The Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ is a profound and glorious event that holds immense significance for our faith and salvation. As we delve into this topic, let us explore the teachings of the early Church Fathers and contemplate the deep theological truths revealed through the Scriptures.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, the divine Son, who became incarnate and took on our human nature, ascended to the right hand of the Father, as prophesied by King David. In Psalm 110:1, David declared, "God said to my Lord, 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.'" This prophecy finds fulfillment in Jesus Christ, as the Epistle to the Hebrews affirms, "But when this priest [Jesus] had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, he sat down at the right hand of God" (Hebrews 10:12).

By sitting at the right hand of the Father, our Lord Jesus Christ demonstrates His divine nature and equality with the Father. It is crucial to understand that this exaltation does not imply any temporal or hierarchical subordination within the Trinity. Rather, it speaks to the profound mystery of the Incarnation, wherein the Son, while on Earth, willingly submitted Himself to the limitations of our human nature. Consequently, when Scripture speaks of Christ sitting at the right hand of the Father, it emphasizes His return to His former glory, without any separation from His divinity.

The Incarnation of Christ signifies that the Word, without diminishing His fullness, assumed a human body and soul from the Holy Virgin Mary for the sake of our salvation. Likewise, His Ascension proclaims that, without separating from the fully united body and soul, Christ ascended in glory for our benefit. In the 24th chapter of Luke's Gospel, the venerable Saint Cyril of Alexandria, a steadfast pillar of our faith, elucidates this truth: "After blessing his disciples, he ascended into heaven and sat in his Father's house, not only in His divinity but also in His unified body." Through His Incarnation and Ascension, Christ united our fallen nature with His divine glory, granting us the possibility of sharing in His heavenly kingdom.

The Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ should not be viewed as a mere physical act of sitting and rising, as befitting our human experience. Instead, it symbolizes the glorification of our human nature, once marred by sin and distanced from God's grace. Our Lord, by uniting our nature with His divinity, bestowed incomprehensible honor upon us. Ephesians 2:6 captures this beautifully, declaring, "And God raised us up with Christ and seated us with him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus."

In the death and resurrection of our Lord, He conquered the power of death, wiping away the consequences of sin. Through His Ascension, our human nature, which was judged and condemned, is now elevated to sit in the presence of the Father. As Saint John the Baptist expounded, Christ offered His body as a sacrifice, serving as our High Priest, presenting Himself to the Father with His body and blood. The Father, in admiration, declared, "Sit at my right hand." The earth that we once were, destined to return to dust, now finds itself exalted beyond measure. Christ surpassed the ranks of angels, ascended above the cherubim, and attained a throne higher than the archangels. His ascent extended beyond mere elevation; it led Him to the throne of His eternal kingdom, where He reigns in glory.

text:

Indeed, the Ascension of our Lord was foretold by the prophets. The Psalms proclaim, "You have taken captives and ascended" (Psalm 68:18) and "God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the Lord amid the sounding of trumpets" (Psalm 47:5). In the Holy Scriptures, our Lord Himself reveals, "In my Father's house are many rooms; if it were not so, I would have told you. I am going there to prepare a place for you" (John 14:2). The evangelists and apostles also bear witness to the Ascension, recording that "after speaking to them, the Lord Jesus was taken up into heaven and he sat at the right hand of God" (Mark 16:19, Luke 24:51-52). As they watched, a cloud enveloped Him and received Him from their sight (Acts 1:9-11). Furthermore, the secret of imitating God is revealed in His glorious Ascension—He was incarnate, justified by the Spirit, seen by angels, preached to the Gentiles, believed in throughout the world, and ultimately ascended in majestic glory (1 Timothy 3:16).

The early Church Fathers, the custodians of our sacred tradition, expounded upon the Ascension of our Lord. Their teachings and exegesis illuminate the depths of this profound mystery. They bestowed upon us invaluable insights into the divine economy of salvation, helping us to grasp the significance of Christ's Ascension and its impact on our lives.

May the contemplation of our Lord's Ascension deepen our understanding of His divine nature and His salvific work. Let us rejoice in the glorification of our human nature through union with the divine. And as we eagerly anticipate His promised return, may we strive to imitate His virtues and partake in His heavenly kingdom. Amen.

text: In the depths of humanity's fallen state, when death entered the world, it did so through three grievous crimes: impatience, pride, and greed. Yet, through the grace of Christ, death was conquered by three great virtues, which we shall explore in depth. Drawing from the wisdom of the Orthodox tradition, we shall delve into the significance of patience, humility, and contentment, and their transformative power in the life of a believer.

Impatience, born from a restless spirit, is a formidable obstacle in the path of righteousness. As we reflect upon the events in the Garden of Eden, we witness the devastating consequences of haste. The serpent, the preacher of sin, whispered to Eve, stirring unease within her heart. Restlessness clouded her judgment, and she failed to investigate the serpent's deceitful words. Subsequently, Adam, who should have stood firm, was also swayed by impatience, leading both of them towards a tragic downfall.

Impatience continues to afflict humanity, as we often succumb to the allure of sin without considering the consequences. Yet, Christ, the second Adam, demonstrated the power of patience. He endured the mocking and scourging silently, willingly accepting the weight of our sins. By His patience, He astonished onlookers and conquered death itself. In imitating Christ's patience, we find the strength to endure, for salvation belongs to those who persevere till the end.

Pride, the first sin, is a perilous temptation that ensnares even the noblest of creatures. It is the root of disobedience and rebellion against God's established order. In the Garden of Eden, this sin manifested itself when Adam and Eve disregarded the fear of God and broke His commandment. The devil himself, consumed by pride, had no opportunity for repentance, succumbing to eternal damnation.

To counteract this destructive pride, we must embrace humility and obedience. Our Lord Jesus Christ, the epitome of humility, willingly submitted Himself to the cross, even unto death, to redeem us from the consequences of our disobedience. He obediently accepted the weight of our sins, showcasing that obedience is the path to true life. Just as a child obeys their parent, even to the point of sacrifice, Christ demonstrated obedience to remove the death sentence imposed upon us by our disobedience. In imitating Christ's obedience, we restore the image of God within us and find our way back to eternal communion with Him.

- Overcoming Greed and Embracing Generosity
Greed, the insidious desire for more, separates us from the company of God and His heavenly angels. It distorts our perception, causing us to covet what is forbidden or unnecessary. In the Garden, Adam and Eve beheld the tree and its fruit, considering it beautiful and desirable only after the serpent planted the seed of greed within them.

Greed leads us down a treacherous path, where the devil entices us with false promises and desires. When we fail to find contentment in the grace bestowed upon us, death lurks nearby, ready to claim our lives. Yet, our Lord Jesus Christ, the Second Adam, offers a powerful antidote. He, who did not even desire His own life, willingly sacrificed Himself for others. Even in death, He gave generously, making amends for the wrongs committed by greed. Our first father rushed to acquire what he lacked, driven by covetousness, while our second father willingly gave

 His own wealth, even His flesh and blood, for our salvation. Through Christ, we learn to replace greed with generosity, finding fulfillment in selflessness and gratitude.

text:
<<< I've Never Met an Atheist!

The young man announced at the beginning of a college class that he was an atheist. I'd been invited as a guest lecturer, and had opened the talk with the observation that everyone has a nous that hungers for God. This young man took exception, declaring there was no God, and furthermore stating that he certainly did not have hunger for a relationship with anything that could be defined as a god.

I asked him to define the god he'd chosen to deny, and after hearing his definition, I declared that I agreed with him. I, too, did not believe in such a god. The average understanding of just who God is, has largely been based on a concept that is not in sync with the biblical description of God, nor the teachings of the historic Church. Furthermore, the false science that is the basis for the denial of God's involvement in creation, and in the life of our world, has come about due, in large part, to this very misconception of just who God is, to begin with.

The accounts of this miraculous event bring forth valuable lessons and spiritual insights that will undoubtedly enrich our lives. Like the holy fathers before us, we must seek the guidance of God as we explore the splendor and significance of the apparition, imploring His divine assistance to shed light upon this extraordinary encounter with our beloved Mother.

text.text: The Prophecy and Significance of St. Mary:

text: In the sacred Psalms, the prophet David, God's chosen servant, foretold that both the nobles of heaven and the nations of the earth would beseech and swear to see the radiant face of our beloved Lady. Throughout history, every prophet and apostle has spoken of St. Mary, affirming her exalted position and the divine grace bestowed upon her. Let us, therefore, beseech the same God who aided them to grant us understanding and illumination in our exploration of this momentous event.

text.text: The Annual Festivals of St. Mary:

text: Our Lady, St. Mary, is honored throughout the year with various festivals and celebrations. Let us focus on the significant annual occasions that commemorate her extraordinary life. May 9th marks the anniversary of the Holy Virgin Mary's birth, followed by May 29th, when she manifested herself to both Gentiles and Christians. On June 28th, her divine Son descended to establish her abode, signifying a momentous day of celebration. Furthermore, August 22nd commemorates the day of her incarnation, while December 13th marks her entrance into the temple. On January 30th, we remember the day of our Lady's rest, and on February 24th, the promise of mercy and salvation was accepted. Let us honor these festivals with reverence and gratitude, as we partake in the richness of our faith.

Hannah and Jacob, who had experienced the heart-wrenching loss of a child, persevered in their faith, beseeching God with unwavering devotion. Their plea was answered, and the Virgin Mary, the mother of God, was given to them as a treasure beyond compare—a treasure that would alleviate not only their own poverty but also the poverty of the entire world.

text.text: The Virgin Mary's Role in Christianity:

text: Dear brethren, we must comprehend the immense significance of the Virgin Mary in our Christian faith. She is the Mother of God, above all creation and below the Creator Himself. Our Lord Jesus Christ promised her, during their exile in Egypt, that a church would be erected in her name on the very site where we stand today. The fulfillment of this prophecy is a testament to God's faithfulness and a symbol of the Virgin Mary's unparalleled intercession.

text.text: The Blessing and Grace of St. Mary:

text:
When the Virgin Mary blesses us, dear brethren, it is not a mere utterance of goodwill or forgiveness. Rather, her blessings carry the power of divine grace, enriching our lives and bringing forth spiritual abundance. Although the Bible does not explicitly speak of her blessings, we acknowledge her as the vessel of God's grace and mercy. Just as she interceded for the wedding guests at Cana, turning water into wine, she intercedes for us, transforming our lives and granting us spiritual abundance.

(Continues) 👇

text.text: 👉🏾 What is the basic purpose of

? Is there a difference between secular marriage and a marriage conducted in church?

✍️Answer፦

text:
The institution of marriage holds a deep significance in the Orthodox Church, reflecting the union of the bridegroom and the bride. It is regarded as a sacred mystery that is celebrated through a ceremony conducted in the church, accompanied by a sacrament that symbolizes the joining and oneness of the couple. In the words of Scripture, "A man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh" (Matthew 19:5). Thus, marriage is a profound mystery in which the couple commits to love and cherish each other exclusively, with the intention of starting a family, sharing their lives and possessions, and living together as long as God permits.

The purpose of marriage can be understood through three pillars: mutual support, procreation, and safeguarding against adultery. Firstly, marriage provides a framework for helping and supporting one another. Recognizing the words of God, "It is not good for man to be alone. Let us create a suitable helper for him" (Genesis 2:18), Orthodox teachings emphasize that marriage is a divine gift that assists individuals on their spiritual journey. At its core, marriage relies on genuine affection and love between spouses, where both partners prioritize the needs of their spouse, care for each other, and honor God through their commitment.

Secondly, marriage is seen as a means of continuing the generations and fulfilling the commandment to multiply. After blessing Adam and Eve in Paradise, God instructed them to "multiply and fill the earth and subdue it..." (Genesis 1:28). This divine blessing signifies God's approval of marriage and the union of Adam and Eve. In the Orthodox tradition, God's presence is invoked during the marriage ceremony, just as He was present during the union of Adam and Eve in Paradise. This demonstrates the significance of a legal marriage, solemnized in the holy church where Christ's body and blood are offered.

Lastly, marriage serves as a safeguard against the temptations of adultery. As the Apostle Paul advised, "Because of the temptation to sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife and each woman her own husband" (1 Corinthians 7:2). By committing to a holy marriage, individuals avoid the perils of yielding to lustful desires outside the confines of a sacred bond. It is essential for those living a religious life to steer clear of adultery, and marriage provides a path to resist such temptations.

Thus, the primary goal of marriage is to walk together in righteousness, pursuing eternal life and inheriting the Kingdom of Heaven. Married life is understood as a spiritual journey, necessitating the initiation of the marriage covenant within the Christian framework of the Church. This sacramental aspect signifies the involvement of three parties: the couple and God. Without all three, a marriage cannot be considered complete. In the sacrament of marriage, the physical union of the couple mirrors the unity of Christ's body and the Church. As stated in the Holy Scriptures, "They will become one flesh" (Mark 10:8), the great mystery of physical and spiritual unity finds its fulfillment in the Holy Eucharist.

The reason for elevating marriage to the status of a sacrament within the Church lies in allowing the Lord Jesus Christ to be the head and center of the couple's spiritual journey. In the words of St. Paul, "This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the Church" (Ephesians 5:32). The sacramental aspect signifies the union between the divine and the physical, and it is through the visible service and the reception of invisible grace that this union is made possible. The Holy Communion, in particular, transforms the marriage into a new reality, where the couple becomes one flesh.

(Continues) 👇

👉Question: Does marital status determine whether to receive Holy Communion? For example, if we are single, married, what if our partner is not willing? Or what should I do if my fiance refuses to marry me in the sacrament?

✍Answer

text:
: One of the sacrements of the New Testament is Christ's holy flesh and His precious blood. We have said that the special gift of the Holy Spirit that we have been blessed with since the birth of a boy on the 40th day and the birth of a girl on the 80th day is the food of eternal life. To separate from this is to die although we seem alive simply because we breath. Our body: If we lose  food for a few days or even for few hours for some people, it is definitely not possible to stay alive. This is one of the common weaknesses of the body where we lose our fleshly existence. Likewise, if the soul loses Christ's holy flesh and precious blood, it dies and has no life. It means that we have killed it. Therefore, in order to eat this eternal life, to drink that gives eternal life, we should learn what kind of system and what kind of spiritual preparation we should follow. We are commanded by God to live a Christian life, of which the Holy Eucharist is the foundation. Any teaching that keeps us away by threatening and exaggerating for other reasons is false teaching and should be avoided. 

Apostle St. Paul said that if we eat and drink the ultimate food of the soul without preparation and understanding, it will be a debt to us. This means that it is necessary to always have a life prepared for repentance and to accept those who are counselors in the affairs of our souls, the fathers of the church whom God has appointed as our servants and shepherds. In other words, we are commanded to always receive with repentance, so that we do not make this mistake that St. Paul wrote about (so that we do not receive without deserving or understanding this), but there is no occasion where we are commanded to depart from this mystery, not even for a single day.

Therefore, for those who are said to be before marriage, as we mentioned above, we should realize that we should continue to accept what we received in our childhood, that started from the time of Christianity,  until the end of our lives. But we should do this without committing any shame or sin as that is the only thing which keeps us away from the Holy Communion. Everyone knows what sin or shame is that keeps us away from the Holy Communion, even a child knows. There is no one who does not know the type of sin from the smallest to the highest level of sin. Murder, adultery, adultery, all these seeming sins can keep you away from the sacrament. But through repentant and reprimanded, you can continue the communion by repenting and being mentored and taught by their penitent father. 

Back to the question, it is to say that we should do this throughout our life, and it is not a matter of martial status. Both the male and female start participating in this sacrement at the time of their baptism and actively participate alone until they reach maturity age. After that, the man chooses someone who resembles him in his spiritual life and the woman chooses someone who resembles her in her spiritual life and they get married and continue with the Holy Communion together. Even those who are not married in the Holy Communion, without having this opportunity, come to repentance and they, too, can continue their holy purpose that they have abandoned. Because the Church has made a system for us, it has reconciliation for all from her creator.

To be continued 👇

text.text: 👉🏾👉🏾👉🏾 About the Holy Family's entrance into Egypt

text: In this lesson, we will explore the remarkable journey of the Holy Family's entrance into Egypt, a period marked by persecution, suffering, and divine intervention. The experiences of the Virgin Mary, Joseph, and their son Jesus provide valuable lessons of faith, resilience, and the unwavering love of God. Through their trials, they demonstrate the power of trust and the triumph of good over evil. Their story serves as an inspiration for us to persevere in the face of adversity and trust in God's providence.

text.text: 1. The Persecution of the Holy Family:

text: The Holy Family, including the Virgin Mary, Joseph, and the young Jesus, faced persecution from the moment of their entry into this world. Our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, came to restore humanity to its former glory and reconcile it with God. Yet, from infancy, Jesus and his family encountered hardships and suffering. The Virgin Mary, filled with love and devotion, endured hunger, thirst, and sorrow for the sake of her beloved son. She willingly embraced the challenges, knowing that they were part of God's plan for their eternal safety.

text.text: 2. The Faithful Devotion of the Virgin Mary:

text: As we examine the history of the Holy Family, we discover the profound faith and devotion of the Virgin Mary. Even at a young age, she dedicated herself to serving in the house of God, choosing a life of piety and prayer. When she conceived Jesus through the Holy Spirit's intervention, she faced confusion and doubt from her husband Joseph. However, she never wavered in her trust in God's plan. Her unwavering faith and purity of heart were evident when she declared, "God knows that I am pure; it is God who has done this."

Throughout their journey, the Holy Family encountered numerous trials and dangers. From the flight to Egypt to escape Herod's wrath to the challenges faced in different lands, they relied on God's guidance and protection. Angels appeared in dreams, warning Joseph and providing guidance. The earth opened up to swallow idols in Egypt, demonstrating God's power. Divine intervention rescued Joseph from brutal beatings, and the Virgin Mary performed miracles to protect herself and her family.

The Holy Family's journey teaches us valuable lessons about perseverance and trust in God's plan. Despite the hardships they faced, they never lost hope or doubted God's presence in their lives. Their unwavering faith enabled them to endure persecution and overcome challenges. We learn from them the importance of relying on God during difficult times and trusting that He will provide the strength and guidance needed to navigate the trials of life.

Above all, the story of the Holy Family highlights the transformative power of love. The Virgin Mary's love for her son and her unwavering commitment to God's plan demonstrate the selflessness and sacrificial nature of true love. Through her example, we are reminded of the immense love God has for each one of us and how we, too, can express that love through our actions and devotion.

The story of the Holy Family's entrance to Egypt serves as a testament to the power of faith, resilience, and divine protection. The Virgin Mary, Joseph, and Jesus faced immense challenges but remained steadfast in their trust in God. Their journey teaches us to persevere in the face of adversity, to have faith in God's plan, and to embody the transformative power of love. By following their example, we can find solace, strength, and hope in our own lives, knowing that God is always with us, guiding and protecting us through the darkest of times.

Today, we will learn about the significance of the Feast of the Paraclete, a day of great rejoicing and blessing in our Orthodox faith. The term "Paraclete" carries deep meaning, representing the spirit, righteousness, spiritual life, natural breath, physical life, and physical breath. It is within this feast that we celebrate the third person of the Holy Trinity, the Holy Spirit of God, who is worshipped alongside the Father and the Son.

In the Gospel of John, chapter 15, verse 26, our Lord Jesus Christ assures us, saying, "But when the Helper comes, whom I shall send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, He will testify of Me." This divine promise was fulfilled when, on the tenth day after Christ's glorious resurrection, the Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles. This day, known as Pentecost, holds great significance in the life of our Church. The term "Pentecost" is derived from the Greek word "pentēkostē," meaning fiftieth, for it occurs fifty days after our Lord's resurrection.

On this extraordinary day, the apostles were gathered together in the house of Mark's mother, Mary. Suddenly, at the third hour, a mighty sound, like that of a rushing wind, emanated from heaven and filled the entire house. The descent of the Holy Spirit was imminent, and the world was about to witness the power of God's grace and the birth of the Church.

Beloved, it is important to recognize that before the ascension of our Lord, He commanded His disciples to wait for the Holy Spirit. For it is by the Holy Spirit's indwelling that heavenly wealth and knowledge are transformed into spiritual treasures. Acts 2:3 tells us, "Then there appeared to them divided tongues, as of fire, and one sat upon each of them." This divine manifestation signified the filling of the apostles with the Holy Spirit. Through this divine encounter, what they already knew was confirmed, and what they did not know was revealed. Furthermore, the Holy Spirit granted them the miraculous ability to speak in seventy-one languages, in addition to the Hebrew language they already spoke.

Witnessing this marvelous spectacle, some skeptics mocked the apostles, accusing them of being drunk on new wine. However, Saint Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, stood before the gathering and addressed their doubts. He proclaimed, "These are not drunk, as you suppose, since it is only the third hour of the day. But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel: 'And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, that I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your young men shall see visions, your old men shall dream dreams'" (Acts 2:15-17).

In response to the people's inquiry about what they should do, Saint Peter instructed them to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Through their obedience, three thousand souls received the Word and were baptized that day, becoming partakers of the divine grace poured out by the Holy Spirit.

Notably, among those who were present were individuals from Ethiopia who, upon hearing Saint Peter's sermon, believed in the Lord Jesus Christ and were baptized. Thus, this day is referred to as the Church's Nativity, a momentous occasion commemorated as one of the nine principal festivals of our Lord Jesus Christ. Moreover, it is fittingly called "the lady of all festivals," for on this day, the Holy Spirit blessed the apostles with seventy-one languages, enabling them to carry the Gospel to the ends of the earth.

(Continues)👇🏾

Question፦ Hello Father, I had a question. It is about the verse of the bible that says "love your enemy". How can we love people who are trying to destroy us? 

Answer፦

text:
Indeed, the question you pose is of great significance, dear member. "Love your enemy," a principle taught by Christ, is often difficult to comprehend, especially when our enemies appear to bring us harm or destruction. The tenet seemingly contradicts our natural instincts of self-preservation and justice. As followers of the Orthodox faith, how then do we interpret this seemingly paradoxical instruction?

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 5, verse 44 tells us, "But I say to you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who spitefully use you and persecute you." But who exactly are these enemies that we are called to love? Surely, it is not a call to love those who aim to obliterate our faith, subvert our rights, and bring calamity upon us.

In our Orthodox belief, our true enemy is not of flesh and blood, but the devil himself. The enemy that Christ instructs us to love is not one who seeks to eradicate our faith, usurp our lands, or eradicate our presence on earth. No, it is not a call for passive submission to destructive forces.

Instead, the enemies referred to here are those among our own brothers and sisters in faith with whom we might have disputes or disagreements, those who have perhaps hurt us or wronged us in personal or communal contexts. It is these individuals, who are nevertheless our brethren in faith, that we are instructed to love and forgive.

But when it comes to those who threaten our existence, our faith, and our lands, the Bible offers other wisdom. In these cases, we are called upon to stand firm, to defend our faith and our people. The Biblical figures such as the Prophet David, who defeated Goliath, and the Prophet Moses, who stood against the Pharaoh's tyranny, exemplify this righteous resistance. Question: Hello fathers, how can I get out of addiction? 

Answer፦

text:
Truly, addiction is one of the most grievous trials of our age. It has touched our society, our church, and even our very families, testing the strength of our faith and causing profound suffering. Addiction is not merely a mundane issue but a spiritual struggle against forces that seek to diminish our inherent dignity and to tarnish the image of God within us.

Many forms of addiction exist, from substances like tobacco and drugs, to behavioural issues such as gluttony, promiscuity, and deceit. Regardless of its form, addiction invariably results in a loss of self-control and a corruption of the soul, as one is led away from virtuous conduct and into behaviours that do not befit a child of God.

Recognize, dear member, that addiction is not just a struggle against mere flesh and blood, but against the spiritual forces of darkness. As our Lord taught, it is the devil who comes to steal, kill and destroy, and addiction is one of the weapons he uses in his relentless war against the human soul.

The holy fathers of the church, drawing from the wellspring of apostolic wisdom and the holy scriptures, have instructed us on how to handle such trials. We do not fight addiction with the weapons of this world, but with the spiritual armour of God. It is by fortifying our souls with faith, prayer, fasting, repentance, and the sacraments that we stand firm against this onslaught.

Yet, in the face of addiction, many people despair, believing that once ensnared in the grip of addiction, escape is impossible. This is a lie from the evil one himself. Do not forget the words of the apostle Paul, "No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it."

The journey to recovery from addiction begins with an honest admission of one's struggles and a fervent desire for transformation. It requires the courage to confront one's sins and weaknesses and the humility to seek help. Remember, the journey might be tough, but with God, all things are possible.

Seek spiritual counsel from the fathers of the church or a trusted spiritual advisor who can guide you through this process. Their wisdom, coupled with the grace of God, can set you on the path to recovery. Remain steadfast in prayer, for prayer is the bridge that connects us to God and the armour that shields us from the assaults of the evil one.

Consider seeking help through confession and spiritual counseling, as these practices can provide an avenue for healing. In the sacrament of confession, we confront our sins and express our desire for repentance, and in doing so, we receive the Lord's forgiveness and mercy.

In this struggle, you are not alone. The church is your family and your support, providing you with the necessary spiritual resources and the fellowship of the faithful. We encourage you to turn to your fellow believers for support and to include them in your journey towards healing.

Rest assured, dear member, that there is hope. Addiction is not an unbeatable foe. With the help of God and the support of the Church, you can overcome this affliction. Through the intercessions of the Mother of God and all the saints, may you find strength, courage, and the determination to break free from the chains of addiction.

In closing, we lift you up in prayer, entrusting you to the mercy and grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, through His death and resurrection, has triumphed over sin and death. May His love be your strength and His peace your comfort, today and always. Amen.

text.text: Are we justified by keeping the law or by faith alone? Righteousness, faith, conduct
Beloved and esteemed brethren, who follow the orthodox teachings that we impart on the John's Repentance website, we humbly present to you an important lesson on the topic of Law, Faith, and Conduct.

text:
As followers of Christ, we are called to live a life that is both righteous and pleasing in the eyes of our Lord. The question often arises, are we justified by keeping the law or by faith alone? We must remember that the foundation of righteousness is indeed faith, but faith without conduct is futile. As it is written in the Holy Scriptures, "Faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead" (James 2:17).

The law is an integral part of our lives, for it brings justice and condemnation to those who transgress it. If we are obedient and keep the law, we shall be justified, but if we refuse and rebel, we shall be devoured by the sword. The prophet Isaiah confirms this truth when he proclaims,

text.text: "If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it" (Isa. 1:19-20).

text: Furthermore, we must not forget that our conscience, which is the spiritual law within us, guides us towards righteousness. It is through our conscience that we do good deeds and follow the moral laws that are ingrained in us. This serves as a reminder that there is one supreme God who rewards both the righteous and the wicked according to their deeds and judges impartially. As Saint Paul writes,

text.text: "For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves" (Romans 2:14-14).
In the Orthodox Tewahedo doctrine, conduct is given the highest priority after religion.

text:
Conduct is inseparable from faith. As Saint Jacob reminds us, "What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? Can faith save him?" (James 2:14). We are called to feed the hungry, sympathize with the bereaved, receive guests, give to one another, visit the sick, preach the gospel to the prisoners, and live in love. These are the hallmarks of Christian ethics, as exemplified in Matthew 25:15-30.

As followers of Christ, we are called to be the salt of the earth, and to stay away from the temptations of fleshly and worldly desires. We must turn away from revenge, malice, deceit, materialism, impurity, adultery, idol worship, and the burden of sin, and return to a good nature. As it is written,

text.text: "Blessed are you when others revile you and persecute you and utter all kinds of evil against you falsely on my account" (Matthew 5:11). Let us take up our crosses and follow Christ, for in Him, we shall find rest for our souls (Matthew 11:29).

text:
Morality is the practical manifestation of our faith. If faith alone were sufficient, then even the demons, who are creatures of God, would have believed and testified that Christ is the Son of God.

As it is written in the Holy Gospel, "When the evil spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, saying, 'You are the Son of God.'" (Mark 3:11) "And when he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him, shouting with a loud voice and saying, "Jesus, son of the Most High God, what have I to do with you? I swear by God that you will not torture me. "Come out of this man, you unclean spirit" (Mark 5:5-8).

In his message, the apostle Saint James said, "And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God." (Jas 2:19)

(Continues) 👇🏾

text.text:
Order

Question፦ On 1 Tim 3:2 it says :"A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behavior, given to hospitality, apt to teach" who are metropolitan bishops in Orthodox Church? Can they get married or can a bishop be a married person?

Answer፦

text:
The nature of the ecclesiastical order as outlined in the Pauline epistle to Timothy gives us insight into the role of bishops within the Orthodox Church. The bishops, serving as successors to the apostles, are regarded as the principal teachers, administrators, and ceremonial leaders of the Church. In Orthodox tradition, bishops have always been seen as leading lives of celibacy, dedicating their lives entirely to the service of the Church and the will of God. This is manifested in their choice to live as monks, separated from worldly affairs from a young age.

From a historical perspective, we see that the apostles themselves had different backgrounds, including marital status and occupations. The focus, however, has always been on their role as disseminators of God's teachings. Similarly, the roles within the Church, be it bishops, priests, or deacons, have expanded and adapted with the growth of the Church, a point that is well illustrated in the example of the appointment of the first seven deacons, led by St. Stephen.

Now, it's important to understand that the evolution of roles within the Church does not imply a shift away from the principles established by St. Paul. Rather, it signifies the Church's efforts to faithfully fulfill its spiritual obligations as its reach expands. Hence, it is indeed the monks who have embraced a life of celibacy and full devotion to God that take up the mantle of the bishopric. This is consistent with the canons of the Orthodox Church.

While the Orthodox Church encourages celibacy for bishops, it also acknowledges the apostolic guidance for bishops to be 'the husband of one wife.' This underlines the significance of monogamy, but it should not be misconstrued as an injunction for bishops to be married. In the practical and historical context of the Church, the role of the bishop has been fulfilled by those who have embraced a monastic life of celibacy.

Yet, it's important to mention that the authenticity of the ecclesiastical office cannot be guaranteed by monastic life alone. It also requires a deep and genuine spiritual life and knowledge, the absence of which has unfortunately led to errors and aberrations. The Church, in its wisdom, acknowledges that all humans, including its leaders, are prone to mistakes and temptations, as seen in the account of Simon the Magician in the book of Acts. It is essential, then, to avoid appointing those lacking in spiritual knowledge and life to leadership positions in the Church.

And so our dear member, we find that the Church continues to adapt to the needs of its faithful while remaining anchored to its apostolic foundations. It understands the challenges of living a life of peace and equality but insists on this aspiration, urging its flock to transcend the earthly trials and tribulations in pursuit of God's will. Let us, therefore, remember to bear our responsibilities faithfully, both within the Church and in the wider world, and to uphold the principles of peace, equality, and righteousness as taught by the apostles and preserved by the saints. Amen.

1. To those who faithfully partake of Holy Communion

text:
"Whoever endures to the end will be saved" Matthew 24:13

The essence of the Christian life resides not only in professing faith but in preserving it until our last breath. This was the counsel of our Lord to His disciples, whom He ordained and sent forth to proclaim the Gospel. He did not promise them a path strewn with roses, but a journey filled with trials, strewn with fiery tests and bearing the sharp edge of persecution.

It is of utmost importance to keep in mind that your victor, the Lord who has overcome the world, is by your side. Despite manifold hardships, remember to remain steadfast in your faith and love of God, and never to let your spiritual crown tumble.

Learn to treat the mundane affairs of this world with equanimity, cherishing the knowledge that all things on earth are but fleeting. With perseverance, transform every aspect of your life, be it commerce, agriculture, learning, marrying, rearing children, into an act of dedication to God. Remember that you do not bear the weight of your life alone; your God is by your side, transforming all your deeds into blessings. 

Heed the wisdom imparted in the scriptures to combat the devil's ploys. Do not disregard the tribulations you face, for these trials temper your faith. After savouring the grace of God, pray fervently that any worldly enticements that could wrench you from God's glory be quashed beneath your feet.

text.text: 2. To those desiring to faithfully partake of Holy Communion

text: "Now is the day of salvation"

Corinthians 6:2/

The Apostle's exhortation that today is the day of our salvation should spur our determination to prepare for Holy Communion. 

The desire to partake in Holy Communion must be birthed from the Holy Spirit. It requires self-examination and contemplation: Why do I desire Communion? How deeply do I comprehend its significance? What are my expectations for life post-Communion? 

Saint Peter proclaimed, "Lord, to whom shall we go?" (John 6:68), emphasizing the enduring, life-giving truth that Christ alone has the words of eternal life. However, many stumbled at Christ's claim, "My flesh is real food, and my blood is real drink." Such people could not fathom how one could consume Christ's flesh and blood, and thus, they fell away. To prevent a similar downfall, ensure that your motivation for Communion stems not from anything else than the depth of your faith and from guidance provided by your spiritual leader.

As you approach Holy Communion, beware of the whispers of Satan, who seeks to fill your heart with doubts and fears.

text.text: 3. To those distant from Holy Communion

text: "If they still refuse to listen, tell it to the church"

18:17/

No Christian who truly grasps the significance of Holy Communion would shun it. Are you hesitant to receive Communion due to personal conflicts or issues? Address these problems openly within the church, as instructed by the Gospel. 

Those who believe they can traverse this world unscathed by troubles are victims of a devilish delusion. Indeed, as followers of Christ, we should expect the world's disdain and hostility, for our Lord warned, "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first" (John 15:18).

Consequently, if we avoid approaching God due to our problems, our error is grave. For no matter the chaos in our lives, we should never consider ourselves unworthy to draw near to God. 

Every Christian has the capacity to dedicate their life to the worship and glorification of God, just as they have the potential to prepare for eternal glory through Holy Communion.

text: In the depths of humanity's fallen state, when death entered the world, it did so through three grievous crimes: impatience, pride, and greed. Yet, through the grace of Christ, death was conquered by three great virtues, which we shall explore in depth. Drawing from the wisdom of the Orthodox tradition, we shall delve into the significance of patience, humility, and contentment, and their transformative power in the life of a believer.

Impatience, born from a restless spirit, is a formidable obstacle in the path of righteousness. As we reflect upon the events in the Garden of Eden, we witness the devastating consequences of haste. The serpent, the preacher of sin, whispered to Eve, stirring unease within her heart. Restlessness clouded her judgment, and she failed to investigate the serpent's deceitful words. Subsequently, Adam, who should have stood firm, was also swayed by impatience, leading both of them towards a tragic downfall.

Impatience continues to afflict humanity, as we often succumb to the allure of sin without considering the consequences. Yet, Christ, the second Adam, demonstrated the power of patience. He endured the mocking and scourging silently, willingly accepting the weight of our sins. By His patience, He astonished onlookers and conquered death itself. In imitating Christ's patience, we find the strength to endure, for salvation belongs to those who persevere till the end.

Pride, the first sin, is a perilous temptation that ensnares even the noblest of creatures. It is the root of disobedience and rebellion against God's established order. In the Garden of Eden, this sin manifested itself when Adam and Eve disregarded the fear of God and broke His commandment. The devil himself, consumed by pride, had no opportunity for repentance, succumbing to eternal damnation.

To counteract this destructive pride, we must embrace humility and obedience. Our Lord Jesus Christ, the epitome of humility, willingly submitted Himself to the cross, even unto death, to redeem us from the consequences of our disobedience. He obediently accepted the weight of our sins, showcasing that obedience is the path to true life. Just as a child obeys their parent, even to the point of sacrifice, Christ demonstrated obedience to remove the death sentence imposed upon us by our disobedience. In imitating Christ's obedience, we restore the image of God within us and find our way back to eternal communion with Him.

- Overcoming Greed and Embracing Generosity
Greed, the insidious desire for more, separates us from the company of God and His heavenly angels. It distorts our perception, causing us to covet what is forbidden or unnecessary. In the Garden, Adam and Eve beheld the tree and its fruit, considering it beautiful and desirable only after the serpent planted the seed of greed within them.

Greed leads us down a treacherous path, where the devil entices us with false promises and desires. When we fail to find contentment in the grace bestowed upon us, death lurks nearby, ready to claim our lives. Yet, our Lord Jesus Christ, the Second Adam, offers a powerful antidote. He, who did not even desire His own life, willingly sacrificed Himself for others. Even in death, He gave generously, making amends for the wrongs committed by greed. Our first father rushed to acquire what he lacked, driven by covetousness, while our second father willingly gave

 His own wealth, even His flesh and blood, for our salvation. Through Christ, we learn to replace greed with generosity, finding fulfillment in selflessness and gratitude.

text.text: Beloved members of John's Repentance service, today (Technically yesterday) is the monthly feast the Holy Trinity. Hence we send you this writing so you may read and partake form the Trinity's blessings.

text:
The Holy Trinity - a profound mystery, one that confounds the human mind and yet, stands as a beacon of divine revelation. The Trinity, the triune God, is a singular essence manifested in three persons - the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This, however, should not be confined within the human concept of numbers. The unity is not merely numerical, but a unity of divine essence, an unity of character. The three, then, surpasses the boundaries of numerics to suggest a unique trinity, a unique interconnectedness and interdependence.

God is beyond the comprehension of human mind, beyond the law of numbers. Thus, it is imperative that God Himself reveals the mystery of the Holy Trinity to His creation. The grand revelation - the incarnation of God - stands as a testament to this mystery. It is through the Son of God, Christ, becoming flesh that the eternal Fatherhood and Sonship become recognizable. It is during the baptism of Christ by John the Baptist that the world comes to acknowledge Christ as the eternal Son of God the Father.

The teachings of Christ post His baptism unraveled the divine nature of God the Father. These teachings, in combination with the moral life led by Christ, exhibited the coequality of the Holy Spirit with the Father and the Son. This divine revelation, in the body of Christ, was then passed on to the church, His body on earth. Christ informed us about God the Father, and the church, in her liturgical prayers, affirms this revelation.

The Holy Spirit, a purifying and glorifying life, is the life of the Father and the Son. He is the God who lives within the Father and the Son. During the baptism of Christ, He descended in the form of a dove, teaching us to be baptized in the Holy Spirit as per the Gospel of Matthew (28:19).

The apostle St. John begins his Gospel by affirming the eternal existence of the Word, indicating its unity with the Father and the Holy Spirit - the divine Trinity. He asserts that the Word was first, suggesting the preeminence of the Word, thereby allowing the fathers of the church to interpret the Old Testament through the lens of the New Testament. As such, the Old Testament is understood as foretelling the New Testament - the incarnation of the Son, who revealed to us His Father, and the Trinity.

When Christ queried His disciples about His identity, Saint Peter responded, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." (Matthew 16:16). Christ then affirms that this knowledge comes from His Father, and blessed Peter for his testimony. This affirmation from Peter not only confirmed the identity of Christ, but also subtly illuminated the mystery of the Holy Trinity. Peter's words imply that Christ is the living Son of God, sustained by the life of the Holy Spirit - thereby acknowledging the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

The essence of this revelation goes further to highlight the mystery of the Incarnation. Christ, who came in the flesh, was the awaited Messiah as prophesied by the prophets. Thus, St. Peter, through divine revelation, testified to the mystery of the Trinity and the Incarnation in one breath.

This revelation of the unity and trinity of God is evident in His creation and His salvation of the world. The Old Testament foretells God's plan for the salvation of the world, and the Gospel of John reveals the Trinity's involvement in the creation and salvation of the world. It is the same Trinity, who created the world from non-existence, that also saves the world with their unified power when it falls due to wrongdoing. Thus, we come to understand the divine interaction between the Creator and the creation as revealed in the Scriptures. The Trinity's nature, revealed

 in the eternal life, is also manifest in the salvation of this world.
